title: Refactor AgenC-injected CLAUDE.md — offload everything offloadable into skills
description:
The AgenC-injected portion of CLAUDE.md (the 'AgenC Agent Operating Instructions' block at the top of every mission's CLAUDE.md) has grown large and consumes context every turn. Many sections describe rarely-used surfaces or one-off concepts that don't need to be always-on — they belong as skills with their own trigger conditions, leaving CLAUDE.md as a thin index that points at them.

Goal: shrink the always-on context budget. Audit every section of the injected block, decide what's truly always-on (Tier 0 rules, daily-used routing) vs what can be offloaded (cross-repo mission spawn recipes, monitoring patterns, send-keys, detach, reload — these can be skills with their own activation triggers). Apply progressive disclosure per /cc-global-instructions-management.

Provenance: AgenC mission ef10a83f-28f2-4008-b95d-e553f9f93cd9 (today's inbox processing).

title: PHASE 0 (GATE): Stabilize the orchestrator foundation before autonomy ships
description: Hard precondition gate for epic agenc-g7nk. With humans out of the real-time loop, autonomy risks shipping orchestrator bugs that go uncaught. Session transcripts ARE fully inspectable via `agenc session print` — earlier framing of 'ephemeral data loss / missions are throwaway' was wrong on this point — but hand-reviewing every transcript at scale is impractical. Planned mitigation: encode a high-fidelity model of Kevin into Claude and have Claude run broad sweeping reflections (e.g. daily) across all recent missions, surfacing anomalies for human review. Until that reflection loop is built, do not build autonomy on a cracked foundation. Scope is NARROW — only the dependency chain and the lifecycle/loop code autonomy actually touches, NOT all 196 open beads. Binds: the config-cache→DB-context→store-interface chain (agenc-347, agenc-337, agenc-350), git-op timeouts so hung loops are detectable (agenc-336), a loop health-RECOVERY policy (crashed background loops currently are marked degraded but never restarted), wrapper.go decomposition (agenc-342), the master tech-debt epic (agenc-351), and a raised test floor on mission lifecycle + background loops (currently ~5%). Plus a checkpoint audit. GATE: this phase must close before Phase 2 autonomy is enabled in production. AgenC mission e68829d7-fade-49b7-bc60-a3b82f1c492d. Framing correction provenance: weekly planning AgenC mission b8827a39, 2026-06-07.
notes:
2026-09-06: this gate's BINDS list needs a decision from Kevin. An audit of the five remaining agenc-351 beads (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61) recommends CLOSE on all five, including agenc-337 and agenc-350, which this gate binds as part of the 'config-cache -> DB-context -> store-interface chain'. Full evidence is in each bead's notes. Surfacing rather than unbinding: the gate is Kevin's to re-scope.

The conflict, stated plainly:
- agenc-337's only justification is cancelling long-running queries. Measured on the real 60MB production DB, the heaviest query the code can issue takes 200ms, contention is capped at 5s by busy_timeout and returns SQLITE_BUSY rather than hanging, and all 11 background loops already take ctx and select on ctx.Done() at their tick boundary. Against this gate's own cut - 'does this failure class corrupt unattended work silently?' - it scores NO: the failure is loud, bounded, logged, and retried next tick.
- agenc-350 has zero consumers. *database.DB appears in one production location (server.go:29); tests use real SQLite in t.TempDir() and pass. The repo's two existing test-double interfaces (launchdManager, GitCommander) are narrow and declared at the consumer, which is the opposite of the broad producer-side interface this bead specifies.
- agenc-342 was already cut from this gate by the 2026-07-05 note; the code independently corroborates it (two of its four extraction targets were deleted by other work, and its 0%-covered targets mean agenc-333 gave it no safety net).

One correction to how this gate has been summarized elsewhere: the 2026-07-05 note names the yes-set as the config cache (agenc-347, since closed), never-restarted background loops, and undetectable git hangs (agenc-336, since closed), and names wrapper.go decomposition as NO. It does not classify 337 or 350 either way. Any claim that the note calls 337/350 'the silent-failure cut' is an inference from the BINDS list, not something the note says.

If Kevin accepts the recommendations, the note's own suggestion applies - 're-scoping the gate to the silent-failure subset so it closes sooner' - and what remains binding is the loop health-RECOVERY policy (crashed background loops are marked degraded but never restarted) plus the raised test floor on mission lifecycle and background loops. Both agenc-347 and agenc-336 are already closed.

Related finding worth weighing here because it IS the silent-failure class this gate exists for, and it is not covered by any bead in the chain: a likely data race at internal/wrapper/wrapper.go:214, which writes w.hasConversation without holding stateMu after line 208 has started the HTTP server goroutine that reads that field under RLock at socket.go:105-110. setupRun has 0.0% coverage, so the race detector in make check never exercises the path. Strongly indicated by inspection, not confirmed by a race-detector run.

title: EPIC: AgenC → autonomous high-quality Claude orchestrator (research + plan)
description: Long-range transformative initiative: evolve AgenC from a human-in-the-loop orchestrator into the 'command center' for FULLY AUTONOMOUS, HIGH-QUALITY Claude Code execution. Driven by Kevin (2026-05-28). Scope spans: (1) autonomy primitives (beyond headless/cron/spawn); (2) harness-level QUALITY loop — review/verification/feedback/retry, since today quality is config-only with no harness enforcement; (3) feedback + work + reference-information storage; (4) AgenC's own code-quality/maintainability and UX-consistency, since a buggy or entropy-filled orchestrator fails its purpose. Approach: Double Diamond (Discover/Define/Develop/Deliver). Deliverable: an intelligent plan/report. Provenance: AgenC mission e68829d7-fade-49b7-bc60-a3b82f1c492d.
notes:

notes:
2026-09-06 audit (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61), triggered by Kevin's challenge that the tech-debt epic predates a much-changed codebase. RECOMMEND CLOSE.

Two of the ticket's four extraction targets were already deleted by other work, not extracted:
- The state machine is GONE. WrapperState/wrapperState, stateRunning/stateRestartPending/stateRestarting and getWrapperStateString were deleted by commit bff7f87 (2026-05-05, 'Remove unused wrapper /restart endpoint and restart state machine'), which removed 161 lines from wrapper.go. grep -rn 'WrapperState' --include=*.go returns nothing. The proposed state.go would contain zero lines.
- Commented-out Keychain code is GONE, removed by commit 7016008 on 2026-02-14, one day AFTER this epic was authored. No occurrence of 'Keychain' remains in internal/wrapper/.
Still present: writeHeartbeat (wrapper.go:545, 25 lines) and watchWorkspaceRemoteRefs (wrapper.go:473, 54 lines).

The ticket's own arithmetic no longer works: extracting everything it names removes ~118 lines from a 788-line file, landing near 670 against its stated target of <300.

The dependency it waited on gives no safety for this work. agenc-333 closed, but per-function coverage shows writeHeartbeat and watchWorkspaceRemoteRefs both sit at 0.0%. The integration suite pins the socket/JSON protocol and the idle/attention hook transitions (handleClaudeUpdate 100%, NewWrapper 90%) - i.e. exactly the parts the ticket leaves alone - and pins nothing it wants to move. The restart tests the spec asked for were written and then deleted with the feature in bff7f87.

No configured quality gate is breached: .golangci.yml sets gocyclo min-complexity 20 and make check passes; there is no funlen/lll/maintidx linter, so 788 lines violates nothing the project enforces.

This corroborates Kevin's 2026-07-05 cut on agenc-9jgp (wrapper decomposition = maintainability, not a silent-failure class) on independent evidence.

Flip condition: a defect traceable to the file's STRUCTURE rather than its length (a merge conflict between concurrent missions in wrapper.go, or adoption of a file/function-length linter that 788 lines would fail).

Separately discovered while auditing, NOT part of this bead - filed as follow-ups rather than fixed here: (1) wrapper.go:71 comment names a 'state' field that was deleted and omits lastUserPromptAt, which stateMu genuinely does protect; (2) wrapper.go:308-309 still describes a three-state machine that no longer exists; (3) LIKELY DATA RACE - wrapper.go:214 writes w.hasConversation without holding stateMu, after line 208 starts the HTTP server goroutine whose handler reads that field under RLock at socket.go:105-110. setupRun has 0.0% coverage so the race detector never exercises this path. Strongly indicated, not confirmed by a race-detector run.

Audited against the current codebase by an independent agent during mission 7e071462, which found the condition this bead describes no longer holds; the file-and-line evidence is recorded in this bead notes. Kevin had challenged the whole epic as predating too much change to still be real, and all five remaining beads came back recommending CLOSE.

title: Make red tests structurally uncommittable in the agenc repo
description:
Kevin's intent: every agent working in the agenc repo should be structurally unable to land a commit against a failing test suite. Fixing the tests is not the same as making broken tests uncommittable.

Empirical findings from mission 424684c5:
- .githooks/pre-commit ALREADY runs 'make check' (go test -race + lint + coverage). The guard exists and works WHEN ACTIVE. make check is green on main at 24.6s.
- 'check: genprime' is already on main, so the hook does NOT inherit the stale-prime_content bug that only affected the standalone 'make test' target (fixed on unmerged branch mieubrisse/agenc-hygiene-sweep, commit fb64bd8). cmd/genprime os.WriteFile's unconditionally, so check is self-healing against stale artifacts.
- REAL GAP 1: hook activation is accidental. core.hooksPath is set only by 'make setup', which reaches mission clones via a machine-local ~/.agenc/config/config.yml postUpdateHook plus the rsync -a copy in internal/mission/repo.go. None of that is tracked in the repo. A plain git clone by anyone has NO hook.
- REAL GAP 2: there is no CI at all. .github/workflows contains only release.yml (tags only). Nothing runs tests on push or PR, so --no-verify or an inert hook goes completely undetected.

Constraints: do not weaken existing hooks; must work in fresh clones without per-clone manual setup; do not restart the AgenC server or rebuild the installed binary.

Acceptance criteria: broken test blocks a local commit (proven by deliberately breaking one); passing state still commits cleanly; a bypassed commit (--no-verify) is caught by CI on push; the residual gap that only Kevin can close (branch protection) is named explicitly.

title: Fold the cron-health auditor into AgenC proper and retire the bridge binary
description:
WHY: the cron health auditor that now protects Kevin's seven crons is installed out-of-band — a launchd job 'agenc-doctor' pointing at a binary copy at ~/.agenc/bin/agenc-doctor, built from an unmerged branch. It works and is verified, but it is a bridge, not a home. Nothing in AgenC knows the job exists, so nothing recreates it if it is lost, and the binary will drift from the codebase as agenc evolves.

The auditor must stay OUTSIDE AgenC's own cron system — a cron that audits crons shares a failure mode with the thing it audits, which is precisely why the 2026-09-01 outage went unnoticed for five days. Whoever picks this up should decide where the scheduling belongs (a server-managed launchd job alongside the cron syncer? a server background loop, at the cost of only taking effect on restart?) weighing that independence against tidiness. Do not simply convert it into an entry in config.yml's crons map.

CONSTRAINTS: the auditor's plist must not use the 'agenc-cron' name prefix — AgenC's own syncer deletes plists matching that prefix with no config entry, and would remove its own watchdog. Removing the bridge means: launchctl bootout gui/$(id -u)/agenc-doctor, then deleting ~/Library/LaunchAgents/agenc-doctor.plist and ~/.agenc/bin/agenc-doctor.

ACCEPTANCE: the auditor runs on a schedule without depending on a hand-copied binary or a hand-installed plist, survives an agenc rebuild and a machine restart, and is still independent of the cron system it audits. Verified by removing the bridge, confirming the auditor still fires, and inducing a cron failure that it catches.

title: Unsynchronized write to hasConversation races the wrapper's HTTP status handler
description:
Found by inspection during the 2026-09-06 audit of the agenc-351 tech-debt epic (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61). Not confirmed by a race-detector run, so the first job is to prove or disprove it.

internal/wrapper/wrapper.go:214 writes w.hasConversation = true without holding stateMu. That line executes after line 208 has already started the HTTP server goroutine, whose status handler reads the same field under stateMu.RLock() at internal/server/../wrapper/socket.go:105-110. Every other access to hasConversation takes the mutex; this one does not.

Why it matters beyond tidiness: hasConversation feeds the status the wrapper reports, which is what AgenC uses to decide whether a mission is idle. A torn or stale read here misreports mission state, and it does so silently - nothing errors. That is the failure class the agenc-9jgp Phase 0 gate exists to catch, and no bead in that gate's dependency chain covers it.

Why the existing gates miss it: setupRun has 0.0% test coverage, so the race detector that runs in make check never exercises this path.

Acceptance criteria: either a test that reaches setupRun and demonstrates the race under -race (then a fix, presumably taking stateMu around the write), or a documented argument for why the write is safe - e.g. a happens-before relationship that makes the goroutine start ordering sufficient - recorded in a comment at the site so the next reader does not re-litigate it.

Two stale comments in the same file, cheap to fix alongside and worth doing because they actively mislead: wrapper.go:71 says stateMu protects a 'state' field that was deleted in commit bff7f87, and omits lastUserPromptAt, which the mutex genuinely does protect (written at :412 under Lock, read at :555 under RLock). wrapper.go:308-309 still describes a 'three-state machine: Running -> RestartPending -> Restarting -> Running' that no longer exists.
notes:
2026-09-06 follow-up, same mission. Upgraded from 'indicated by inspection' to CONFIRMED BY CONSTRUCTION. The race detector cannot see it, and that fact is itself part of the finding.

What was verified directly:
- wrapper.go:208 starts the HTTP server goroutine (go startHTTPServer(ctx, socketFilepath, w, w.logger)). wrapper.go:214 then writes w.hasConversation = true with no lock held. The ordering claim is confirmed: the write happens AFTER the reader goroutine is live.
- socket.go:103-110 handleStatus reads w.hasConversation under stateMu.RLock().
- Every OTHER production write is correctly synchronized: wrapper.go:396 and :410 are both inside handleClaudeUpdate, which takes stateMu.Lock() with defer Unlock at wrapper.go:390-391. Line 214 is the SOLE unsynchronized production access to this field.

So this is an unsynchronized write concurrent with a mutex-protected read - a data race by the Go memory model, not a maybe.

Why 'go test -race' does not catch it, and why a clean run is not evidence of safety: go test -race ./internal/wrapper/ PASSES, but go tool cover reports setupRun (wrapper.go:145, the function containing line 214) at 0.0% coverage. handleStatus is at 100% and startHTTPServer at 59.1%, so the reader side is exercised and the writer side never is. The detector only reports races it actually executes. This is the trap worth recording: the green -race run in make check reads as reassurance and means nothing here.

Reachability and blast radius, stated honestly rather than maximally:
- Line 214 is inside 'if isResume', so it fires only on mission resume/reload - common in AgenC, not rare.
- The exposure window is narrow: between the goroutine launch at :208 and the write at :214. A status request has to land inside it.
- Consequence when it does land there: handleStatus reports HasConversation=false for a mission that does have a resumable conversation. Nothing errors. That is the silent-misreport class.

Suggested fix, deliberately NOT applied here (core runtime, and this should be reviewed rather than landed at the end of an unattended run): the simplest correct change is to move the 'if isResume { w.hasConversation = true }' block ABOVE the goroutine launch at :208, which removes the concurrency entirely rather than adding a lock. Taking stateMu around the write also works but leaves a needless lock on a single-threaded setup path.

Whoever fixes it should still add coverage for setupRun, or the next race introduced on this path will be equally invisible.

title: mission detach fails when the mission pane lives outside the assumed tmux session
description:
Detaching a finished mission fails when its tmux pane is not in the session the pool lookup assumes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have a mission whose tmux pane lives in a session other than cockpit. On 2026-08-30 this was mission 87897981, whose pane %131 was alive in the deepwork session.
2. Run: agenc mission detach 87897981
3. Observe the failure:

     failed to unlink window: pane 131 not found in session cockpit
     at internal/server/pool.go:104 (unlinkPoolWindowByPane)

4. Confirm the pane is genuinely alive and resolvable: agenc tmux resolve-mission %131 correctly returns 87897981-6a95-4fda-b31b-cf863dfed4db.

Kevin runs several tmux sessions concurrently (cockpit, hyperspace, and deepwork were all live on this machine), so a pane lookup scoped to one session name will miss any mission whose pane lives elsewhere.

## Why This Matters

Detach is the terminal operation in Kevin workflow. He does not archive missions at all, so detach is the only way finished work leaves his active mission list. A detach that cannot complete means completed missions accumulate in the active view permanently, which erodes the signal value of the mission list.

## Goal

Make detach resolve a mission pane wherever that pane actually lives, instead of assuming a single session.

## Constraints

Do not introduce a new terminal operation or push users toward archive as a workaround; Kevin relies on detach specifically. Preserve current behavior for missions whose panes are in the expected session. Note that agenc tmux resolve-mission already maps a pane id to a mission uuid across sessions, so the needed capability may already exist elsewhere in the codebase.
acceptance_criteria: agenc mission detach succeeds for a mission whose pane is in a non-default tmux session (the mission 87897981 case completes cleanly rather than erroring); missions whose panes are in the expected session still detach as before; a regression test covers the multi-session lookup.
notes:
ESCALATED P3 -> P1 on 2026-08-30. This is not cosmetic: it is actively blocking mission-pool management.

New evidence gathered after filing. Attempted to detach two separate finished missions; both failed identically:

  agenc mission detach b680b0e4  ->  pane 132 not found in session cockpit
  agenc mission detach 87897981  ->  pane 131 not found in session cockpit

Panes %132 and %131 were live in the hyperspace and deepwork tmux sessions respectively. Every mission pane on this machine currently lives outside cockpit, so detach fails for ALL of them.

The downstream consequence: because nothing can be detached, the attached-mission count only ever climbs. Spawning a new mission then fails with:

  Attached mission limit reached (6) - detach a mission before attaching another

So the bug is self-compounding. It blocks the very operation (detach) that is the documented remedy for the cap it causes users to hit. Kevin is currently unable to spawn new missions at all without manual tmux intervention, which is what raises this above a hygiene issue.

Worth considering as part of the fix: whether the cap error message should point at this failure mode when detach itself is failing, rather than telling the user to do something that will not work.

---

FIX LANDED 2026-08-30 (mission 40beba93-47be-4755-b16c-5307c7ff762e, commit a31ae40). Open pending Kevin's install + real-machine verification.

## Where reality diverged from the filed repro

1. Step 4 of the repro does not establish what it claims. `agenc tmux resolve-mission` is a pure database lookup (pane column -> mission row, cmd/tmux_resolve_mission.go); it never queries tmux. A mission UUID coming back proves only that the DB still records that pane, not that the pane is alive anywhere.

2. Live tmux state when the fix was written: there is no `deepwork` session on the machine at all, and pane %131 exists in no session. Mission 87897981's `tmux_pane` column is now empty, so `agenc mission detach 87897981` no longer reaches the unlink code at all — before this fix it returned 400 "mission has no tmux pane".

3. Pane %132 (mission b680b0e4) is linked ONLY into `agenc-pool` — i.e. that mission is already detached. Its failure was a second, distinct variant: detach erroring on a mission that has nothing left to unlink.

4. The cross-session variant is real and is what drives the cap. Six missions are attached (panes 79, 113, 134, 135, 140, 142) — exactly the limit of 6 — and four of them (79, 113, 134, 140) live in `hyperspace` while the CLI is typically run from `cockpit`. Detaching any of those four from cockpit hit the reported error, so the documented remedy for the cap was genuinely unavailable.

## What changed

`internal/server/pool.go` gains `resolveUnlinkTargets(callerSession, linkedSessions)`: when the caller's own session holds the window it stays the sole unlink target (unchanged behavior, and it still avoids yanking a mission out of someone else's session); otherwise detach unlinks the window from every non-pool session it is linked into, since a mission counts as attached while its pane is linked anywhere outside the pool. The handler in `internal/server/missions.go` sources the session list from the existing `getLinkedPaneSessions` helper, and treats "nothing to unlink" — no pane recorded, or pane linked only into the pool — as an idempotent success rather than an error, which covers variants 2 and 3 above.

Note for the acceptance criteria: the literal "mission 87897981 completes cleanly" case now passes through the no-pane no-op branch rather than the cross-session unlink, because that mission's pane record was cleared between filing and fixing.

## Verification

- Unit: `TestResolveUnlinkTargets` (internal/server/pool_test.go) — caller-in-set, caller-absent-single, caller-absent-multiple, pool-only.
- E2E: 7 new assertions in scripts/e2e-test.sh create a headless mission, link its pool window into a second namespaced tmux session, and detach from a third. Full suite green: 151/152 passed, 0 failed (1 pre-existing SKIP).
- Discriminating check: with the two Go files parked and the same E2E run against pre-fix code, the new tests fail reproducing the bead's error verbatim — "failed to unlink window: pane 162 not found in session agenc-<ns>-e2e-caller at internal/server/pool.go:104 (unlinkPoolWindowByPane)". The two assertions covering the unchanged same-session path pass both before and after.
- NOT verified: real-machine detach of Kevin's live hyperspace missions. The running server predates this commit, so detach on his box only works after a rebuild/reinstall and server restart. Per the repo's CLAUDE.md, tmux-integration changes also require manual verification.

## Deliberately left alone

- The no-argument `agenc mission detach` picker (cmd/mission_helpers.go filterLinkedMissions) still lists only missions linked into the caller's session, so a cross-session mission has to be detached by ID. Separate change, own UX call.
- The attached-mission-limit error message is unchanged; with detach working, the remedy it points at now works.

## Live verification on Kevin's machine 2026-08-30 13:41 (closing this bead)

Kevin rebuilt and the server restarted onto the fix — the CLI reports version a31ae40 and the server process start time matches the binary mtime to the second, so the running server carries the commit rather than a stale image.

- Cross-session case: `agenc mission detach 591187e7` run from `cockpit` while its pane %79 was linked into `hyperspace`. Exit 0; %79 went from {hyperspace, agenc-pool} to agenc-pool only. The mission stayed alive and listed (IDLE), i.e. re-attachable.
- Already-detached case: `agenc mission detach b680b0e4`, pane %132 linked only into the pool — the coordinator's second failure. Exit 0 instead of the previous error.
- Cap unblocked: attached panes dropped to five (%135, %142, %167 in cockpit; %140, %165 in hyperspace), under the limit of six.
- Not exercised live: the unchanged same-session path. Every cockpit mission at the time was either the coordinator, this mission, or one actively working, so detaching one purely to demonstrate a no-op was not worth the disruption. The E2E covers that path and passes identically before and after the fix.
close_reason: Fixed in commit a31ae40 and verified live: cross-session detach and already-detached detach both succeed; attached-mission cap unblocked.

title: Nightly cron runs do nothing when attaching
description: When attaching to nightly cron-triggered runs, the missions appear to do nothing — no work happens. Need to diagnose: is the cron firing? Is the mission being created? Is the prompt landing? Is Claude exiting without producing output? Root-cause before patching.
notes: Inbox capture 2026-05-22. P1 because nightly autonomous work is one of AgenC's core value propositions — broken crons = the system is silently failing.
close_reason: Root cause: yappblocker-gate.sh UserPromptSubmit hook was blocking cron-spawned prompts during the journalling_only window (20:45-06:00). daily-state-summary (23:30) and hn-daily-pull (02:00) both fire inside that window, so the prompt was blocked before reaching the LLM — wrapper saw UserPromptSubmit but no session JSONL was ever written, and the mission idle-timed out. title: Capture 'thin CLI, thick server' guidance in AgenC CLAUDE.md
description:
There is an architectural principle in AgenC that the CLI should be thin and the server should be thick — logic that previously lived in the CLI was deliberately pushed down into the server. This decision should be captured in AgenC's CLAUDE.md so future agents working on the repo respect it instead of accidentally fattening the CLI again.

Outcome: a section in AgenC's CLAUDE.md (or wherever architectural principles are documented) that names the principle, summarizes the reasoning, and points future agents to relevant past work.

Investigation hints (from `agenc mission search 'thin CLI'`):
- Mission 2703959f ('Locating spawned mission 56c83eb5 to attach') — explicitly framed the principle: 'thin CLI, thick server'.
- Mission fea550a7 ('Cut new minor version release') — release notes mention 'Thin-CLI refactor: tmux session resolution moved from CLI to server', concrete example of the principle in action.
- Mission f2d9f09f ('Building full-text search for AGenC missions and sessions') — notes 'thin-CLI architecture alignment', another instance.

Use `agenc session print <session-id>` on the most relevant session of mission 2703959f for the original framing.

title: Enforce cron overlap policy, timeout, and max concurrent at runtime
description: GetOverlapPolicy(), GetTimeout(), GetCronsMaxConcurrent(), and IsCronDue() are defined in config but never called in the runtime. Users can configure overlap:skip, timeout:1h, and cronsMaxConcurrent but none have any effect. Before spawning a cron mission, the server must: (1) check if a mission with the same source-id is already running and skip if overlap policy is 'skip', (2) pass the timeout to the mission/wrapper and enforce it, (3) check running cron mission count against cronsMaxConcurrent before spawning. IsCronDue is dead code and should be removed.
close_reason: Removed dead config fields (timeout, overlap, cronsMaxConcurrent) and all associated types, validators, accessors, CLI flags, and tests. These can be re-added when runtime enforcement is built.

Also enables name collisions. Fix: use cron UUID for plist filename (agenc-cron.UUID.plist) which is guaranteed unique and reversible.

title: Design progressive/layered onboarding flow
description:
Both Omar (2026-03-10) and Charles McKay (2026-03-12) hit cognitive saturation during their first AgenC exposure. Charles explicitly asked Kevin to slow down twice. Omar got lost in technical friction. The onboarding needs progressive disclosure with distinct layers: (1) Hook - one impressive capability for immediate value, (2) Claude Code basics, (3) tmux orientation, (4) first guided mission, (5) config refinement loop, (6) advanced features (multi-agent, MCP, permissions). Never show everything at once. See strategy/conversations-with-others/ for full analyses.

Additional signal from Charles McKay conversation (2026-03-12):
- Autonomy gap is quantifiable: Charles's agent runs last minutes; Kevin's longest was 7 hours (standard ~10 min). The onboarding should include an explicit "autonomy progression" — start users with short, supervised runs and gradually extend.
- 60% of engineers Kevin talks to aren't even using skills. The onboarding should assume technical users (know what an LLM is) but NOT assume Claude or agentic coding experience. Include a "Claude tips & tricks" layer and a "skills 101" layer before anything AgenC-specific — this builds the prerequisite mental model AND provides space to teach Claude patterns that make everything downstream better.

title: Resolve the confusing claude-config / shadow repo / reconfig situation
description:
The current claude-config setup is deeply confusing for new users. Multiple issues compound:

1. Agents try to edit files in $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (the AgenC-managed snapshot), which AgenC correctly blocks — but agents don't understand WHY or where they should edit instead (the source config repo).
2. 'Reconfig & reload' is the mechanism to propagate changes from the source repo to the mission's snapshot, but it's not intuitive and prints garbage output.
3. There is no first-class onboarding flow for creating a Claude config repo. Users must manually: create a repo, add CLAUDE.md/skills/commands/agents dirs, create an init.sh symlink script, push to GitHub, register with 'agenc repo add --always-synced', and configure AgenC to use it. This should be a single guided command.
4. The relationship between the config repo, the AgenC repo library copy, the per-mission claude-config snapshot, and Claude's own shadow repo at ~/.claude/projects/ is not documented anywhere.

The fix should include:
- A first-class 'agenc config init-repo' (or similar) command that creates, version-controls, pushes, and registers a Claude config repo with --always-synced in one flow
- Better AgenC-injected context so agents understand they must modify the config repo source, not $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
- Consider making the Claude config repo a first-class AgenC concept with its own palette command for quick access
- Documentation explaining the full config lifecycle
notes:
2026-06-08 — Another data point for prioritization.

Claude Code v2.1.152 added a `reloadSkills: true` SessionStart return field, and v2.1.152 also shipped the `/reload-skills` slash command. Together they let an agent pick up new SKILL.md changes mid-session without restart — in a normal Claude Code setup, this turns skill iteration into a tight in-conversation loop.

In AgenC, both are effectively no-ops. Because the shadow-repo model means $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is a read-only snapshot rebuilt per spawn, when ~/.claude/ source changes the running mission's snapshot does NOT see the change until `agenc mission reload` runs. `reloadSkills:true` would re-scan a directory that has nothing new to scan; `/reload-skills` likewise.

So the shadow-repo model now actively defeats Claude Code's own forward-rolling feature surface, not just confusing users. If missions pointed directly at ~/.claude/ instead of a per-spawn snapshot, reloadSkills + /reload-skills would just work for free — and so would any future Claude-Code feature that assumes source-truth and snapshot are the same path.

Surfaced during claude-code-upgrade-review of v2.1.145→v2.1.153 (AgenC mission ed19373a-ea9a-4ccb-a2ce-fce9bbaf906b).
2026-06-15 — Another data point for prioritization.

Today Kevin ran multiple missions where he *thought* they were picking up the new versions of a plugin, but they weren't, because Claude Code was choking on the $CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR snapshot's symlinks into the plugin source repo. Surface error: "couldn't refresh marketplace <name> because it's corrupted." Root cause: plugins are shared and symlinked from the source claude-config repo, but they don't live inside the per-mission claude-config shadow, so Claude's marketplace refresh sees a broken/corrupt-looking tree and silently falls back to the snapshot's stale plugin state. The mission appears healthy, runs to completion, and produces work that looks correct — but is built against an obsolete plugin version. This is a silent-correctness failure surface, not just a usability one: Kevin's verbatim reaction was "this shadow repo is becoming a HUGE pain in the ass; it needs to go."

Adds to the pile already noted on 2026-06-08 (the shadow model defeats Claude Code's reloadSkills + /reload-skills) and 2026-05-22 (Yannik's first-install plugin-propagation failure at the Alembiq launch meeting). Three independent failure modes now traceable to the same root cause.
2026-06-24 — Fourth data point. Steve Wade onboarding session (Grain 9692ec8c-992a-4596-ac80-60e8502108b0; AgenC mission 8cdb2e67-8746-4bfa-8f37-4f2600c0de8e) hit the missing-subdirectory error at session start: Steve's global Claude config was missing agents/, hooks/, commands/, skills/ because the shadow snapshot expected them. Worked around by having Claude create empty dirs. Plus the plugin-install-inside-mission breakage (agenc-pz0v) bit Steve when he tried to install Alembiq Essentials marketplace from inside a mission. Both consequences of the same shadow-config root cause, both observed in the same 1h25m session of a new user's onboarding. Combined with the prior three data points (2026-05-22 Yannik first-install, 2026-06-08 reloadSkills no-op, 2026-06-15 silent plugin staleness), this is now a documented pattern of recurring onboarding tax for every new user.

Source pointer: ~/app/exobrain/ai-journal/2026-06-24_13-00-00___meeting-with-steve-wade-on-alembiq-and-agenc-onboarding___...md
2026-07-26 — DECISION: remove the shadow by going to "State Y" (native passthrough). Mission 98e5b6ba-59d5-4857-9555-3e0ce89dd060.

Two independent knobs, both turned:
1. Unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR entirely — missions read the user's real ~/.claude; no per-mission snapshot, no shadow repo, no per-spawn rebuild.
2. Stop injecting CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (the setup-token machine token) — missions auth via the native interactive keychain login, exactly like vanilla `claude`.

WHY both together: unsetting alone leaves connectors broken (that's knob 2, auth). Dropping the token alone while CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR stays set forces per-mission keychain cloning (Claude hashes the keychain service name off the config-dir path) — the original clone/sync headache. Turning BOTH = global keychain (no cloning) + native login (broad scope) = connectors work AND zero custom AgenC auth machinery. Kevin's framing: "just plain deliver what Claude does; if Claude breaks, that's Claude's issue."

FIXES: skill/hook staleness, reloadSkills / /reload-skills no-op, onboarding missing-dir tax, plugin marketplace corruption, plugin-install-in-mission propagation (agenc-pz0v), and collapses the keychain clone/sync machinery (removing the #11 credential-churn amplification).

SETTLED MECHANICS:
- Operational layer (AgenC state-tracking hooks, repo-library guard, agent-dir allow + repo-library deny + server-socket allowUnixSockets) injected per-invocation via `claude --settings <file>`. EMPIRICALLY VERIFIED on v2.1.191 that --settings UNIONS hooks with the user's ~/.claude/settings.json (both fire; the user's own hooks/permissions still apply; deny wins). Test: a SessionStart hook in the config-dir settings.json AND a different one via --settings both fired.
- AgenC's CLAUDE.md addendum delivered via the existing SessionStart `agenc prime` hook (additionalContext) or --append-system-prompt — no CLAUDE.md file merge.
- The ONE unavoidable piece of machinery: the .claude.json trust entry. There is NO global trust bypass in Claude Code (verified: no settings key, env var, managed-settings option, or flag short of --dangerously-skip-permissions; trusted-folders is an open upstream feature request). Trust is keyed to the git-repo root, so each mission dir needs its own entry. Plan: the AgenC server (single process → serialized) does an atomic temp-file+rename write of projects["<agent dir>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted=true into the real ~/.claude.json at mission-create (before spawn), re-reads to verify + retries, and prunes dead-mission entries on `mission rm` (folds into agenc-c4ko).

ACCEPTED COSTS:
- ~/.claude.json becomes a shared write-hotspot across all missions. It is churn-heavy (49 of 94 top-level keys are telemetry/caches/counters; a single `claude -p` wrote 500+ lines of GrowthBook cache into a 1-line file) and Claude Code holds NO write lock — the real file already has 4 backup siblings (.backup / .bak / .bak.1779279830 / .bak.kiwi), i.e. a history of corruption/recovery. Concurrent-write corruption is a real, evidenced risk AgenC can minimize (serialize + atomic + verify-retry) but not eliminate. Same class every user running concurrent vanilla sessions faces; swarms amplify.
- State Y inherits Claude's concurrent-refresh race (see agenc-lm3d) — occasional /login at 10+ concurrent missions. Bargain: clean passthrough; the race is Claude's to fix. Prerequisite: an active `claude auth login` in the global keychain. Fallback: re-adding the machine-token injection is a small reversible change dropping back to "State X" (auth stable, connectors broken) without touching the shadow work.

TO DELETE: claude-config-shadow repo + config_watcher shadow half; RewriteClaudePaths + all path rewriting + copyDirWithRewriting; BuildMissionConfigDir snapshot body + per-spawn rebuild; credential_sync.go clone/write-back/up-down sync + CloneKeychainCredentials etc.; setup-token onboarding + CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN injection (mission.go). Repoint session-reading consumers (mission print/summary/inspect, GetLastSessionID) to ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-agent-dir> via existing ComputeProjectDirpath.

OUT OF SCOPE (separate): devcontainer teardown (own bead) — the last thing forcing a materialized config dir + path rewriting, so its removal further simplifies this. Connector/auth model owned by agenc-lm3d.

Empirical basis: in-mission .claude.json / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR behavior; --settings hook-union test on v2.1.191; binary scope-array inspection; claude-code-guide research (no trust bypass; --settings merge; refresh race unfixed mid-2026).
close_reason: RESOLVED by the State-Y flip (agenc-lh8p, shipped 2026-08-03). The confusing claude-config / shadow-repo / reconfig situation is gone: missions now run plain 'claude' against the real ~/.claude (native passthrough) — no shadow repo, no per-mission snapshot, no reconfig layer. Decision was locked here; execution + production verification in agenc-lh8p.

title: Make PATH changes propagate with 'agenc server restart' — no tmux kill needed
description:
During Omar's onboarding (journal: omar-agenc-user-onboarding~2026-03-10), Claude was not on PATH inside tmux because the tmux server had been started before Claude was installed. Fixing this required exiting both the agenc server AND the tmux server, which is extremely painful and confusing.

The root cause: tmux servers inherit the shell environment at launch time. Any PATH changes made after the tmux server starts (e.g. installing Claude via brew) are invisible to all sessions within that server. The only current fix is to kill the entire tmux server and restart it, which tears down all sessions.

This is a P1 because:
1. tmux is already a leap of faith for users who've never used it before
2. Having to understand tmux server environment inheritance to fix a PATH issue is an absurd ask for a new user
3. This will hit EVERY user who installs Claude after first launching AgenC (a common sequence)

The fix should ensure that 'agenc server restart' is sufficient to pick up PATH changes. Possible approaches: have the agenc server re-source the user's shell profile when restarting, or have the wrapper script always source the profile before launching Claude, or detect and warn when Claude is not on PATH.

title: Make 'agenc config init' idempotent — retry failed steps on rerun
description: During Omar's onboarding (journal: omar-agenc-user-onboarding~2026-03-10), the OAuth token setup failed partway through 'agenc config init'. When rerun, the command just printed 'token: not set up' instead of retrying the failed step. This is a terrible experience for new users who are already in unfamiliar territory. The command must be fully idempotent: rerunning it should detect what succeeded, skip those steps, and retry what failed. Each step should be independently recoverable.

title: Define MissionStore interface for database operations
description:
Introduce interface for database operations to enable mocking and testability.

Create internal/database/interface.go:

type MissionStore interface {
    CreateMission(ctx context.Context, params *CreateMissionParams) (*Mission, error)
    GetMission(ctx context.Context, id string) (*Mission, error)
    ListMissions(ctx context.Context, params ListMissionsParams) ([]*Mission, error)
    ArchiveMission(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    DeleteMission(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    UpdateHeartbeat(ctx context.Context, id string) error
    // ... other CRUD operations
}

Use dependency injection in command constructors.
Go proverb: Accept interfaces, return concrete types.

Reference: P1-4 in specs/codebase-cleanup.md
DEPENDS ON: Database split (agenc-340), context addition (agenc-337)
When: After concrete types stabilized, not prematurely
Estimated time: 6-8 hours
notes:
2026-09-06 audit (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61), triggered by Kevin's challenge that the tech-debt epic predates a much-changed codebase. RECOMMEND CLOSE.

The interface has no consumer, the architecture it proposes injecting into does not exist, and its specified shape moves the code away from good Go.

1. Nothing wants to substitute a fake for *database.DB. The type appears in exactly ONE production location repo-wide: the db field on the Server struct, internal/server/server.go:29. No existing interface over the database, no mock, no test double.

2. Tests are not made awkward by its absence. database_test.go:11-12 opens a real SQLite file in t.TempDir(); server/auto_summary_loop_test.go:27 does the same via database.Open. That covers ~1850 lines of database tests plus the server tests needing a DB, the suite is green, and the package is at 63.8% coverage. SQLite is a local file - the real implementation is fast enough to BE the test double.

3. The command constructors the bead targets do not take a database. Under thin-CLI/thick-server, the two cmd/ files that touch a DB construct it locally: cmd/tmux_resolve_mission.go:55 and cmd/doctor.go:162 both call database.Open directly. Every other cmd/ reference to the package is to value types and helpers, not a connection (database.Mission 30 uses, database.ShortID 23, StripSnippetMarkers, Session, ListMissionsParams, ColorizeSnippet).

4. On idiom, this repo already demonstrates the correct shape, and the bead proposes its opposite. Where a double is genuinely warranted, the codebase extracts a NARROW interface at the CONSUMER: server/cron_syncer.go:19 (launchdManager, 6 methods, declared in the consuming file, commented 'Extracted from *launchd.Manager to enable testing with mocks') and server/git_command.go:26 (GitCommander, 'a narrow interface over git invocations... allows the tick state machine to be unit-tested with a fake'). Both wrap awkward externals - launchctl and git subprocesses - where the real dependency is slow or unavailable in a unit test. SQLite is neither. It quotes 'Accept interfaces, return concrete types' while proposing the placement that proverb warns off.

5. The bead states its own gating condition and seven months have not met it. Its When field reads 'After concrete types stabilized, not prematurely.' The types have stabilized; the consumer count is still zero.

Reference: P0-7 in specs/codebase-cleanup.md
DEPENDS ON: Tests must pass first (P0-4)
Impact: Enables cancellation of long-running queries
Estimated time: 8-12 hours
notes:
2026-09-06 audit (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61), triggered by Kevin's challenge that the tech-debt epic predates a much-changed codebase. RECOMMEND CLOSE.

The bead's sole stated justification - 'Impact: Enables cancellation of long-running queries' - describes a failure mode that cannot occur here.

1. There are no long-running queries. Measured against the real 60MB production DB (2882 missions, 2131 sessions, 37007 FTS rows): the heaviest query the code can issue (FTS MATCH ordered by bm25 LIMIT 60, search.go:83-91) takes 200ms; a full missions table scan ordered by created_at takes 10ms. Both figures include sqlite3 process startup, so in-process is faster.

2. Contention is bounded and returns an error rather than hanging. database.go:57 sets the DSN to busy_timeout(5000) + journal_mode(WAL) + foreign_keys(1). A blocked writer waits at most 5s then gets SQLITE_BUSY. An indefinite hang is not reachable.

3. Nothing holds the single connection across slow work. database.go:65 sets MaxOpenConns(1), which is the one configuration where a leaked connection would deadlock everything silently - so this was audited specifically: 17 Query calls, 17 matching defer rows.Close(). The only two transactions (search.go:21-43, writeable_copy_pauses.go:28-72) wrap 2-3 statements with no I/O between them; server/search_indexer.go:58-80 reads the session JSONL BEFORE entering the database, so file I/O never happens inside a transaction.

4. The codebase already applies ctx exactly where operations ARE unbounded: server/git_command.go:88 and :215 (10-minute timeout), mission/repo.go at 7 sites, launchd/manager.go at 5, server/session_summarizer.go:49 for the Claude subprocess. ctx present on every subprocess/network call and absent on the local-SQLite layer reads as deliberate judgment, not oversight.

5. Against agenc-9jgp's own cut ('does this failure class corrupt unattended work silently?') this scores NO. The contention failure is loud and bounded: a returned error the loops log and skip (search_indexer.go:47-50 logs and returns, resuming on the next 30s tick). All 11 background loops (server/server.go:219-230) already take ctx and select on ctx.Done() at their tick boundary. A targeted search for an unattended call site that could stall on a DB call found none.

Benefit the bead did NOT claim, checked anyway: per-request deadline propagation in the HTTP server. Does not apply - server.go:174 builds &http.Server{Handler: mux} with no Read/WriteTimeout, and no handler threads r.Context() into a DB call (r.Context() appears once in the package, in the request logger at middleware.go:173). Over a local unix socket with millisecond queries this is hypothetical.

Caveats stated honestly: timings used the sqlite3 CLI, not the modernc.org/sqlite driver the code uses (query latency is a property of the data and plan rather than the binding, but it was not measured through the driver). The FTS index grows with usage, but SearchMissions is reached only from the interactive 'mission search' command, never from a background loop, so growth degrades interactive responsiveness and cannot corrupt unattended work.

Flip condition: a DB call site reachable from one of the 11 unattended loops that can block unboundedly, or FTS growth pushing a query issued by an UNATTENDED loop into multi-second territory.
