description:
**Symptom:** Mission tmux window titles randomly start with "Security review…" / "Security vulnerability review…" — unrelated to the actual work.

**Real cause (NOT the Haiku classifier; original framing was wrong).** Two-layer interaction:

1. The Claude Code plugin `security-guidance` (`claude-plugins-official`, currently v2.0.6 at `~/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/security-guidance/2.0.6/hooks/security_reminder_hook.py`) registers `UserPromptSubmit` and `Stop` hooks. When a turn ends with changed files in the repo, the hook spawns a Python Claude Agent SDK process (`~/.claude/security/agent-sdk-venv/`) with `cwd` = mission project dir and prompt: `Review this change for security vulnerabilities. Changed files (you may Read these…): …`. That spawns a fresh Opus session whose JSONL lands in the same `~/.claude/projects/-Users-…-agent/` dir.

2. AgenC's auto-summarizer (`internal/server/session_summarizer.go` → Haiku) correctly summarizes the first user message of that new session to "Security vulnerability review of …". Then `GetActiveSession` (`internal/database/sessions.go:111`: `ORDER BY updated_at DESC LIMIT 1`) is called by `reconcileTmuxWindowTitle` (`internal/server/tmux.go:27`) and returns the just-finished review session. Its `auto_summary` displaces the real session's title in the mission's tmux window.

**JSONL signature of the spawned sessions (line 3, first `type: user` record):**
```
promptSource: sdk
entrypoint:   sdk-py
userType:     external
isSidechain:  false
cwd:          /Users/odyssey/.agenc/missions/<mid>/agent
```

**Why it correlates with /compact in observation:** any turn ending with file changes triggers the hook. Compact-end + commit-end + any-Stop with diffs are all triggers. The compact pattern is observation bias, not causation. Confirmed in mission `2f5599e1`: compact at 12:41:31; reviews fired at 12:53:35 / 12:54:08 / 12:54:53 / 12:55:23, aligned with commit→rebase→push, not with compact.

**Two handles for fixing:**
- **(A) Remove the source** — uninstall/disable `security-guidance` in Claude Code. Cleanest if user does not actively use the plugin.
- **(B) Make AgenC robust against SDK-spawned sessions** — the metadata (`promptSource:sdk` / `entrypoint:sdk-py`) is structured and reliable. Filter such sessions out of active-session resolution for title purposes (they shouldn't displace user-driven sessions), or out of `SessionsNeedingAutoSummary` entirely. Bug survives even if user uninstalls the plugin — any future SDK-spawning automation reproduces it.

**Provenance:** Investigated 2026-06-14 in AgenC mission `456473ec-80b3-41a7-a781-3f3bb26e864f`. Reproduced from observed mission `20cd12c0-…` (alembiq, 13 sessions, 12 displaced) and mission `2f5599e1-…` (alembiq, 4 displacements in a 2-minute commit/push window). Original framing ("Haiku biased toward 'Security review' prefix") was disproved by reading the input it actually sees — Haiku is correctly summarizing a literal "Review this change for security vulnerabilities" first user message.

title: AgenC as a secrets permission broker — missions request specific op:// refs at runtime, default-deny, brokered out-of-band
description:
The vision
----------

AgenC already has a credential-injection primitive: `BuildClaudeCmd` (internal/mission/mission.go) wraps the Claude launch with `op run --env-file .claude/secrets.env` when that file is present, resolving 1Password `op://` references into env vars at launch — outside the per-Bash seatbelt that blocks in-mission `op read`. Good primitive, but the grant is declared at rest, per repo: every mission spawned in that repo gets every injected ref, with no runtime consent.

The next step is the **dynamic, governed** version of the same data flow. Missions *request* specific secret refs at runtime; AgenC, holding a default-deny registry of grantable refs, brokers the `op` resolution out-of-band and notifies the user for per-request approval. Claude never holds standing creds — it gets a just-in-time value (or a typed handle) only for the duration of one operation.

This is philosophically the same posture as 1Password's official Codex MCP "Environments" server: the agent never holds standing creds; a broker injects just-in-time. Applied AgenC-natively.

How this fits with existing work
--------------------------------

- Sibling to `agenc-415l` (per-mission unix-socket API scoping). 415l scopes cross-mission API access; this scopes secret access. Both move AgenC from "flat trust" toward per-mission capabilities — same theme, different surface.
- Builds directly on the static `secrets.env`-in-repo primitive in `BuildClaudeCmd`. The runtime layer is the new engineering.

Concrete first proof-point
--------------------------

`github.com/mieubrisse/haircut-booking` is the first real use of the static primitive in Kevin's setup — a single-purpose repo whose `.claude/secrets.env` injects Trinks creds for the `/book-haircut` skill (which runs in two modes: launcher spawns the credentialed mission; booking does the work). Watching this in production tells us whether the static "repo-is-the-boundary" model is sufficient, or where the dynamic broker starts being missed (e.g., per-call consent for a credential, one-off ad-hoc requests, audit-logged exposure).

Design seeds (not prescriptions)
--------------------------------

- Grant registry probably lives in `agenc config` (structured config already exists).
- The request → approve loop needs a real notification + response channel, heavier than the file-based primitive — that's the actual new engineering.
- Open: what's the right handle the agent uses without ever holding the literal value? Options span inline string (status quo, agent sees value), typed reference (broker mediates each use, à la 1Password's MCP injection model), and browser-extension autofill (agent never sees value at all).

Provenance
----------

Drafted in AgenC mission `daf208e7-71ab-45ae-88ab-0150f604e55c` / session `7acb9488`. The full conversation — research on 1Password access patterns under the Claude sandbox, the divergent option set, and the build of the haircut-booking precedent — is replayable via `agenc session print 7acb9488 --all`.

title: Keybinding regeneration leaks removed bindings into tmux
description:
## Problem

When a palette command's `tmuxKeybinding` is removed or remapped to a different key in `config.yml`, the previous binding stays resident in the running tmux server's memory until the server is restarted.

Concrete repro from a real user session:
- User had `copyMissionUuid: tmuxKeybinding: -n C-v` at some point.
- User later changed it to `-n C-,`.
- `tmux list-keys -T root` still shows BOTH a C-v and a C-, binding running the copyMissionUuid shell. Pressing Ctrl-V fires the stale binding, which then fails with exit 1 on non-mission panes.

## Root cause

`internal/tmux/keybindings.go:233` regenerates the AgenC-managed keybindings file and runs `tmux source-file` on it. `source-file` is additive — it does not unbind keys that have been removed from the file since the last source. So any key the user removes or remaps persists in tmux's in-memory binding table indefinitely.

## Why it matters

- Stale bindings silently override new ones (or coexist confusingly).
- Users have no way to discover what's bound except `tmux list-keys`, which is not an AgenC affordance.
- The mismatch between `config.yml` and live tmux state breaks the user's mental model of the config as the source of truth.

## Scope hints (not prescriptive)

- The AgenC-managed keybindings file already has a known shape; the regeneration step has full knowledge of which keys *should* be bound. The gap is reconciling that against what's currently bound.
- Need to be careful not to unbind keys outside AgenC's ownership (user-defined bindings, tmux defaults like copy-mode C-v).
- Possibly: track previously-emitted AgenC keys (e.g. via a sentinel file or sidecar manifest) and unbind any that aren't in the new set before sourcing.

## Provenance

AgenC mission: 79823280-b7ae-44dc-804f-a9aeb942ab51

title: Add a formal 'done' status to missions (separate from archive/active)
description:
Missions currently have active/idle/archived states but no formal notion of 'resolved' — i.e. 'this mission's work is finished, the outcome is captured, nothing more is needed here.' Without that distinction, it's hard to tell at a glance which missions are still in flight vs which have already been wrapped up.

Use cases: a mission listing view that filters out done missions; an end-of-day summary that counts how many missions were resolved that day; reload/spawn flows that don't accidentally resume a mission that's already considered finished.

Surface: probably a new 'agenc mission done <id>' subcommand (or similar) plus state field in the mission record. Should compose with existing detach/archive semantics.

title: Refactor GenerateOverlay to accept host home dir via params (stop tests polluting ~/.claude/projects)
description:
internal/devcontainer/overlay.go:72-78 calls os.UserHomeDir() directly to compute the host bind-mount source for ~/.claude/projects/<encoded>/. The function legitimately needs to pre-create this directory on the host so devcontainers can bind-mount it (session JSONLs flow host↔container through that path), but because the home directory is read inline instead of passed via OverlayParams, every overlay_test.go run writes real entries (mission ID "test-uuid-123") into the developer's actual ~/.claude/projects/. Every make check pollutes the user's Claude config.

Fix: thread the host home directory (or the claude-projects directory) through OverlayParams so tests can supply a t.TempDir() and production passes the real home dir from the wrapper. Update internal/wrapper/devcontainer.go to populate the new field, and overlay_test.go's newTestParams helper to use t.TempDir().

Side effect: removes the need for any "~/.claude/projects/**" sandbox allowlist in .claude/settings.json (which would mask this bug rather than fix it).

Discovered while debugging make check sandbox failures in AgenC mission 4a635222-88a6-4b5b-a80b-bba523c913f5. Replay: agenc session ls --mission 4a635222-88a6-4b5b-a80b-bba523c913f5
acceptance_criteria:
- OverlayParams gains a field for the host home (or claude-projects) directory
- overlay.go no longer calls os.UserHomeDir() — it uses the params field
- overlay_test.go's newTestParams uses t.TempDir() so no test writes outside the temp dir
- internal/wrapper/devcontainer.go populates the new field from the real os.UserHomeDir() (the one place that legitimately needs it)
- make check passes the devcontainer test suite without writing to ~/.claude/projects/

title: Replace repoUpdateCh buffered channel with per-repo pending-state map
description:
The repo-update-worker channel (repoUpdateCh, size 64) periodically saturates under normal load, producing one-per-minute warnings like:

    Repo update: channel full, skipping 'github.com/mieubrisse/dotfiles'

Saturation pattern recurs across days (observed 2026-03-01, 2026-03-09, 2026-05-25). Root cause is structural: the channel treats updates as distinct events, but the actual semantic is a state ("this repo should get fetched soon"). Same-repo bursts (e.g., a writeable-copy push storm, or the 60s periodic sweep running while a fetch is slow) enqueue redundant work that fills the buffer and gets dropped via the non-blocking `default:` branch.

Proposal: replace the buffered channel with a per-repo pending-state map plus a size-1 wake-up notify channel. Producers call `s.requestRepoUpdate(req)` which coalesces by repoName (OR-merging flags refreshDefaultBranch and forceRunHook). Worker drains pending entries; if a new request arrives during processing of the same repo, it lands in pending and triggers a re-run after the in-flight one finishes. Eliminates "channel full" warnings entirely (no buffer to overflow), eliminates redundant work, and removes the magic 64 constant.

Companion change: move postUpdateHook off the worker (run in a goroutine with per-repo "hook in flight" guard). Today's design allows a 30-minute hook timeout to block ALL repo updates synchronously.

Full diagnosis and proposal in AgenC mission 4a635222-88a6-4b5b-a80b-bba523c913f5. Replay with: agenc session ls --mission 4a635222-88a6-4b5b-a80b-bba523c913f5
design:
Data structure (in Server):

    type repoUpdateState struct {
        mu       sync.Mutex
        pending  map[string]repoUpdateRequest  // repoName -> merged request
        inFlight map[string]bool               // repoName -> currently processing
        notify   chan struct{}                 // size 1, wake-up signal only
    }

Replace these 4 call sites that send on s.repoUpdateCh with s.requestRepoUpdate(req):
- internal/server/template_updater.go:100 (periodic sweep)
- internal/server/template_updater.go:137 (first-clone hook)
- internal/server/repos.go:39 (push-event handler)
- internal/server/writeable_copies_watcher.go:187 (writeable-copy ref watcher)

Enqueue (non-blocking, never drops):
  - If pending[repoName] exists: OR-merge flags, return
  - Else insert and non-blocking send on notify

Worker:
  - Block on notify or ctx.Done
  - Drain loop: pick a pending entry where !inFlight[name]; move to inFlight; mu.Unlock; processRepoUpdate; mu.Lock; remove from inFlight; if pending[name] exists (new request arrived during processing), re-signal notify
  - This naturally handles "push arrived while fetching" — the new push creates a fresh pending entry, the worker sees it after finishing, and re-runs

Async postUpdateHook:
  - processRepoUpdate spawns hook goroutine and returns immediately
  - Per-repo hookInFlight map; if already running, set sticky "run-again" bit instead of overlapping

Out of scope for this issue:
  - Worker pool size (stays at 1; head-of-line bounded by 30s git timeout, not 30min hook timeout)
  - 60s periodic sweep (stays as safety net)
  - writeableCopyReconcileCh size 16 (same shape of bug, separate follow-up)
  - mission.ForceUpdateRepo using context.Background() (separate code smell)

Test plan:
  - Unit: coalesce-merges-flags, in-flight-guards, push-during-fetch-triggers-re-run, hook-async-doesn't-block-worker
  - E2E (scripts/e2e-test.sh): POST /repos/.../push-event 5x in quick succession for same repo, verify exactly one HEAD-changed sequence and zero "channel full" lines
  - Update docs/system-architecture.md section "8. Repo update worker"
acceptance_criteria:
- s.repoUpdateCh chan removed; replaced with repoUpdateState struct
- All 4 producer call sites use s.requestRepoUpdate(req) instead of channel send
- "channel full" warnings impossible from this code path (no buffer to overflow)
- postUpdateHook runs in goroutine; worker is not blocked by slow hooks
- Per-repo hook-in-flight guard prevents overlapping hooks for the same repo
- E2E test verifies 5 rapid push-events for the same repo produce one fetch
- docs/system-architecture.md section 8 updated to describe pending-state map
- make build and make e2e both pass

title: Plugin installs in a mission don't propagate to global claude-config
description: When a user runs Claude Code plugin install inside an AgenC mission, the plugin lands in the mission's claude-config snapshot but doesn't get installed globally — so it disappears the next time a fresh mission spawns. Tied to the per-mission claude-config snapshot architecture: missions read from a read-only snapshot of ~/.claude/, so plugin-installer writes that land inside a mission have no upstream propagation path. Need a mechanism to forward plugin installs back to the canonical ~/.claude/ tree (or to forbid plugin installs inside missions and route them through the global config edit surface).
notes:
Inbox capture 2026-05-22. Originally categorized as an Alembiq problem; rerouted to AgenC since the root cause is the per-mission claude-config isolation, not Alembiq itself.

2026-05-22 — Yannik hit this at first Alembiq install during 2026-05-21 AgenC workflow review meeting [06:28]: "a limbic in an agency session did not install it to my global system plugin. Stuff. Probably might want to look into that." Kevin acknowledged: "I'm getting really close to ripping out the like isolation thing. It's getting really annoying to me." Customer-facing first-install friction with a paying user. See journal: ~/app/exobrain/ai-journal/2026-05-22_16-25-07___kevin-yannik-agenc-workflow-review___ai-generated,coaching,meeting,alembiq,agenc.md
2026-06-24 — Recurrence. Steve Wade hit this trying to install Alembiq Essentials marketplace from inside a mission during his 1:1 onboarding session. Workaround applied (install in Claude session outside any mission, then Reload Mission). Same root cause as agenc-tcoh (the shadow-config model). Source: AI journal entry 2026-06-24_13-00-00 (AgenC mission 8cdb2e67-8746-4bfa-8f37-4f2600c0de8e).
close_reason: FIXED by the State-Y flip (agenc-lh8p) via mechanism. The plugin-propagation gap was caused by the per-mission claude-config SNAPSHOT — plugin installs wrote to the frozen snapshot, not global. State Y removes the snapshot; missions read AND write the user's real ~/.claude / ~/.claude.json natively, so a plugin installed in a mission lands in the global config directly. Fixed by mechanism, not separately regression-tested — recommend a quick spot-check (install a plugin in a State-Y mission, confirm it appears globally); reopen if it fails.

title: Pin allow-rename off on AgenC mission windows
description: GitHub issue #5: shell-emitted OSC title escape sequences (ESC]2;<title>) can overwrite the AgenC mission title in tmux windows when the user has 'allow-rename on' in their tmux config. Reporter (ro0mquy, issue #5) confirmed: with allow-rename on, opening a Side Shell rewrites the window title to the shell's cwd; with allow-rename off, title stays pinned. Fix: chain 'set-window-option allow-rename off' onto the tmux new-window invocation in internal/server/pool.go so every AgenC-created mission window pins the flag at birth, regardless of the user's global setting. Per-window scope means user's non-AgenC windows are untouched.
close_reason: Pinned allow-rename=off on AgenC mission windows via tmux set-window-option chained into the new-window invocation. Commit b878464. Issue #5 closes via 'Fixes' keyword on push.

title: claude.ai-connector MCPs (composio, polar, canva, grain, posthog, vercel) don't work in AgenC missions due to setup-token scope limitation
description:
## Symptom

In any AgenC mission, claude.ai-mediated MCP connector servers — composio, polar, canva, grain, posthog, vercel — fail to function. The /mcp picker shows them as "needs authentication" and tool calls into them fail with auth prompts.

Direct-OAuth MCPs (notion, todoist, chrome-devtools, deepwiki) continue to work normally. The same MCP connectors work fine when invoked via vanilla `claude` outside of AgenC, on the same machine, same user, same Keychain.

## Root Cause (verified by binary inspection)

AgenC's wrapper injects `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var when spawning Claude (see `internal/mission/mission.go:115`). The Claude Code binary's auth resolver, when this env var is set, returns a credential object with **`scopes: ["user:inference"]`** only — verified by string extraction from the v2.1.119 binary at /opt/homebrew/Caskroom/claude-code/2.1.119/claude:

```js
if (process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN) return {
  accessToken: process.env.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN,
  refreshToken: null,
  expiresAt: null,
  scopes: ["user:inference"],
  ...
}
```

claude.ai connector endpoints require broader scopes than `user:inference` to authorize per-server OAuth handshakes. The interactive `claudeAiOauth` credential in the Keychain (used by vanilla Claude) has the broader scope set; the programmatic `claude setup-token`-issued token does not.

Empirical confirmation: spawning Claude with the AgenC mission's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR but **without** CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN makes connectors work and exposes additional claude.ai connectors (Facebook Ads, Gmail, Calendar, Drive) that AgenC missions can't see at all.

## Why AgenC uses CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (history)

This was a deliberate workaround for anthropics/claude-code#24317 — concurrent Claude Code sessions sharing one OAuth refresh token race against each other on rotation, each refresh invalidates the others' in-memory copy, forcing repeated /login. Kevin documented this workaround himself on the issue (2026-02-21): "I worked around this using claude setup-token and feeding it in as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN environment variable. It skips all the 'OAuth tokens invalidating each other', but has the downside that it doesn't allow /usage." We've now discovered the silent third cost: no claude.ai connector MCPs.

## Why we can't just switch to claudeAiOauth

The refresh race is NOT fully fixed in current Claude Code. Multiple fixes shipped between v2.1.119 (currently installed) and v2.1.148 (current latest, released 2026-05-22): 2.1.126, 2.1.129, 2.1.133, 2.1.136, 2.1.143. But user reports in anthropics/claude-code#54443 (open as of 2026-05-17 on v2.1.143) and #58066 (closed dup) confirm the race still triggers /login prompts with **2-3 concurrent sessions**. AgenC typically runs 10+ concurrent missions — well beyond the known-broken threshold.

The fundamental issue is server-side: refresh tokens are single-use and access tokens are revoked when siblings refresh. Per #58066: "Each refresh appears to revoke any previously issued access token server-side, so sibling processes immediately receive 401."

## Investigation provenance

- AgenC mission: 60f74315-be4c-42e3-a2df-27431806e378
- Session UUID for full transcript: see mission's wrapper log
- Date: 2026-05-21/22
design:
## Three paths considered

### A. Status quo — keep CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, accept no connectors
Refresh race avoided. Connectors permanently broken in AgenC missions. New minor wrinkle from anthropics/claude-code#54999: parallel spawns sharing one setup-token see ~5-10s server-side serialization tax (latency, not failure).

### B. Switch to claudeAiOauth — drop the env var injection
Connectors work. Refresh race comes back hard at 10+ mission scale based on May 2026 reports on Claude 2.1.143. **Not recommended** — would re-introduce the exact problem the current workaround was designed to solve.

### C. AgenC-side refresh coordination
The only path that gets both connector access AND stability under concurrent missions.

Shape of work:
1. AgenC server takes over claudeAiOauth refresh: implements the Anthropic OAuth refresh protocol (POST https://platform.claude.com/v1/oauth/token with grant_type=refresh_token), proactively refreshes well before the access token's expiresAt.
2. Server writes refreshed token to Keychain on a single-writer schedule (no concurrent writes).
3. Existing credential_sync.go upward/downward broadcast plumbing can be extended to coordinate.
4. Critical and tricky: prevent in-mission Claude from doing its own refresh. There may not be an env flag for this. If Claude detects an expired access token, it'll try to refresh regardless. Workaround: keep the Keychain entry fresh enough that missions never hit the expiry threshold.

Open questions on (C):
- Does Claude Code have any way to be told "don't refresh, just use what's in the Keychain"? If not, the server has to be very aggressive about refresh frequency.
- How to handle the proactive-refresh failure case (claudeAiOauth refresh token expires / gets rejected)?
- Does the user's existing daemon at ~/.claude/daemon/ already do this for the desktop app? Can AgenC piggyback?

### Decision deferred
Kevin is choosing to defer this. Connectors don't work in AgenC for now. Revisit when either:
- Anthropic ships a fix to anthropics/claude-code#54443 / #24317 such that vanilla concurrent-session refresh is reliable at 10+ session scale
- Or connector access becomes important enough to invest in (C)
notes:
## Re-surfaced 2026-05-27 weekly retrospective

A retrospective scan of 116 substantive interactive missions from 2026-05-18 → 2026-05-25 (mission d303ef1d-caaa-4003-9f14-577c8f4948d9) identified Composio/MCP auth fragility as the #2 friction class across the entire week. The pain manifests as:

- Vendor 5xx silently breaking downstream skills (`/weekly-plan`, `/process-todoist-inbox`) — missions 49fef4da, 449dca67
- OAuth doesn't persist across missions — every Composio-touching task hits an interactive paste-back dance (a8de8aa8, 81899588, d3b59e5b, c95626ef)
- Scheduled/headless verification jobs cannot refresh tokens at all (efffcc32)
- Pre-mission MCP-auth probe is missing — agents discover unauthenticated state mid-draft rather than at spawn

Related downstream Todoist project: "🔌 Fix MCP servers needing constant login" (6gj27CGW4R53HHF6).

User hypothesis 2026-05-27: "the fix is to get rid of the claude-config shadow directory". This doesn't match the documented root cause above — the per-mission snapshot is not the load-bearing problem; the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` env var injection (mission.go:115) limits scopes to `user:inference`. Path C (AgenC-side refresh coordination) remains the clean fix; Path B (drop the env var) re-introduces the refresh race that's worse than no connectors.

Adjacent infra: agenc-tpde (Supergateway exploration), agenc-10mi (MCPs-as-CLIs).
2026-07-26 — Re-checked on Claude Code v2.1.191 (72 versions past the original v2.1.119 finding). Mission 98e5b6ba-59d5-4857-9555-3e0ce89dd060.

setup-token still does NOT carry connector scopes. Binary evidence: two OAuth scope arrays are defined next to claude.ai/oauth/claude-code-client-metadata — a narrow set (~[user:profile, user:inference]) and a broad set ([..., user:sessions:claude_code, user:mcp_servers, user:file_upload]). user:mcp_servers (what claude.ai connectors need) is ONLY in the broad set, which is wired to the interactive-login OAuth client — not setup-token. `claude setup-token --help` exposes no scope-selection flag. claude-code-guide research found no dated changelog broadening setup-token's scopes. So keeping the machine token keeps connectors dead; connector scope comes only with interactive claudeAiOauth login. (Kevin chose NOT to spend the definitive fresh-setup-token test — settled on native login.)

Daemon: ~/.claude/daemon/ IS an auth supervisor doing proactive OAuth refresh (~7.9h schedule, single writer). But it does NOT coordinate/serialize refresh across concurrent sessions (no lock / IPC / leader election; daemon.log is auth-refresh-only). The concurrent-refresh race (#24317 / #54443) remains unfixed as of mid-2026 per research. The daemon does not rescue interactive-login-at-scale.

RESOLUTION (supersedes the "decision deferred" in DESIGN): the connector fix is folded into the shadow-removal work (agenc-tcoh "State Y"): unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR + STOP injecting CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN → missions use the native interactive keychain login (broad scope) → connectors work by construction, with zero custom AgenC auth machinery. Cost: inherits Claude's refresh race at 10+ concurrent missions — Kevin's accepted bargain: be a clean passthrough, the race is Claude's to fix. Prerequisite: an active `claude auth login` in the global keychain.

REJECTED alternative: injecting the interactive login's broad-scope ACCESS token via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (env tokens can't self-refresh → would dodge the race, but needs AgenC to own refresh + re-inject on ~8h expiry; running sessions age out → 401). Rejected as fragile, and "we don't want interactive sessions pretending to be machine sessions" (Kevin).

FALLBACK if the race proves intolerable: re-add the machine-token injection (drops to "State X": auth stable, connectors broken) — small and reversible.
close_reason: FIXED by the State-Y flip (agenc-lh8p). Root cause: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (setup-token machine token) injection broke the claude.ai-connector MCPs. State Y makes token injection CONDITIONAL (default = native ~/.claude auth). Kevin confirmed empirically 2026-08-03 in the go-live test — 'MCP auth is persisting, things are Just Working': connectors work under native auth. (Requires no machine-token file present; 'agenc token clear' if one lingers.)

title: Pre-meeting Mac notification scheduling feature
description:
[What]: Implement a mechanism in AgenC for users to schedule local macOS notifications that fire at a specified time before a calendar event, with custom reminder text. Could be a CLI command (e.g., agenc notify schedule --at "<datetime>" --message "...") or integration with macOS calendar reminders. The notification needs to surface as a native macOS notification, not just an in-tmux message.

[Why]: Solo-founder behavioral risk surfaced 2026-05-21 during Kevin's first AI office hours conversion event: Kevin tends to over-narrate / go theoretical during live calls, instead of dropping into hands-on demonstration. Validated by two independent observers in one day (Kevin's own self-reflection + Yannik's debrief feedback). Structural fix is a pre-meeting reminder firing 5-10 min before each scheduled office hours or sales call, with content like "listen more, theorize less, do hands-on". Verbal commitments don't scale across months between events; an automated reminder does.

title: Auto-inject macOS BSD user temp dir into mission sandbox allowWrite
description:
AgenC missions on macOS run Bash subprocesses under a sandbox whose `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite` does not include the macOS BSD user temp directory (`/var/folders/<hash>/T/`, returned by `confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)`). BSD `mktemp(1)` without args writes to that path *regardless of $TMPDIR*, so any tool that shells out to `mktemp -d` — pre-commit hooks (husky, lefthook), test runners, build scripts — fails inside a mission with `Operation not permitted`. The user can work around it per-script (`mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/prefix.XXXXXX"`), but BSD-mktemp-in-third-party-tooling is a recurring footgun that an AgenC user has no way to fix from their own settings without per-mission edits.

## Fix

In `internal/claudeconfig/merge.go`, alongside the existing `mergeAgencSandbox` (which injects the AgenC server socket into `sandbox.network.allowUnixSockets`), add `mergeAgencSandboxFilesystem` that, on Darwin only, resolves `getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR` and appends `<that-path>/**` to `sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite`. No-op on Linux/container missions.

## Out of scope

This is *not* a fix for the original misdiagnosis that filed this bug ("agenc drops user-level sandbox additions"). AgenC's deep-merge is correct; user-level entries land in the merged on-disk `claude-config/settings.json`. The original symptom — Kevin's nested `sandbox.filesystem.write.allowOnly` entries appearing to be ignored — is a Claude Code schema mismatch: the supported schema is *flat* (`sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite`, additive), not nested (`sandbox.filesystem.write.allowOnly`). Zod silently drops the unrecognized fields. Kevin's `~/.claude/settings.json` needs migration to the flat schema separately (handled in a different conversation).

## Provenance

Originated in AgenC mission 46c2e412-df56-4ce2-adad-b5c1e80a991d. Cross-investigated and rescoped in AgenC mission $AGENC_MISSION_UUID.
notes:
Reverted in c4c63fc (2026-05-21). Kevin's call: AgenC silently auto-injecting /var/folders/<hash>/T/** into every mission's sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite is the wrong layer. The user decides what their missions can write to via their own ~/.claude/settings.json — not AgenC expanding the allowlist on their behalf.

Kevin's exact words (mission 46c2e412-df56-4ce2-adad-b5c1e80a991d): "I'm not comfortable with this; it's up to the user to decide. revert the AgenC change, and instead store it in my own settings.json."

User-side fix already in place: Kevin's ~/.claude/settings.json has /var/folders/*/*/T/** and /private/var/folders/*/*/T/** in sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite (flat schema). Confirmed working empirically — mid-path wildcards expand correctly in the Claude Code sandbox glob matcher.

Closing as wontfix.
close_reason: WONTFIX — user-side mechanism preferred. AgenC should not auto-inject paths into mission sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite; that's the user's decision via their own ~/.claude/settings.json. Reverted in c4c63fc. Kevin's settings.json already has /var/folders/*/*/T/** covering this, working empirically.

title: Audit AgenC docs for single-source-of-truth drift and interpolate canonical references
description:
Two Adjutant missions tried to use a cron --overlap flag in the past 24 hours because internal/claudeconfig/adjutant_claude.md and CLI Long help text documented it — but the flag was never implemented. While fixing that, I also caught a separate drift: cmd/cron.go and docs/configuration.md wrote `git: github.com/owner/repo` in example YAML, but the actual struct tag is `yaml:"repo"` (internal/config/agenc_config.go:30). This is the classic stale-cache problem: docs duplicate technical details (flag names, YAML keys, struct field names) without any mechanism keeping them in sync with the canonical source.

Kevin's preference (explicit): interpolate everywhere a doc references a technical identifier, even at the cost of harder-to-read source. "Agents know how to deal with interpolation easily; agents struggle with remembering to update duplicated strings."

Scope:

1. Sweep all Cobra Long help strings in cmd/ for hardcoded flag names, YAML keys, and struct field names. Replace with fmt.Sprintf using the existing flag-name constants (cronConfigRepoFlagName etc.) and reflection-derived YAML keys from the config structs.

2. Sweep docs/ markdown for the same — at minimum docs/configuration.md, docs/system-architecture.md, internal/claudeconfig/adjutant_claude.md, and anything under docs/cli/ that isn't auto-generated. Most docs/cli/ files ARE regenerated from Cobra Long text by `make build`, so fixing the Cobra strings handles them.

3. Add a round-trip YAML test: parse every fenced YAML block from Cobra Long strings (and ideally docs/configuration.md examples) through the actual config loader with strict mode (unknown fields → error). This catches drift at build time as a structural guarantee, complementing the interpolation.

4. Document the convention in CLAUDE.md or a skill so future contributors don't reintroduce the pattern.

Context: AgenC mission c992afb7-8c18-4760-9534-94e0a37cb6ab, session 6a7de280. Run `agenc session print 6a7de280` for the full discussion. The fix for the immediate symptom (removing the false --overlap/--timeout references) landed in commit af9993a; this bead is the broader structural sweep.
notes: Prior art for the interpolation pattern: the CLI flag-name constants in cmd/ are already used at flag-registration time but not in the surrounding help text. That's the cheapest first win.

title: Track skills used per mission; enable skill-based mission search
description: Record which skills a mission invokes and make missions searchable by skill. Lets a skill find its own past usages so missions become an ever-appending log — useful for skill iteration, debugging, and pattern discovery.
notes:
Concrete incident illustrating this feature's value (AgenC mission 44b55cf7, session 1d728ec5, 2026-06-02 HN-daily-pull cron run):

In this mission, the agent edited a SKILL.md (hacker-news-daily-pull/SKILL.md) without first invoking /alembiq:cc-skill-management — despite a CLAUDE.md rule mandating skill invocation for prompt edits. Root cause from Five Whys: the rule is intent-keyed documentation, not action-keyed enforcement. Both major branches of the diagnosis converge on the same bedrock — "a hook should mechanically enforce the SKILL.md → cc-skill-management mapping at the file-path level" — but mechanical enforcement requires the agent harness to know whether a skill has been invoked in the current mission. That is this feature.

In the meantime, the user is shipping a soft-reminder PreToolUse hook in ~/.claude/hooks as a documented workaround. The soft reminder is the highest-priority structural fix achievable WITHOUT this tracking infrastructure. Once zmhy and agenc-w039 land, the workaround can be upgraded to a hard gate.

Replay: agenc session print 1d728ec5 --all

---

Second instance, same pattern (AgenC mission d291a7a0, session 335b6ed8, 2026-06-08 Diamond Cascade on SKILL.md skill underfiring):

The Cascade independently rediscovered the same root cause through transcript analysis of mission a7fea299 (newsletter V0): agent did ~18 Write/Edit ops on SKILL.md files before /alembiq:cc-skill-management fired. PROBLEM diagnosed trigger-modality mismatch (linguistic skill-selection vs. file-path-typed work). SOLUTION matrix-converged on the same soft-reminder workaround already documented here. Implementing dotfiles-jql (rule + non-blocking PreToolUse hook on **/SKILL.md) in this session. Cumulative demand signal for zmhy+w039 enforcement layer.

Replay: agenc session print 335b6ed8 --all

---

Third instance, same pattern (AgenC mission 36a84689-8297-4bb7-913f-98eb1b228585, session 524ce1e4, 2026-06-09 Diamond Cascade authoring /agenc-cron-loops skill):

Agent invoked /prompt-engineer directly (per explicit user direction "Can you use prompt-engineer to create this") instead of routing through /cc-skill-management. PreToolUse hook fired 5 times (1 Write + 4 Edits) — agent noted the warnings but deferred to REFLECT rather than looping back mid-flow. Diamond Cascade REFLECT phase ran /five-whys; bedrock causes identified: (a) /prompt-engineer's upstream-only constraint is invisible at the description level (only visible after the skill body is loaded, by which point invocation already happened), (b) CLAUDE.md had no MANDATORY rule for /cc-configuration on Claude config work paralleling the existing /software-engineer rule, (c) soft-warn hooks teach agents to ignore the warning class under sunk-cost pressure (5 fires, 0 loopbacks this session). Confirms that even with explicit user routing direction, the bypass produces real gaps: design.md decision was never made; classification (instructional vs FYI) was never explicit. User shipped a CLAUDE.md MANDATORY rule for /cc-configuration in this session as the documented workaround (parallels existing /software-engineer rule); reaffirms zmhy+w039 as the durable hard-gate path once the harness can know which skills were invoked in a mission.

Replay: agenc session print 524ce1e4 --all

title: Bug: missions not spawning as headed when --headless not passed
description: Repro: agenc mission new <repo> --prompt '...' (without --headless) is spawning in background pool window instead of as a headed tmux mission. Originating example: mission 9837c12c-ba83-49fb-9ea5-d9533c6fc7a9 spawned d734187a, which landed in background despite no --headless flag.

title: Make lesson rollback easier via in-session notes consumed by background sweeper
description: Let the mission record session-quality notes (what's going well, what's not). The background sweeper/upgrader then consumes these notes when analyzing the session and proposing fixes — so rollback / structural-fix decisions are grounded in the agent's own running self-assessment, not just post-hoc transcript analysis.
notes: Expand scope: 'add a note to this session' should support POSITIVE signals too, not just negatives. Example: 'wow, Claude reliably called complexity-estimator in mission X — keep doing that.' The sweeper/upgrader treats positive notes as proposals to codify the pattern (skill, CLAUDE.md rule), not just bug fixes. Notes carry signed signal {+ / -}; upgrader treats them differently.

title: Add labelling of missions; allow skills to set labels
description: Let skills tag missions with labels (e.g., 'inbox-processing', 'content-production'). Enables later filtering and discovery via the existing skill-search machinery — see related bead about tracking skills used per mission.

title: Require skill invocation before specific commands (e.g., CLAUDE.md edits need cc-claude-md-management)
description: AgenC enforces that a mission has invoked a specified skill before certain commands are allowed. Example: editing CLAUDE.md is blocked unless cc-claude-md-management has been invoked. Hook-level enforcement, mission-scoped.
notes:
Concrete instance and reference workaround (AgenC mission 44b55cf7, session 1d728ec5, 2026-06-02 HN-daily-pull cron run):

This mission produced the canonical parallel to the bead's CLAUDE.md/cc-claude-md-management example — the mapping SKILL.md edits → /alembiq:cc-skill-management. Same shape: 1:1 deterministic file-path → skill mapping. Diagnosis (Five Whys in session 1d728ec5) traced the failure to intent-keyed documentation when the mapping is mechanizable on path.

Reference workaround pending this feature: a soft-reminder PreToolUse hook installed at ~/.claude/hooks/ that fires on Edit|Write|MultiEdit when file_path matches **/SKILL.md and injects additionalContext suggesting /alembiq:cc-skill-management. Soft-only because hard-gate enforcement requires zmhy (skill-invocation tracking) to know whether the skill was already invoked this mission. Once zmhy + w039 land, the soft reminder is replaced by mechanical block.

Depends-on candidate: agenc-zmhy.

Replay: agenc session print 1d728ec5 --all

---

Second instance, same pattern (AgenC mission d291a7a0, session 335b6ed8, 2026-06-08 Diamond Cascade on SKILL.md skill underfiring):

The Cascade independently rediscovered the same root cause via transcript analysis of mission a7fea299 (newsletter V0). Matrix-converged on the same soft-reminder workaround documented here. Implementing dotfiles-jql (rule + non-blocking PreToolUse hook on **/SKILL.md) in this session. Cumulative demand signal for zmhy+w039 enforcement layer.

Replay: agenc session print 335b6ed8 --all
---

Third instance — soft-reminder fired but agent rationalized past it (AgenC mission a46a1023, session 24c85995, 2026-06-08 Diamond Cascade extracting Alembiq aesthetic):

The soft-reminder PreToolUse hook (the workaround above) DID fire on the SKILL.md edit. Path-gated rule .claude/rules/skill-authoring.md surfaced the routing reminder in the tool call's additional context. The agent still made the wrong call BEFORE the hook fired and noticed the reminder only AFTER the edit landed. Diagnosis (Five Whys in session 24c85995): the agent had invoked /alembiq:cc-skill-management once earlier in the same cascade for a different SKILL.md (alembiq-aesthetic, fresh creation) and treated the workflow as session-cleared rather than per-action. Compressed mental model dropped the "new paragraph does not qualify as small targeted edit" threshold.

Significance: this is the first documented instance where the soft-reminder workaround was in place AND it failed to close the gap. Demonstrates that even with reminder hooks firing, training-prior-driven judgment overrides documentation. Confirms that the hard-gate (w039 + zmhy) is what's actually needed; the soft reminder is structurally insufficient.

Replay: agenc session print 24c85995 --all
---

Fourth instance — soft-reminder fired post-Write twice in the same cascade, agent rationalized BOTH times (AgenC mission 53b7c924-20bc-4f5e-a93e-7b91bc8d9ab2, session current, 2026-06-13 Diamond Cascade extracting vr-instagram-caption-writing):

First miss: cascade routed directly from /diamond-cascade → /prompt-engineer for SKILL.md authoring, skipping /alembiq:cc-skill-management entirely. Soft-reminder hook fired on the first Write; agent caught the miss, invoked /alembiq:cc-skill-management retroactively as a verification pass, and patched the design.md template conformance gap that catch surfaced.

Second miss, same session: agent then performed a substantive rewrite of the SAME SKILL.md (new sections — Source Extraction pre-step, IG hook-format ranking, character-count gate — well beyond typo-class) via direct Write without re-routing through /prompt-engineer for the substantive-edit specialist regeneration that /alembiq:cc-skill-management's editing process requires. Soft-reminder fired again, post-Write again, after the edit had already landed on disk.

Pattern, novel relative to instance 3: the rationalization layer was "the cascade is the procedural wrapper; the specialist skill bodies are already in context; re-routing would be ceremony." The failure shape that follows is per-action gate-skipping rationalized as session-cleared workflow trust — same root as instance 3 but reached via a different surface argument.

Significance: this is the second documented case (after instance 3) of the soft-reminder failing to close the gap, and the FIRST documented case of the soft reminder failing twice in a single cascade. Strengthens the structural conclusion that the hard-gate (w039 + zmhy) is what's needed; the soft reminder is structurally insufficient under cascade-style workflows where the parent agent perceives itself as already inside the specialist's behavior umbrella.

Replay: agenc session print <current> --all
---

Fifth instance — same pattern, parallel-batch slip-through documented for the first time (AgenC mission 6baa4bfb-ef45-4918-a275-28c74c067c96, session 8a3ce3e1-c9fc-469f-aacf-3a3c4ac1683d, 2026-06-15 carousel-lessons extraction session):

Agent dispatched four parallel research subagents at task-start (did invoke skills appropriately for the research phase), then transitioned into propose → execute multiple turns later for SKILL.md edits and skipped the skill check on the phase transition. Sent six SKILL.md Edit calls in parallel without invoking /alembiq:cc-skill-management. The soft-reminder PreToolUse hook fired on each call, but PreToolUse reminders surface AFTER a parallel batch completes — by which time all six edits had landed on disk. Kevin asked "so you skipped cc-skill-management and prompt-engineer for writing these?" and reverted the conversation.

Five-whys (in-session, tree form) identified three independent bedrock leaves:
1. Skill-First Reach rule was applied at outer task-start only, not at the research → propose → execute phase transition. Agent treated "task start" as the outermost conversation turn rather than each phase boundary.
2. "I had stale model of /cc-skill-management content in memory and treated that as equivalent to invoking the skill." Direct violation of CLAUDE.mds "Skills evolve. Read current version" Red Flag, with no automation to catch.
3. Parallel batching defeats reminder-tier hooks structurally: PreToolUse reminders arrive after the entire batch has executed; reminder-tier hooks cannot interrupt parallel batches mid-stream.

Significance: this is the FIRST documented case where the failure was the parallel-batch slip-through itself. Instances 3 and 4 documented reminder-fires-but-agent-rationalizes; this instance is reminder-cannot-fire-in-time. Strengthens the conclusion that the enforcement-tier (w039 + zmhy) is mechanically required — there is no reminder-tier configuration that closes parallel-batch.

Architecture proposal from a follow-on structural-fix session (AgenC mission 8ba07ca2-0a5b-4e35-a7c4-d646df8466d5, session 1de0f9ac, 2026-06-15):

Two-hook design that should compose w039 (block when skill not invoked) with zmhy (track per-mission skill invocations):

1. PreToolUse hook on the Skill tool — when skill name matches the cc-configuration cluster (cc-configuration umbrella, cc-skill-management, cc-global-instructions-management, cc-rules, cc-settings-editing, cc-mcp-editing — with or without the alembiq: prefix), drop a per-surface session-scoped marker (file in $TMPDIR keyed on session_id × surface). cc-configuration as umbrella unlocks ALL surfaces; sub-skills unlock their specific surface.

2. PreToolUse hook on Edit/Write to cc-config surfaces — check for the corresponding marker. Above threshold + no marker → BLOCK. Below threshold (typo-class single-field, single-bullet, single-line) → existing reminder-only behavior. Marker present → silent pass-through.

Diff-size threshold: net-added lines > 3 in new_string (or total lines > 3 in content for Write). Below threshold honors the typo-class escape hatch baked into the cc-* skills themselves; above threshold requires the workflow.

The marker approach handles the cases the reminder hook cannot: parallel batches (all calls in the batch get blocked synchronously since they each independently check the marker), subagent edits inheriting parent session_id (marker drops at parent invocation, subagent edits pass through), and stale-skill-content-from-memory (marker requires a real Skill() call, not a Read of the SKILL.md file).

- cc-skill-management → SKILL.md, design.md
- cc-global-instructions-management → CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.design.md
- cc-rules → .claude/rules/
- cc-settings-editing → settings.json, .claude/hooks/
- cc-mcp-editing → .mcp.json
- cc-configuration → all of the above

- Fix C: tightened CLAUDE.md Skill-First Reach to explicitly cover phase transitions within a multi-phase task. Shipped to personal dotfiles. CLAUDE.design.md provenance added.

Neither B nor C closes the parallel-batch case — that remains w039+zmhy work.

title: Wrapper should source user shell rc to pick up bashrc PATH changes without tmux restart
description:
The AgenC wrapper inherits its environment from the long-running tmux server. When a user adds something to `~/.bashrc` (e.g., a new directory to PATH), tmux's process env doesn't pick up the change — and every wrapper subsequently spawned (including via `mission reload`) inherits that stale env. Claude then has a stale PATH, and its shell-snapshot captures the stale PATH, so even the Bash tool can't find binaries the user has on their interactive shell PATH.

**Symptom:** A binary newly added to `~/.bashrc`'s PATH_ADDITIONS (e.g., Composio CLI at `~/.composio/composio`) is not on PATH inside Claude, even though `which composio` works in any fresh terminal the user opens. `mission reload` does not fix it — the new wrapper still inherits stale env from tmux.

**Root cause chain:**

```
tmux server (PID, started long ago — frozen process env)
  └─ wrapper (fresh on reload, but inherits stale PATH from tmux server)
      └─ Claude (fresh, inherits stale PATH from wrapper)
          └─ snapshot generator dumps current PATH → captures stale PATH
              └─ Bash tool sources snapshot → sees stale PATH
```

**Why simple tmux fixes don't work:**

- `tmux set-environment -g PATH ...` propagates *some* variables to new panes but does NOT override PATH for spawned children (verified empirically: arbitrary new vars like `COMPOSIO_TEST_VAR` propagate fine, but PATH and TERM are special-cased — tmux's pane-creation code uses the server's process PATH).
- `tmux kill-server` would work but kills every running mission simultaneously — too disruptive.
- `lldb -p <tmux-pid>` injection of `setenv()` works but is high-risk (tmux crash takes down all missions) and not durable.

**Proposed fix:** Have the wrapper source the user's shell rc file before exec'ing Claude.

Wherever the wrapper currently does the equivalent of `exec.Command("claude", args...)`, replace with one of:

```go
// Option A: shell-out
cmd := exec.Command("bash", "-c",
    "source ~/.bashrc 2>/dev/null; exec \"$0\" \"$@\"",
    "claude", args...)
cmd.Env = wrapperEnv  // preserve CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, AGENC_MISSION_UUID, etc.

// Option B: in-process env capture
out, _ := exec.Command("bash", "-c", "source ~/.bashrc 2>/dev/null; printf '%s' \"$PATH\"").Output()
env := overrideEnvVar(os.Environ(), "PATH", string(out))
// exec claude with merged env
```

**Why this fixes it:**

The user's `~/.bashrc` rebuilds PATH from `PATH_ADDITIONS[]` every time it's sourced — so a fresh source captures whatever is currently in the file, regardless of tmux server age. Claude inherits the fresh PATH; the snapshot generator captures it; Bash tool sees it.

**Caveats to consider during implementation:**

1. **Shell detection.** Not every user is bash. Detect `$SHELL` or check which rc file exists (`.zshrc`, `.bashrc`, `.config/fish/config.fish`).
2. **Non-interactive source side effects.** Some users' rc files early-return for non-interactive shells (common pattern: `case $- in *i*) ;; *) return;; esac` at the top). That would defeat the fix. Mitigation: invoke with `-l` (login) instead of relying on `-i`, since rc-source plus login flag is more reliable.
3. **Cost.** Sourcing rc adds ~50-200ms to mission startup/reload. Probably worth it.
4. **Alternative API surface:** instead of sourcing the full user rc, expose `~/.agenc/env-refresh.sh` that the wrapper sources — users opt in to what gets refreshed. Less invasive but adds config surface.

**Where in the AgenC codebase:** the `mission resume --run-wrapper` code path. Process tree from the live session confirms `agenc mission resume --run-wrapper <mission-id> --prompt ...` is the exec'd command. The fix should land in whatever spawns Claude from that path.

**Provenance:** designed in AgenC mission `de11711b-e912-4455-a3a5-592b803354e6`, session `80f9bff1-02e6-4c3a-8f81-f33faee978f0`. Run `agenc session print 80f9bff1-02e6-4c3a-8f81-f33faee978f0 --all` for the full debugging trace — includes the empirical evidence chain that ruled out simpler tmux-only fixes.

title: Sharpen tmux-session-resolution error when socket is unreachable
description:
## Problem
When a caller runs a tmux-dependent command (e.g., `agenc mission detach`) from inside a tmux session where the tmux socket is unreachable (sandbox restriction, permissions error, dead tmux server), they see a misleading error:

> mission detach requires tmux; run inside a tmux session

The caller IS inside a tmux session ($TMUX is set) — the real failure is that `tmux display-message` can't reach `/private/tmp/tmux-501/default` (`Operation not permitted`). The error sends users in the wrong direction ("go run it outside the mission") instead of the right direction ("disable sandbox / fix tmux socket access").

## Repro
Run `agenc mission detach $AGENC_MISSION_UUID` from inside an AgenC mission with the default sandbox enabled. You'll see the misleading error. Re-run with sandbox disabled and it works.

Real-world hit: mission 16c5969a-5020-4bd4-876b-d43e7039570d — agent spent multiple turns thinking it couldn't self-detach.

## Root cause
`cmd/mission_helpers.go:getCurrentTmuxSessionName()` swallows the tmux error and returns empty string. Callers like `runMissionDetach` (cmd/mission_detach.go:41) then produce the generic 'requires tmux; run inside a tmux session' error — which is wrong when $TMUX was set the whole time.

```go
func getCurrentTmuxSessionName() string {
    if os.Getenv("TMUX") == "" {
        return ""
    }
    out, err := exec.Command("tmux", "display-message", "-p", "#{session_name}").Output()
    if err != nil {
        return ""  // <-- error info lost; caller can't distinguish 'not in tmux' from 'socket blocked'
    }
    return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
}
```

## Proposed fix
Make `getCurrentTmuxSessionName` (and the wrapper `getCallingSessionName`) return `(string, error)` so callers can distinguish:
- **No tmux at all** ($TMUX unset, AGENC_CALLING_SESSION_NAME unset) → 'run inside a tmux session'
- **Tmux env set but socket unreachable** → surface the actual socket error (`couldn't reach tmux server: <underlying err>`)

Update callers (`runMissionDetach`, `runMissionAttach`, and any other consumers — grep for `getCallingSessionName` and `getCurrentTmuxSessionName`) to produce appropriate error messages.

## Acceptance criteria
- Running a tmux-dependent command from inside tmux but with the tmux socket blocked produces an error that names the socket-access failure (not 'run inside a tmux session')
- Running outside tmux entirely still produces 'run inside a tmux session'
- E2E coverage for the two failure modes in scripts/e2e-test.sh (where feasible — the socket-blocked path may need a unit test against a fake exec instead)

## Files to touch
- cmd/mission_helpers.go (getCurrentTmuxSessionName, getCallingSessionName signatures)
- cmd/mission_detach.go (error message)
- cmd/mission_attach.go and any other callers (grep first)

title: Allow missions to detach themselves from user's tmux session
description:
Currently `mission detach` must be run from inside a tmux session, which prevents a mission from detaching itself — the mission's Claude process is not running inside the user's tmux session, so it has no $TMUX context.

## Repro
In mission 16c5969a-5020-4bd4-876b-d43e7039570d, Kevin tried to have the mission detach itself from his tmux session. It failed because `mission detach` requires $TMUX to be set.

## Why this matters
Missions can already manipulate the user's tmux workspace in other ways (e.g., `mission attach` foregrounds a mission window). `mission detach` is the symmetric operation but currently can't be triggered by a mission itself.

## Proposed direction
This likely needs a notion of a **workspace** and tracking **which workspace the user is currently focused in**, so missions can manipulate the workspace (attach/detach/etc.) without needing to be inside it themselves. This mirrors how `mission attach` already works — the server resolves the target workspace from server-side state, not from the caller's $TMUX env.

Concretely: the server should know which tmux session(s) the user has open and which one is 'active' (most recently attached / focused), so any mission can issue 'detach me from the user's current workspace' and the server resolves the target.

## Acceptance criteria
- A mission running outside the user's tmux session can successfully detach itself (or any mission) from the user's currently-focused tmux workspace
- `mission detach` no longer requires $TMUX to be set in the caller's environment when a server-side workspace concept can resolve the target
close_reason: Premise was wrong. `mission detach` already works from inside a mission — the failure in mission 16c5969a was a misleading error caused by the default sandbox blocking the tmux socket (/private/tmp/tmux-501/default). With sandbox disabled, the call succeeded. No workspace abstraction needed; the real follow-up is sharpening the diagnostic error message in mission_helpers.go's getCallingSessionName fallback.

title: Sandbox blocks AgenC Unix socket despite allowlist entry
description:
Inside a sandboxed Claude Code mission, an `agenc` CLI invocation failed to connect to the local server's Unix socket even though the sandbox config (as visible to the agent in its system prompt) explicitly lists the socket path in `allowUnixSockets`.

## Symptoms

From inside mission 62f124ce-24b4-4047-8957-7b1b83ee559a (Kevin's session 2026-05-11), agent ran:

```
agenc mission new mieubrisse/alembiq --prompt "..."
```

Result: `dial unix /Users/odyssey/.agenc/server/server.sock: connect: no such file or directory`

Sandbox config (from the agent's system prompt) included:
```
"allowUnixSockets":["/Users/odyssey/.agenc/server/server.sock"]
```

Subsequent sandboxed `/bin/ls /Users/odyssey/.agenc/server/` did not list `server.sock` in the directory — only `requests.log`, `server.lock`, `server.log`.

After re-running the same `agenc mission new` with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`, the call succeeded and spawned mission 3c6cf712. A subsequent `/bin/ls -la` on the socket path showed it present.

Kevin confirmed out-of-band: the server was up the entire time. The socket existed on disk continuously.

## Suspected behavior

The sandbox appears to either:
1. Hide the socket file from `readdir`/`stat` even when the path is in `allowUnixSockets` — i.e., directory listings don't see it even though `connect()` is supposed to be allowed.
2. Block `connect()` to the socket despite the allowlist entry.

The combination of (1)+(2) is the most consistent with what was observed (both the connect failure and the missing-from-`ls` result).

## Repro

1. Confirm AgenC server is running and socket exists: `ls /Users/odyssey/.agenc/server/server.sock`.
2. From a sandboxed Claude Code mission whose sandbox config includes that socket path in `allowUnixSockets`, run:
   - `ls /Users/odyssey/.agenc/server/`
   - `agenc mission ls`
3. Compare against same commands with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true`.

## Why this matters

Agents inside missions need to be able to spawn child missions and use `agenc` CLI generally. Today this requires `dangerouslyDisableSandbox`, which is both noisy (extra permission prompts) and overbroad (disables the sandbox for the entire invocation, not just the socket access).

If the design intent is that sandboxed agents SHOULD be able to reach the AgenC server (the allowlist entry suggests yes), then the sandbox enforcement is buggy.

If the design intent is that sandboxed agents should NOT be able to reach AgenC (loops, recursion concerns), then the allowlist entry is misleading and should be removed, and `agenc` CLI calls from inside missions should be explicitly documented as requiring unsandboxed execution.

Either way: align the allowlist behavior with the design intent.

## Provenance

- Caller mission: 62f124ce-24b4-4047-8957-7b1b83ee559a (Kevin's session 2026-05-11)
- Spawned child mission: 3c6cf712 (mieubrisse/alembiq)
- Session: fc6413aa

title: Add standardized field types with built-in parsing (RepoRef, Path, etc.)
description:
## Context

Several CLI commands take the same kinds of arguments — repo references, absolute paths, repo names — but each command has to remember the right parsing function. We just hit this with `agenc repo writeable-copy set`: the original code called `config.IsCanonicalRepoName`, which rejected shorthand `owner/repo` even though `agenc repo add` accepts it via `mission.ParseRepoReference`. The two commands diverged silently because there's no type-level enforcement that all repo args go through the same parser.

This is the same problem Kurtosis solved with its standardized field-type system: each domain field (PortSpec, ServiceID, FilesArtifactID, etc.) had a single type with a single canonical parser, and any code accepting that field had to use the type, which in turn forced every input through the standard parser.

## Proposal

Define standardized field types in a shared package (e.g. `internal/fields`) for the recurring argument shapes. Each type wraps a parsed value plus its original input and exposes:

- `Parse(input string) (FieldType, error)` — single canonical entry point
- Zero direct construction (private constructor + `Parse` factory) so callers cannot bypass parsing
- Display methods for round-tripping back to user-facing form

Initial candidates from existing code:

- **RepoRef** — wraps the canonical `github.com/owner/repo` name plus the originally-typed form. Backed by `mission.ParseRepoReference`. Replaces the ad-hoc `IsCanonicalRepoName` checks scattered through CLI commands.
- **AbsolutePath** — absolute, symlink-resolved, validated path. Replaces the manual expand-tilde + filepath.Abs + sanity-check sequence repeated in `config.ValidateWriteableCopyPath`, sleep-window-related code, and others.
- **MissionID** / **SessionID** / **NotificationID** — wraps a full UUID. Knows how to resolve from a short prefix via the appropriate DB lookup. Replaces the scattered short-ID logic.
- **CronSchedule** — wraps a validated 5- or 6-field cron expression.

## Why this matters

We just shipped a bug where one new CLI command rejected a perfectly valid shorthand only because the dev (me) used the wrong parser. With type-enforced fields, that mistake becomes impossible: `runRepoWriteableCopySet` would take a `fields.RepoRef` parameter and Cobra's RunE wrapper would do the parsing once, in one place. Future commands inherit the standard.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `internal/fields` package exists with at least RepoRef, AbsolutePath, and one ID type
- [ ] At least two existing CLI commands migrated to use the new fields, demonstrating the pattern
- [ ] Each field has a focused unit test covering valid + invalid inputs
- [ ] A README or doc in the package explains how to add a new field

## References

- Kurtosis design: ask Kevin for context (he ran into this in 2020-2024)
- Currently divergent: `cmd/repo_writeable_copy_set.go` (now uses ParseRepoReference) vs. the ad-hoc `IsCanonicalRepoName` checks elsewhere
- Path validation duplication: compare `internal/config/writeable_copy_path.go` to other path-handling code

title: Include 'this prompt comes from mission $UUID' header when missions spawn missions
Per-mission scoping for the AgenC unix socket — replace flat trust boundary with scoped API tokens
description:
# Per-mission scoping for the AgenC unix socket

## The problem

`~/.agenc/server/server.sock` is currently a **flat trust boundary**. Any mission with access to the socket can call any AgenC API on any other mission. In a Claude Code mission whose sandbox allows `Write(~/.agenc/server/server.sock)` (the default for missions today), that translates into:

- `agenc mission new <any-repo> --prompt '...'` — spawn arbitrary new missions in any repo the user has registered.
- `agenc mission send-keys <other-mission-id> "..."` — type into any other live mission's tmux pane. RCE-equivalent against other agents.
- `agenc mission print <other-mission-id>` — dump the full transcript of any other mission. High-value exfil channel because users concentrate sensitive content in dedicated missions (coaching journals, personal journal work, secrets discussed with specialized agents).
- `agenc session print <other-session-id>` — same, at session granularity.
- `agenc mission inspect <other-mission-id>` — discover other missions and their state.

Combined with Claude Code's `defaultMode: auto` (commands not in deny/ask are auto-allowed if sandboxable), and combined with the broader github.com / `*.vercel.com` / `*.posthog.com` exfil channels already in the network allowlist, a prompt-injected or compromised-dependency-laced agent in mission A can read mission B's transcript and exfil the contents to attacker infrastructure without ever prompting the user.

The current settings.json mitigation — moving `agenc mission new`, `mission send-keys`, `mission print`, `session print` to `ask` — closes the silent-action path but keeps the underlying API surface flat. Every cross-mission action becomes a prompt, which is the wrong primitive: the user shouldn't be approving cross-mission reads/writes one at a time, they should be configuring scopes once.

## Proposed direction

Replace the flat unix socket with a **per-mission scoped API surface**. Sketch:

1. When AgenC spawns a mission, it issues that mission an API token (or unix-socket-credential equivalent) bound to:
   - The mission's own UUID.
   - A scope set defaulting to "self only": the mission can read its own state, print its own sessions, and that's it.
2. Operations against other missions (`mission new`, `mission send-keys <other>`, `mission print <other>`, `session print <other>`, `mission inspect <other>`) require an explicitly broader scope.
3. Orchestrator-style missions (the user's "spawn another mission to do X" pattern) opt into the broader scope at spawn time — `agenc mission new --scope=orchestrator` or similar — and that gets surfaced clearly to the user when they launch one.
4. The existing CLAUDE.md guidance ("you can spawn missions to delegate work in other repos") still works for orchestrator missions; everything else gets the safer default.

This isn't a sandbox-permission problem and Claude Code can't fix it. The unix socket is one entry point; the right place to enforce mission identity and scope is on the AgenC server side.

## Why this matters now

Two recent threads pushed this up the priority list:
1. Sandbox conversation around `enableWeakerNetworkIsolation` in Claude Code — concluded that the trustd OCSP exfil channel is *much* narrower than channels the user has already accepted, including the AgenC socket. Flagging the bigger gap is the higher-leverage move.
2. `~/.claude/settings.json` was just tightened (`agenc mission new`, `mission print`, `session print`, `mission send-keys` → `ask`) as a stopgap. That works for one user with attentive prompts, but the user has been wanting per-mission scoping for a while and the ask-prompt UX won't scale.

## Out of scope for this bead

- Stronger network isolation (Anthropic's job — Claude Code TLS-terminating proxy).
- Sandbox profile changes (Claude Code's job).
- Specific token format / crypto choices — those belong in a follow-up design bead once direction is agreed.

## Provenance

Designed in AgenC mission `8d3afa33-5bd2-4cf4-9dbc-cd9a28df7e79`, session `0982938e`. Run `agenc session print 0982938e` for the full sandbox-security thread that produced this.
close_reason: Duplicate of agenc-415l.

title: bd dolt stop falsely reports server not running in shared-server mode
description:
When run from a repo configured for shared-server mode (`dolt: shared-server: true` in .beads/config.yaml), `bd dolt stop` fails with "Error: dolt server is not running" — even when the shared server is actually running.

## Reproduction

1. From a repo with shared-server mode enabled (e.g. agent-factory, where `.beads/config.yaml` has `dolt: shared-server: true`), confirm the shared server is up:
   ```
   lsof -i :3308
   # => dolt PID listening on port 3308
   ```
2. Run:
   ```
   bd dolt stop
   ```
3. Observe: `Error: dolt server is not running` (exit 1), even though the shared dolt process is alive and bd commands like `bd list` work fine against it.

## Expected

`bd dolt stop` should detect that this repo uses the shared server (`~/.beads/shared-server/`), find the running shared dolt process (port 3308), and stop it.

## Likely cause

The `stop` command is probably looking for a *per-repo* dolt process (e.g. via a PID file in the local `.beads/`) and failing to fall through to the shared-server detection path that other commands like `bd list` and `bd dolt show` use.

## Impact

Blocks the standard rename-DB workflow from inside a repo. Forces users to either kill the shared server PID directly, or run the stop command from a different working directory where shared-server detection works.

## Environment

- bd version: 0.61.0 (from local_metadata)
- macOS, shared server at `~/.beads/shared-server/` on port 3308
- Repo: agent-factory (`.beads/config.yaml` shared-server: true)
