title: Support no-Git-repo missions with filesystem directory as agent workspace
description: Enable AgenC missions that target a plain filesystem directory rather than a Git repository. This supports GitHub-oriented workflows (e.g., issue triage, PR review, project management) where the agent doesn't need a repo clone — just a working directory on the filesystem. The mission's agent directory would point to an existing directory instead of cloning a repo.

title: Sleep mode: block mission and cron creation during configured sleep windows
description: Add a sleep mode feature to AgenC that blocks non-cron mission creation and cron creation during configured time windows. Encourages the user to stop working and go to sleep. Config in config.yml with day-of-week and HH:MM time windows (matching YappBlocker's schedule format). Server-side sleepGuard middleware returns 403 with friendly message. Cron-triggered missions are exempt. No escape hatch.
close_reason: Closed

title: Refactor cron CLI commands to use server CRUD endpoints
description:
Currently all cron mutation commands (config cron add, config cron update, config cron rm, cron enable, cron disable) write directly to config.yml from the CLI. Refactor these to go through server HTTP endpoints so that all mutations flow through the server.

Endpoints to add: POST /crons (create), PATCH /crons/{name} (update, enable, disable), DELETE /crons/{name} (remove). Server handlers should acquire the config lock, read/modify/write config.yml, and update cachedConfig — follow the same pattern as the sleep window endpoints in internal/server/handle_sleep.go. CLI commands become thin HTTP clients calling serverClient().

Read-only commands (cron ls, cron logs, cron history) already go through the server or read config directly — migrate these too if they read config directly.

After this lands, wrap POST /crons with the sleepGuard middleware (tracked as agenc-4ebm).
close_reason: Closed

title: Teach all AgenC missions about repo library read access
description: Update the AgenC CLAUDE.md (or per-mission instructions) to document that all missions have read access to the repo library at ~/.agenc/repos/. Explain what the repo library is (managed collection of registered git repos), how to list available repos (agenc repo ls), and how to read files from them using Read/Glob/Grep tools directly against repo library paths — without needing to spawn a new mission.

title: Teach Adjutant to file beads for arbitrary repos
description: Give the Adjutant agent access to beads (bd CLI) and teach it how to create/manage beads in any repo by using BEADS_DIR pointed at the repo library. This enables the Adjutant to file issues against any registered repo without needing to be inside that repo.

title: Opus 1M context window option missing in AgenC missions
description: When running /model in a regular Claude Code session (e.g. in /tmp), the Opus 1M option is available. But in AgenC missions, /model only shows Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus — no 1M variant. Need to investigate what AgenC configuration is preventing the extended context option from appearing.
close_reason: Removed defaultModel: opus from AgenC config.yml — it was passing --model opus to Claude Code, overriding the opus[1m] setting in settings.json and hiding the 1M context option from /model

title: Add E2E test suite using agenc-test
description: Create an automated test suite that exercises the actual binary via the test-env. A TestE2E test or make e2e target that boots the test-env, runs common workflows (mission ls, repo ls, server start/stop), and verifies output. The test-env infrastructure exists but has no automated suite exercising it. Catches integration-level regressions that unit tests miss.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add go mod tidy check to make check
description: Add 'go mod tidy' followed by 'git diff --exit-code go.mod go.sum' to make check. Agents sometimes add dependencies without tidying, or remove code without removing the dependency. This catches stale module state structurally.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add deadcode analysis to make check
description: Add golang.org/x/tools/cmd/deadcode to the make check pipeline. The unused linter catches unexported dead code, but deadcode uses whole-program analysis to catch exported-but-unreachable code too. Agents frequently add functions 'for later' and never use them.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add architecture doc staleness check to pre-commit
description: Add a pre-commit check that detects new/removed/renamed packages under internal/ and verifies docs/system-architecture.md was also modified in the same commit. Currently enforced only by convention in CLAUDE.md, which agents ignore under pressure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Pin golangci-lint version in CI
description: CI currently installs golangci-lint@latest. A new lint release could silently change what passes. Pin to a specific version (e.g., v1.64.1) in .github/workflows/ci.yml and update deliberately.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add govulncheck to make check
description: Add govulncheck to the make check pipeline to catch known CVEs in dependencies. Agents use latest versions by convention but don't verify vulnerabilities. One line in the Makefile catches known issues structurally.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add test coverage threshold to make check
description: Add go test -coverprofile and a script/check that fails below a per-package coverage threshold (start at 60%, ratchet up over time). Currently an agent can add a new package with zero tests and the build passes. This structurally forces agents to write tests.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add -race flag to go test in Makefile
description: Add the -race flag to the go test invocation in make check. This catches data races in concurrent code (server goroutines, tmux, file watchers) that agents routinely introduce without realizing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Unify cron next-run calculation to a single code path
description: GetNextCronRun (agenc_config.go:1075) uses the gronx library while actual scheduling uses the hand-rolled ParseCronExpression -> launchd StartCalendarInterval path. These two parsers could disagree on edge cases. Consolidate to a single code path so display and scheduling always agree. Either derive next-run from the CalendarInterval that launchd actually uses, or validate that gronx and ParseCronExpression produce equivalent results for all accepted expressions.
close_reason: Removed GetNextCronRun, NextRunFromCalendarInterval, and all next-run display code from cron ls/new/enable/config-cron-add. Removed gronx dependency.

title: Add file locking to config.yml read-modify-write operations
description: CLI commands (enable, disable, add, rm, update) all perform read-modify-write on config.yml without file locking. Two concurrent CLI invocations can race and one write is lost. Solution: add flock-based file locking around config read-modify-write cycles. This is simpler than routing all mutations through the server and works without the server running.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add fallback recovery when unload fails during cron plist reload
description: In cron_syncer.go syncCronJob, when content changes and the job is loaded, UnloadPlist failure is logged but execution continues to LoadPlist. If the job is still loaded (because unload failed), launchctl load will reject the duplicate, and the error IS returned — leaving the cron broken with new plist on disk but old schedule in launchd. Fix: if UnloadPlist fails, try RemoveJobByLabel as a fallback before attempting LoadPlist.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add missing cron syncer test coverage
description: Missing tests for: disabled crons (unload path), no-ID skip path, error paths (LoadPlist/UnloadPlist failures), removeUnmatchedPlists/orphan removal, concurrent sync safety, plist with no StartCalendarInterval, Sunday normalization (weekday 7→0), sanitized name collisions, RemovePlist, ListAgencCronJobs parsing.
close_reason: Added tests for disabled crons (unload path + not-loaded noop), launchd orphan detection (removes orphan UUIDs and legacy labels, preserves known). Also added plutil validation test and ptrToString fix in earlier commits.

title: Add sync.Mutex to CronSyncer to prevent concurrent syncs
description: SyncCronsToLaunchd is called from startup (sync) and fsnotify callbacks (goroutine). Two rapid config changes >500ms apart can produce concurrent syncs racing on the same plist files and launchctl calls.
close_reason: Added sync.Mutex to CronSyncer, locked at top of SyncCronsToLaunchd

title: Add launchd-side orphan detection to cron syncer
description: reconcileOrphanedPlists only scans filesystem for plist files. If a plist is deleted while the job is loaded in launchd, the phantom job persists forever. Use ListAgencCronJobs + RemoveJobByLabel to catch loaded jobs with no corresponding config entry.
close_reason: Added removeOrphanedLaunchdJobs that calls ListAgencCronJobs and RemoveJobByLabel to catch phantom loaded jobs with no config entry

title: Use AGENC_DIRPATH-based prefix for generated plist files to isolate test environments
description:
When generating launchd plist files, use a prefix derived from AGENC_DIRPATH to prevent collisions between the main AgenC installation and per-agent test environments.

**Rules:**
- If AGENC_DIRPATH is empty (default): prefix plist filenames with 'agenc.'
- If AGENC_DIRPATH is set: prefix plist filenames with 'agenc-HASH.' where HASH is the SHA hash of the absolute resolved path of AGENC_DIRPATH

This allows agents running their own pocket AgenC environment (with a custom AGENC_DIRPATH) to register launchd services without colliding with the main system's plist files or each other's.
close_reason: Plist prefix now derived dynamically from AGENC_DIRPATH via config.GetCronPlistPrefix()

title: Fix unchecked fsnotify.Watcher.Add error
description: The errcheck exclusion for fsnotify.Watcher.Add hides a bug in the addWatch() helper function in internal/server/config_watcher.go lines 192-194. This function silently ignores errors, meaning if watcher.Add() fails due to permissions, config changes won't be detected. Most other callsites (config_watcher.go:64, wrapper.go:549, credential_sync.go:158) already check the error properly. Fix: remove the addWatch() helper and check errors at the callsite, or have addWatch() return the error. Remove Watcher.Add from errcheck exclusions.
close_reason: Removed blanket Watcher.Add errcheck exclusion. addWatch() helper now uses explicit _ = with comment explaining intentional ignore during recursive walks. All other callsites already check errors.

title: Fix unchecked exec.Cmd.Run/Wait and os.Process.Kill errors
description: The errcheck exclusions for exec.Cmd.Run, exec.Cmd.Wait, and os.Process.Kill are too broad. Exit codes matter in several contexts: tmux state changes (wrapper/tmux.go), process lifecycle (server/pool.go). Some callsites already check the error despite the exclusion being active. Remove these from errcheck exclusions and add proper error handling where exit codes matter. For genuinely fire-and-forget contexts (e.g., best-effort tmux display updates), use explicit _ = assignment.
close_reason: Removed exec.Cmd.Run, exec.Cmd.Wait, os.Process.Kill from errcheck exclusions. All 11 flagged instances were genuinely fire-and-forget (tmux cleanup, test teardown) — added explicit _ = assignments.

title: Fix unchecked os.Rename errors in log rotation
description: The errcheck exclusion for os.Rename hides silent log rotation failures. In internal/wrapper/wrapper.go lines 844 and 848, os.Rename is used for log rotation without error checking. If rotation fails, logs never rotate and disk usage grows unbounded. Remove os.Rename from errcheck exclusions and log rotation failures at the callsite (don't need to return error — just log it).
close_reason: Added error logging to log rotation os.Rename calls in wrapper.go. Removed blanket os.Rename errcheck exclusion. All other callsites already checked errors.

title: Fix unchecked os.Remove/os.RemoveAll errors
description: The errcheck exclusions for os.Remove and os.RemoveAll are hiding real bugs. Critical instances: (1) wrapper/socket.go lines 65, 80, 99 — if socket file removal fails, subsequent Listen() fails with 'address in use'. (2) claudeconfig/shadow.go line 379 — os.RemoveAll in loop silently fails on permission errors. (3) server/server.go lines 127, 199 — socket removal failure causes startup failure. Remove these from errcheck exclusions and add proper error handling at each callsite. Defer-cleanup contexts (cmd/mission_draft.go, test files) are acceptable — use explicit _ = assignment for those.

Tighten further after refactoring the worst offenders.

AgenC should detect the absence of .tmux.conf and set sane defaults programmatically (e.g. via tmux set-option) to ensure a consistent experience.

This lets the user mark up, annotate, or edit the response before sending it back — enabling a tighter feedback loop where the user can visually indicate what to change rather than describing it in text.

title: Eliminate package-level agencDirpath global in cmd package
description: The cmd package relies on a package-level 'agencDirpath' variable that gets magically set as a side effect of getAgencContext(). Different code paths may or may not call getAgencContext(), leading to bugs where agencDirpath is empty (e.g., the --run-wrapper code path in doRunWrapperDirect). The fix that papered over this just added another magic initializer. The proper fix is to refactor the cmd package so agencDirpath is resolved once at the entry point of each command and passed explicitly through the call chain as a function parameter, eliminating the global.
close_reason: Eliminated package-level agencDirpath global. 24 files changed: removed global from root.go, deleted getAgencContext(), made readConfig/readConfigWithComments/ensureServerRunning resolve path internally, all cmd/ callers use config.GetAgencDirpath() at point of use.

title: Self-contained test environment for agent e2e validation
description:
Allow agents working on the AgenC codebase to build, run, and test their own changes in a fully isolated pocket environment. See docs/plans/2026-03-24-test-env-design.md for the full design.

Key components:
1. Namespace resolver — system-global resources (tmux sessions, launchd plists) get a hash suffix derived from AGENC_DIRPATH
2. Wrapper script — _build/agenc-test sets AGENC_DIRPATH and AGENC_TEST_ENV=1, execs _build/agenc
3. make test-env / make test-env-clean — create and tear down the pocket environment at _test-env/
4. AGENC_TEST_ENV gating — features that conflict with global state (tmux keybinding injection) return errors in test environments
5. _build/ for binaries, _test-env/ for runtime state — independent lifecycles
close_reason: Implemented namespace isolation (tmux sessions, launchd plists), AGENC_TEST_ENV gating, wrapper script, make targets, and CLAUDE.md docs

title: Give agents explicit instructions about repo library at $AGENC_DIRPATH/repos
description: Ensure agents have clear instructions (if they don't already) that the user's cloned repos live at $AGENC_DIRPATH/repos and agents can explore them as needed for reference. Check whether the prime content or CLAUDE.md already covers this; if not, add it.

title: Explore Supergateway for system-level MCP server caching
description:
Explore using Supergateway so that MCP servers don't need to be restarted upon each mission that uses them, and MCP servers instead get cached at the system level. This also addresses the persistent auth problem: MCP servers could be instantiated once at a system level, auth'd via 1Password secrets, and each mission just calls into the shared MCP server. The user would only need to auth to 1Password once, rather than re-authing for every mission.

Status (2026-05-13)
-------------------

Active design. Long-form design content lives in [`docs/plans/2026-05-13-mcp-gateway-design.md`](../docs/plans/2026-05-13-mcp-gateway-design.md) (in the AgenC repo). The 2026-03-18 landscape sweep at [`docs/plans/2026-03-18-supergateway-research.md`](../docs/plans/2026-03-18-supergateway-research.md) is still canonical for off-the-shelf comparison.

Headline decisions from the 2026-05-13 design pass:

- **Go-native MVP**, not wrap-sparfenyuk. AgenC owns the gateway.
- **stdio shim over Unix socket**, no exposed HTTP port. Mission `.mcp.json` gets `{"command": "agenc", "args": ["mcp", "client", "<name>"]}` entries that pipe to the daemon over the existing socket.
- **Per-backend mutex by default** (configurable). Needed for multi-subagent concurrency.
- **Daemon never holds plaintext secrets.** Each backend spawn uses `op run --` (or `op inject` for batches). `OP_CACHE=false` to dodge Tahoe TCC hang.
- **Daemon stays detached** (`Setsid: true` unchanged). Accept N Touch ID prompts at daemon startup.
- **Composio as hybrid partner** for the cloud-SaaS slice; AgenC gateway for the custom-local slice. Run both.

**Gating empirical question for Phase 0:** does `op run --` work from a `setsid`'d daemon (no controlling TTY), or does the design need a fallback to service-account-token? See the design doc for details.

Discussion provenance: mission `207a2561`, session `400f310e`. Run `agenc session print 400f310e --all` for the full conversation.

Related: `dotfiles-cnd` (Todoist MCP -> CLI, the per-server CLI alternative). The "MCPs as CLIs" future direction in the design doc subsumes this pattern at the gateway level.
notes:
Related tool to evaluate (2026-05-22): mcpc — https://github.com/apify/mcpc — universal CLI client for MCP with persistent sessions, stdio/HTTP, OAuth 2.1, tasks, JSON output for code mode, proxy for AI sandboxes, x402. Consider whether mcpc can serve as the cache interface layer Kevin wants, or if the Go-native MVP still wins. Cross-cuts the MCPs-as-CLIs direction (agenc-10mi). Note (2026-05-27): mcpc is an MCP *client*, not a process supervisor — useful later for the stdio shim consumer side, not for supervising server processes.

mcpc reference added by AgenC mission 1a66205e-687c-4d05-a15d-60756d3ebba7, session 24513d60-f155-4ae9-8aa3-1f62dbc09a1d (Todoist inbox processing, 2026-05-22). Run `agenc session print 24513d60-f155-4ae9-8aa3-1f62dbc09a1d --all` for context.

Validation evidence (2026-05-22): research mission confirmed Gas Town / Gas City do NOT solve the multi-Claude MCP auth-sharing problem. They orchestrate on top of Claude Code with worktree-based isolation for code, not auth state. The underlying bugs are Claude Code issues #43000 (clientId derived from ephemeral localhost callback port — each new instance stores its token under a different key) and #24317 (single-use refresh token race across concurrent sessions). Adopting Gastown alone would expose the bug harder at 20-30 parallel polecats. The agenc-tpde gateway direction (single supervised backend, shared auth via 1Password) is the correct structural fix. Discussion provenance: mission d4bda84b-a376-42fe-82c3-bfac4f48ea1e, session d70de552. Run `agenc session print d70de552 --all`.

Status update (2026-05-27): explored a HTTP-only pilot narrowing — supervise workspace-mcp under AgenC without the stdio multiplex / Unix-socket routing layer; defer that to a later phase. Scope shrinks to ~400-600 LOC vs the prior 1500-2500 LOC gateway estimate. Concrete pain evidence in mission 0779c7e6 (workspace-mcp standup): manual launcher script, manual tmux session, orphan PID holding port 8000 after `tmux kill-session` (alias was not used), manual ~/.claude.json mcpServers edit, manual settings.json sandbox allowlist for 127.0.0.1, upstream `WORKSPACE_MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0` LAN-exposure default caught only by an ad-hoc lsof check. All preventable by the pilot.

Library landscape finding (surprising gap): no clean drop-in Go library exists for embedded process supervision with logs / restart / health. Evaluated ochinchina/supervisord (Go port of Python supervisord — daemon-shaped, not library-shaped; importable `process.Manager` exists but its types assume standalone-daemon use), cirello.io/oversight (Erlang-tree style — supervises in-process goroutines, not OS processes), kontera-technologies/go-supervisor (library-shaped but barely more than os/exec with a restart loop). Honest assessment: stdlib `exec.Command` + `SysProcAttr.Setpgid: true` (kills the orphan-PID class via process group) + natefinch/lumberjack (log rotation) + cenkalti/backoff/v4 (restart loop) is less total code than the adapter for any heavyweight library. Heavy supervisord-as-subprocess (Arch B in the discussion) was rejected for adding a daemon-of-daemon-of-server layer.

Recommended Phase 1 architecture (Arch C in the discussion): thin supervisor on stdlib + lumberjack + backoff inside the existing AgenC daemon. Config schema is `managed_servers:` in ~/.agenc/config.yaml with map-key as the instance name (named instances fall out for free — `workspace-mcp-personal`, `workspace-mcp-work`). Port handling: per-server `port` key; AgenC sets `AGENC_SERVER_PORT` env var on the child *and* does simple `$VAR` substitution on command args (no template engine). Bind defaults to 127.0.0.1; refuse 0.0.0.0 unless explicit opt-in (closes the LAN-exposure default). Logs to ~/.agenc/servers/<name>/logs/ via lumberjack. CLI `agenc server { ls | status | url | logs | restart }`. Mission injection: at per-mission claude-config snapshot rebuild, AgenC writes `.mcp.json` entries pointing at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<url_path>` and appends 127.0.0.1 to settings.json `network.allowedHosts` — replaces Kevin's manual edits to global ~/.claude.json and global settings.json.

Explicitly OUT of Phase 1: stdio MCP backends, 1Password op:// integration (user supplies plain env values for now — keeps the Phase 0 op-from-setsid-daemon question off the critical path), per-mission scoping/permissions (all managed servers available to all missions for now; permission system is its own future project), on-demand startup (servers start when daemon starts), Composio integration.

Open questions before Phase 1 build: (a) .mcp.json injection scope — per-mission snapshot (cleaner; non-AgenC Claude sessions won't see managed servers) vs global ~/.claude.json (universal but pollutes outside AgenC); (b) auto-reload on config.yaml change vs explicit `agenc server restart`; (c) failure-to-start policy (refuse daemon startup vs log-and-continue vs retry-forever vs fail-after-N); (d) secrets — plain values in config.yaml for Phase 1, op:// integration deferred.

Status: deferred. Not slotted for active work right now — Kevin has other priorities. Discussion provenance: AgenC mission 6a1abcbc-e134-4d01-a45f-8f87a9c96014, session ad45c738. Run `agenc session print ad45c738 --all` for the full conversation.
Interim stopgap now in place (2026-08-24), to be absorbed when this ships.

Two MCP servers run as long-lived background processes in detached tmux sessions instead of being cold-started per mission, registered globally in ~/.claude.json as HTTP endpoints:
  - Google Workspace (taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp) — tmux 'gws-mcp', http://localhost:8000/mcp
  - Hevy (chrisdoc/hevy-mcp) — tmux 'hevy-mcp', http://localhost:8001/mcp

Brought up idempotently by ~/app/dotfiles/bash/utils/start-mcp-servers.sh (alias 'mcp-start'), which is table-driven — adding a server is one row plus a start-<name>-mcp.sh launcher. Each launcher execs 'op run' so secrets stay in process memory. One Touch ID prompt per server per boot.

What this stopgap deliberately lacks, and what the gateway should provide: no supervision or restart-on-crash, no health monitoring, no auto-start after reboot (Kevin runs 'mcp-start' by hand), no per-backend mutex, and an exposed loopback HTTP port rather than the Unix-socket shim this design calls for.

Migration note: when the gateway lands, delete start-mcp-servers.sh, the per-server launchers, and the 'mcp-start' alias from dotfiles, and remove the 'workspace-mcp' and 'hevy' entries from ~/.claude.json.

title: Adjutant-assisted work triage and prioritization
description:
Once AgenC has a work tracking system (agenc-181j), the Adjutant should help users triage and prioritize incoming work. The model is a 'work hopper' — tasks flow in from ambient capture (Siri voice notes, email, chat, agent-generated items) and accumulate in an inbox. The user then decides what gets 'let into the factory' (i.e., becomes a mission). The Adjutant's role: surface what's in the inbox, help the user prioritize based on urgency/impact/dependencies, suggest which items to greenlight into missions, and flag items that have been sitting too long. Omar's Siri inbox → Claude triage pipeline is an early example of this pattern. This is the 'CEO of an agent org' vision applied to work intake — the user makes strategic decisions about what to work on, agents handle execution.

Key concept: MIRN (Most Important Right Now). The Adjutant should help users identify from their global task list which tasks are the biggest levers — the most important ones to work on right now. The global task view is a necessary input to output a MIRN-prioritized view. This is linked to the /prioritization skill's MIRN concept.

[UPDATE 2026-03-18] May (non-technical PMM user, March 6 interview) independently validated this need from outside the technical ICP: 'I need to keep surfacing things to ask, is this worth prioritizing right now?' and 'I don't think all the things I'm doing right now are the RIGHT things to get me where I want to go.' Her core unmet need is prioritization, not execution. She wants to build a personal assistant ('April') that captures thoughts, categorizes them P0-P3, and sends reminders. This confirms the triage/prioritization need exists across both technical and non-technical users. Signal strength upgraded from SINGLE-SIGNAL to VALIDATED.

title: Pluggable task management interface (agenc task)
description: Expose an 'agenc task' interface that supports different backend implementations: Obsidian/Markdown (Omar), Markdown repo (Yannik), Todoist (Kevin). This is a potential product differentiator — baking GTD methodology into AgenC while letting users keep their preferred task storage. Key challenges: no easy dependency graph or queries with pure Markdown. Consider a background sync daemon that monitors Markdown files, keeps a DB for queries, injects UUIDs, and builds dependency graphs. Three users have independently expressed the need for structured task management inside agent workflows.
notes: [2026-05-13] Thinking evolved: AgenC should have its own task interface (e.g. 'agenc task'), even when backed by Beads (or another store). The leverage of owning the interface layer is AgenC-specific semantics — most importantly, every bead filed and every update made gets stamped with a mission UUID for provenance tracking. The interface layer is where AgenC-aware behaviors (mission attribution, cross-repo routing, etc.) become first-class. Source: Todoist inbox capture.

title: Green tab color when Claude is done, clears after user views

Both Omar and Yannik requested this. Requires building a polling loop to detect when the user is viewing a specific tmux pane, as tmux has no native hook for this. Orange remains reserved for permission requests.

title: Auto-retrospective on session close
description: When a Claude session closes (Ctrl+C, idle-kill, or explicit stop), automatically run a retrospective that analyzes the session for friction points and suggests improvements to CLAUDE.md, skills, or settings. Omar built /retrospective manually and explicitly requested this be automated. Related to agenc-317 (monitoring) and agenc-321 (summarization) but focused specifically on the close-time improvement extraction, not summarization.
notes:
## Re-surfaced 2026-05-27 weekly retrospective

A retrospective scan of 116 missions (2026-05-18 → 2026-05-25, mission d303ef1d-caaa-4003-9f14-577c8f4948d9) found that mega-mission context bloat without close-time summarization is a recurring failure mode.

Concrete evidence:
- Mission 9837c12c (Alembiq launch day): 4,621-line session juggling pack rebrand + V15 copy + 4 content pieces + infra fixes. Eventually required manual diff handoff and explicit child-mission spawn (d734187a) to continue. No future agent can economically `agenc mission print` this transcript.
- Mission 1eb3de61: 60+ minutes lost to git-history spelunking just to discover a parallel session had already completed the requested work. A queryable per-mission close-summary would have closed this in seconds.
- Mission 49fef4da: ended with five open beads as next-session work and no synthesizing summary linking them.

Closely related: agenc-gsu (handoff command: dump context and reload into fresh session), agenc-fq7 (session switcher with latest response summaries). All three feel like one feature.

Adjacent downstream Todoist project: "🧠 Add AgenC mission auto-summarization" (6ggG2JQhCJm75xHr).

title: Build skill sharing/distribution mechanism via Git
description: Build a mechanism for sharing and discovering skills via Git repositories. Users independently build skills that mirror each other's work — a sharing mechanism would eliminate redundant effort and create network effects.

title: Run missions in Docker containers for safe YOLO mode
description: Running missions inside Docker containers would allow full YOLO mode (unrestricted agent permissions) without risk to the host system. This eliminates the need for complex allow/deny permission lists and makes the trust model simpler: the container IS the sandbox.
notes:
Idea (2026-06-06): microsandbox (https://github.com/superradcompany/microsandbox) as a candidate microVM substrate for the Docker-container YOLO mode this bead proposes. Worth comparing against straight Docker before committing to a runtime.

Surfaced from HN 'Ask HN: What is your (AI) dev tech stack/workflow?' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48413629), jpeeler's comment weighs his current herde+Nono policy-based sandboxing setup against switching to microsandbox-based microVM isolation. He names the core tradeoff: the VM boundary lets you skip policy maintenance entirely, but you lose all installed tools inside the sandbox and have to either provision at runtime or pre-build an image matching your dev environment. Same tradeoff this bead's Docker approach will hit.

Provenance: /hacker-news-daily-pull cron run, AgenC mission 27c46618-4020-4c6b-9c5e-cf720d27a791.

title: Consider adding default allowed commands to settings.json for fresh Claude onboarding
description: New Claude users are bombarded with permission prompts for basic commands (git add, ls, touch, file, mkdir, etc.). Consider adding a set of safe default allowed commands to the AgenC-generated settings.json to reduce friction for people who are fresh-onboarding to both AgenC and Claude. This could be an opinionated default that users can override.

title: Add 'Claude Explained' documentation section for new Claude users
description:
Many AgenC users will be new to Claude Code. Add a documentation section covering:
- How Claude sessions work (context window, conversation history, session persistence)
- The settings.json permission prompt: what it means, how it works, how to configure it (link to agenc-tcoh for the claude-config situation)
- When to use CLAUDE.md vs skills: global CLAUDE.md (every mission gets this context, always), global skills (every mission has the option, loaded on demand), repo CLAUDE.md (every mission to that repo gets the context, always), repo skills (every mission to that repo has the option, loaded on demand). Omar was confused about this distinction.
- What the 'don't ask again' Claude permission prompt means in an AgenC context: it means the MISSION won't ask again, because settings.local.json is mission-specific and ephemeral

title: Research and implement a documentation site tool (Docusaurus, alternatives)
description: Evaluate documentation site generators: Docusaurus, Nextra, Mintlify, VitePress, MkDocs, Starlight, etc. Consider: ease of setup, Markdown support, search, versioning, custom theming, deployment (GitHub Pages vs Vercel vs Netlify), and fit with AgenC's brand.

title: Create a documentation website for AgenC
description: AgenC needs a dedicated documentation website beyond the README. The README is getting long and can't serve as both marketing landing page and comprehensive docs. A proper docs site would improve discoverability, allow structured navigation, and make AgenC more professional and approachable for new users.

title: Research requirements for building a native Mac app (a la Conductor)
description: Research what would be needed to create a Mac app for AgenC, similar to the Conductor app. Evaluate: Swift/AppKit vs Electron vs Tauri, terminal emulation libraries, tmux integration vs replacement, distribution (App Store vs direct download vs Homebrew cask), code signing requirements, and estimated engineering effort.

title: Build a GUI for AgenC
description:
tmux is the single biggest barrier to entry for new users. It adds unfamiliar hotkeys, a confusing server/session model, opaque status bars, and environment inheritance issues (see agenc-2ome for the PATH problem). Omar's onboarding session confirmed this — he'd never used screen/tmux before and the learning curve was steep.

A native GUI would:
- Lower the barrier to entry dramatically (just download and run)
- Allow better visual presentation (colors, tabs, Markdown rendering)
- Enable custom input syntax (e.g. # for mission ID tab-complete, @ to summon agents)
- Eliminate the tmux environment inheritance problem entirely
- Make the product more demo-friendly and visually compelling

This is a large investment but may be necessary to reach the ICP (technical but not tmux-native users).

title: Consider building prompt-engineer skill into AgenC as auto-generated per-mission skill
description: The prompt-engineer skill is so universally valuable that it may warrant being a built-in AgenC feature rather than something users must manually install. AgenC could auto-generate it with each mission, with a config flag to disable it for users who don't want it. Omar found this skill immediately valuable during onboarding.

title: Teach Adjutant what 'always synced' means
description: The Adjutant doesn't understand the --always-synced flag on repos. When Omar asked about it during onboarding, the Adjutant couldn't help. The Adjutant prompt should explain that --always-synced repos are automatically kept in sync with their remote — AgenC pulls the latest version before each mission launch, so the mission always gets fresh content. This is critical for config repos that are updated frequently.

title: Make Adjutant aware of the user's GitHub username
description: The Adjutant prompt should include the user's GitHub username so it can reference it in commands and suggestions. Currently the Adjutant doesn't know the username, which means it can't help with GitHub-related operations without asking.

title: Create starter .tmux.conf with recommended settings for new users
description: During onboarding, new users who have never used tmux are dropped into a raw tmux environment with no customization. AgenC should offer to create a .tmux.conf with recommended settings (status bar, sensible defaults, AgenC-friendly keybindings) if the user doesn't already have one. This lowers the tmux learning curve significantly.

title: Fix reconfig not preserving tab status / Claude status correspondence
description: After running 'Reconfig & Reload Mission', the tmux tab status indicator no longer corresponds to the Claude session status. The tab should reflect the actual Claude state after reconfig. Discovered during Omar's onboarding (journal: omar-agenc-user-onboarding~2026-03-10).

title: Fix 'reconfig & reload' printing garbage output
description: When a user runs the 'Reconfig & Reload Mission' palette command, it prints a bunch of garbage output that confuses users — they don't know what to do with it (ENTER doesn't work to dismiss). Discovered during Omar's onboarding (journal: omar-agenc-user-onboarding~2026-03-10). Related to agenc-vbvp (suppress mission stop tmux output).

description: When a mission is stopped, tmux prints output to the pane that is confusing for users. The user has to press q or enter to dismiss it. This output should be suppressed or handled gracefully so that the pane returns to a clean state automatically.

title: Fix GitHub cloning to use user's preferred auth method (SSH vs HTTPS)
description: During Omar's onboarding (journal: omar-agenc-user-onboarding~2026-03-10), cloning a GitHub config repo prompted for username/password instead of using the user's configured Git credential method (SSH keys, gh auth, etc.). AgenC should respect the user's existing Git authentication setup rather than falling back to basic auth.

title: Organize cmd/ directory into subdirectories
description:
Reorganize 78 command files in flat cmd/ directory into logical subdirectories.

Create subdirectories:
- cmd/mission/: All mission-related commands
- cmd/config/: Configuration commands
- cmd/cron/: Cron management commands
- cmd/tmux/: Tmux integration commands  
- cmd/daemon/: Daemon management commands

Update import paths atomically.
Target: ~40 files after consolidation.

Reference: P2 (formerly P0-3) in specs/codebase-cleanup.md
Note: Deprioritized from P0 - navigation issue, not critical
Estimated time: 1 week
notes:
2026-09-06 audit (AgenC mission 7e071462-4819-4684-b12d-0183477cdb61), triggered by Kevin's challenge that the tech-debt epic predates a much-changed codebase. RECOMMEND CLOSE.

Every load-bearing number in the premise is stale, and one of the five proposed subdirectories maps to zero files.
- File count: cmd/ held 76 non-test .go files at commit 9f69e0d; it now holds 125 (139 including tests). The ticket's '78 files' is off by 61, and its '~40 after consolidation' would now mean deleting or merging ~100 files - a different and much larger proposal than the one written.
- cmd/daemon/ maps to nothing. There are no daemon command files; the daemon was replaced by the server (see the deprecation note at internal/config/config.go:24-26). Meanwhile cmd/ has 10 server*.go files the plan never mentions.
- The five buckets cover only 55% of the directory: mission 23, config 24, tmux 11, cron 10, daemon 0, and 56 files (notifications_*, repo_*, server_*, summary*, doctor, token, attach, fzf_picker) fit no proposed bucket.

The claimed benefit does not apply to this repo's actual reader. Navigation and onboarding are the stated value; this codebase is worked almost entirely by agents, who reach cmd/mission_ls.go by grep or exact path. The filename prefix already encodes the grouping a directory would add.

The cost is far higher than 'navigation refactor' implies:
- 248 cross-file reference edges cross the proposed bucket lines (regex-derived, so an approximate upper bound; the largest, serverClient declared at cmd/mission_helpers.go:141, was hand-verified as referenced from 53 non-test files).
- The naive split is illegal Go, not merely laborious: edges run both ways across the same boundary, so root would import cmd/mission (for serverClient) while cmd/mission.go:13 does rootCmd.AddCommand(missionCmd), i.e. an import cycle. Resolving it means extracting a new shared package and exporting ~207 currently-unexported identifiers.
- SILENT failure mode the ticket does not anticipate: commands self-register via 109 init() functions in package cmd (112 AddCommand calls). Today main.go imports cmd once and all of them run. Under subpackages each needs a blank import; omit one and its commands simply do not exist - no compile error, no test failure. This propagates further: cmd/genprime/main.go:39 walks rootCmd.Commands() to generate the prime template injected into EVERY mission, so a missed subpackage silently removes commands from every agent's command reference.

ANSI / ForPicker enforcement (specifically checked): the reorganization would WEAKEN this guard rather than disturb it neutrally. All 13 cmd/ test files are internal (package cmd) and call unexported functions directly. Several ForPicker functions already cross the proposed bucket lines - displayGitRepoForPicker declared cmd/mission_ls.go:147 but called from cmd/repo_helpers.go:18; formatRepoDisplayForPicker (mission_ls.go:182) called from cmd/repo_rm.go:80 and cmd/mission_new.go:340; formatMissionCellForPicker lives in cmd/notifications_manage.go:192, which has no bucket at all - so the split forces them to be exported. Unexported-ness is exactly what bounds the blast radius today, as the test comment at cmd/repo_display_test.go:99-100 states. Once exported, nothing structural stops a future agent calling the colour-emitting variant on a stdout path. CLAUDE.md's rule is also single-package-scoped ('Within cmd/, an unsuffixed name returns plain text') and would need restating per package. The E2E half (run_test_output_has_no_ansi, scripts/e2e-test.sh:117) is package-agnostic and survives - but CLAUDE.md already warns that list is hand-maintained and not a sweep.

Flip condition: sustained human contributors in cmd/ (say 3+ distinct non-Kevin, non-agent authors in a quarter), since the value claim is entirely about human navigation. Even then the ticket needs rewriting from scratch given the cmd/daemon/ and file-count errors.
close_reason: Closed on Kevin approval 2026-09-07. Audited against the current codebase by an independent agent during mission 7e071462, which found the condition this bead describes no longer holds; the file-and-line evidence is recorded in this bead notes. Kevin had challenged the whole epic as predating too much change to still be real, and all five remaining beads came back recommending CLOSE.

title: Create pre-commit hook for code quality
description:
Create a pre-commit hook that enforces gofmt and runs go vet.

Create .git/hooks/pre-commit:
#\!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

unformatted=$(gofmt -l .)
if [[ -n "$unformatted" ]]; then
    echo "Files need formatting: $unformatted"
    echo "Run: gofmt -w ."
    exit 1
fi

go vet ./...

Make executable: chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
Test by attempting a commit with unformatted code

title: Stop Mission palette command should return instantly
description: The Stop Mission palette command currently blocks the tmux popup until the mission finishes shutting down. It should return control to the user immediately so they can navigate to other tmux panes while the stop runs in the background. Attempted fixes: (1) appending & to background the shell command — didn't work, likely because the tmux display-popup PTY teardown kills the backgrounded process. (2) Using nohup with output redirection and & — also didn't work. The root challenge is that the palette runs inside tmux display-popup -E, which destroys the PTY when the popup command exits, likely killing any child processes. A solution needs to fully detach the stop process from the popup's process group/session (e.g., setsid, or handling it in Go code with SysProcAttr.Setsid, or having the palette write to a file/socket that a daemon picks up).

title: Run make e2e in CI
description:
WHY: CI (added in mieubrisse/agenc-csvm-uncommittable-red-tests) runs 'make check' only. The repo's CLAUDE.md says E2E testing is mandatory for behavioral changes, but nothing enforces it — an agent can skip 'make e2e' and no automated gate notices.

Making it work in CI means solving those three, or carving out a subset of e2e-test.sh that runs without a live Claude session.

Recording this so the coverage gap is visible rather than silently assumed covered.

title: Make mission search-result ordering E2E-testable
description:
The mission picker's search path now sorts rows by two tiers (direct mission-ID match, then recency), but neither tier has a discriminating E2E test, so a regression in either would ship green.

WHY THIS IS HARD TODAY: the only row source the test environment can populate is the substring merge over ListMissions, which already returns newest-first — a test over it passes whether or not the sort runs at all. The two paths that actually reorder need state the test environment cannot produce: FTS rows need indexed session content, and putting a second row in front of a mission-ID query needs a session title (mission rename fails with 'no sessions found'), both of which require a live Claude session. The mission row's prompt column is also not written at creation time, so --prompt cannot seed a matchable string either.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: any way to seed rows in the test environment whose pre-sort merge order differs from their post-sort order. Worth considering: a hidden test-only seeding command, letting the search index be populated directly, or persisting the initial prompt on the mission row at creation.

ACCEPTANCE: scripts/e2e-test.sh asserts newest-first ordering AND the direct mission-ID match landing first, and both assertions fail when the corresponding tier is removed from sortSearchRows. The visible SKIP added alongside the fix is then removed.

Context: PR #41 (github.com/mieubrisse/agenc/pull/41) and its follow-up. AgenC mission 7cb1c2c3-edd1-4a1d-bf7d-c9bf4828d630.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/e2e-test.sh asserts newest-first ordering AND the direct mission-ID match landing first, and each assertion fails when its tier is removed from sortSearchRows. The visible SKIP added alongside the fix is then removed.
notes: The SKIP this closes was added in PR #42 (https://github.com/mieubrisse/agenc/pull/42), which superseded PR #41. See scripts/e2e-test.sh, 'search-fzf orders results newest-first'.

title: Color missions waiting on a background agent as blue in mission status output
description:
GOAL: `agenc mission ls` colors each mission by display status so Kevin can scan the fleet and tell at a glance which missions need him. Blue currently means IDLE (cmd/mission_ls.go:232, `colorizeStatusForPicker`), fed by `getMissionStatus` (cmd/mission_ls.go:273), which maps Claude's reported `claudeState` of idle/busy/needs_attention onto IDLE/BUSY/WAITING and sends everything else to RUNNING (green). A mission parked in Claude Code's "Waiting for background agent to finish" state is neither consuming Kevin's attention nor doing work he needs to watch — it belongs in the same at-rest blue bucket, but today it falls through the default branch. Kevin's ask, verbatim (Todoist capture 2026-09-04): "update the status reporting so that agents which are in 'Waiting for background agent to finish' are also marked as blue."

CONSTRAINTS: Whether this means folding the state into IDLE or introducing a new display status that also renders blue is the executor's call — but the at-a-glance meaning of the other colors must not shift, and the bare (uncolorized) status string that command output prints is what agents compare against, so changing that string has downstream readers.

OPEN QUESTION for the executor: confirm what color that state renders as today, and which `claudeState` value (if any) Claude Code actually reports for it. The current default-to-RUNNING mapping suggests green, but that was inferred from reading the switch rather than observed on a live mission.

PROVENANCE: routed from Todoist inbox during AgenC mission 2e94e194-6341-44a5-8c51-062bebb845df.
acceptance_criteria: A mission whose Claude session is waiting on a background agent renders blue on the colorized status surfaces (fzf picker and any other human-facing status output), and every existing state — IDLE, BUSY, WAITING, RUNNING, STOPPED, ARCHIVED — renders exactly as it does today. Verified by observing a real mission in that state, not only by reading the switch statement.
notes: 2026-09-05, Kevin — OBSERVED, and it supersedes the OPEN QUESTION guess in the description: today a mission waiting on a background agent renders as "agent is done" with the tab uncolored. It is NOT the default-to-RUNNING/green path the description inferred from reading the switch. That sharpens the why: the state currently reads as FINISHED, so Kevin looks at the fleet and believes a still-working mission has completed — the harm is a false done-signal, not merely an off palette choice. Whoever picks this up should start from the uncolored/done rendering path, not from getMissionStatus's RUNNING default.

title: Close the E2E blind spots in the no-ANSI check
description:
## Why

The E2E section added by agenc-hxr4 looks like it guards every agenc command against ANSI escapes. It does not — it is a hand-maintained list of ten invocations, and three specific holes were found by a clean-context review of PR #38 rather than by the suite itself.

The holes matter because this bug class is silent by nature. A command that regains colour errors nowhere; the parse on the other end just stops matching. A coverage gap here is indistinguishable from coverage.

1. `agenc cron history` was de-coloured by the same commit and is in neither the E2E list nor any unit test. Reverting that line would be caught by nothing. It takes a required name argument, so covering it needs a cron to exist in the test environment first.
2. The `cron ls` entry is on the list but vacuous: no cron exists at that point in the suite, so the loop body containing the line the change touched never executes. Restoring the yellow would pass.
3. The `mission search` entry is likewise vacuous: no search hits, so no snippet is rendered and the ColorizeSnippet-to-StripSnippetMarkers change is unexercised.

Roughly ten of twenty-six output-producing commands are on the list at all.

The deeper question worth answering before adding entries one at a time: whether a hand-maintained list is the right shape for this at all, given that the failure mode is precisely someone forgetting to extend it. A check that enumerates commands from the Cobra tree, or that asserts the invariant somewhere it cannot be forgotten, may be the better answer — but that trades against runtime and against commands that cannot run unattended.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The three named holes either have real coverage — meaning the test would fail if the colour were restored — or are documented as deliberately uncovered with the reason
- Whatever shape the check ends up in, forgetting to extend it is not silently equivalent to passing
- CLAUDE.md's description of the enforcement matches what the enforcement actually does, whichever way this is resolved

## Provenance
Found by clean-context review of PR #38 during AgenC mission 2c644c10-f76c-441c-8e1f-092a90b0566b. Follows agenc-hxr4 (the change) and agenc-afp8 (the documentation). Recorded rather than fixed there to keep that PR's scope; the inaccurate coverage claim was the half fixed immediately.

title: Document the no-ANSI-in-command-output convention in AgenC's CLAUDE.md
description:
## Why

agenc-hxr4 removed ANSI colour from all agenc command output because agents parse it and an escape inside a status field breaks a comparison silently. The invariant is now enforced by tests (an E2E section that captures output to a file and greps for 0x1b, plus Go unit tests on the shared formatters), but it is not stated anywhere an agent reads before writing new output code.

The gap that leaves: someone adding a new command, or a new column to an existing one, has no reason to know the rule exists. They find out when `make e2e` fails, if they run it — the pre-commit hook runs `make check`, not `make e2e`.

The line the convention needs to draw is destination-based, not file-based: output a command writes to stdout carries no escapes; strings handed to fzf as TUI chrome (the tmux command palette and the pickers it opens) keep their colour. Kevin confirmed the palette half explicitly.

## Why it was not done in agenc-hxr4

The repo has no CLAUDE.design.md sibling. /cc-global-instructions-management requires bootstrapping one when editing a CLAUDE.md that lacks it, and reconstructing design rationale for the whole AgenC CLAUDE.md from the outside risks recording a 'why' that was never true. That bootstrap is a decision for Kevin, not a side effect of this fix.

## Acceptance Criteria
- An agent about to add or change agenc command output encounters the rule without having to run the test suite to discover it
- The interactive-surface exception is stated as part of the rule, so a future change does not strip the palette's colour while 'fixing' output
- Whatever the repo's CLAUDE.design.md situation ends up being, it is resolved deliberately rather than left half-done

## Provenance
Split out of agenc-hxr4 during AgenC mission 2c644c10-f76c-441c-8e1f-092a90b0566b. Bead filed by Kevin's agent 2026-09-01.
notes:
2026-09-01 KEVIN AUTHORIZED: start the design.md, with the explicit constraint 'obviously it shouldn't fabricate anything'. This resolves the reason mission 2c644c10 originally declined — it correctly judged that bootstrapping a design doc for a whole CLAUDE.md it never witnessed risked recording a 'why' that was never true.

LINE TO HOLD, relayed to 2c644c10: write only what is known firsthand or verifiable. In-scope because witnessed — the ANSI change's rationale: the destination-based split, why named colouring variants were chosen over runtime conditionals (a stdout caller cannot pick up colour by accident rather than merely being expected not to), Kevin's palette carve-out (he uses the palette heavily while CLI output is agent-consumed), and that the inline escape at cmd/tmux_palette.go:333 is deliberately kept. Also in scope: anything sourceable from git history or beads. Everything else is OUT — for unsourceable parts, state so on the page rather than reaching for a plausible why, and include an explicit note that the document begins at this change and that pre-existing decisions were not reconstructed. Rationale for that instruction: a fabricated why teaches wrong generalisation precisely where the reader most needs to trust the record. Scope bounded to STARTING the document, not auditing the whole CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md convention section plus a new CLAUDE.design.md shipped in PR #38 (https://github.com/mieubrisse/agenc/pull/38). Design doc deliberately starts at 2026-09-01 and says so on the page; pre-existing CLAUDE.md sections were not reconstructed, per Kevin's instruction not to fabricate rationale.

title: mission detach fails when the pane's window was already unlinked from the recorded session
description:
## Why
`agenc mission detach` errors and leaves AgenC's bookkeeping inconsistent when tmux and AgenC's stored session attribution have diverged. The user asked for a mission to be parked; the command reported failure, so it is unclear whether the mission still counts against the attached-mission limit.

## Observed
`agenc mission detach dd09fd51` fails:

    Error: failed to detach mission
     --- at cmd/mission_detach.go:65 (runMissionDetach) ---
    Caused by: failed to unlink window: pane 134 not found in session hyperspace
     --- at internal/server/pool.go:104 (unlinkPoolWindowByPane) ---

Reality per tmux: the pane is `agenc-pool:@126.%134`. It is NOT in `hyperspace`, which is why the lookup fails — the window had already been unlinked from hyperspace, so the desired end state was effectively reached, but AgenC still recorded the mission as attached to hyperspace and errored trying to unlink it again. Note windows can be linked into multiple sessions simultaneously (`@75.%79` appeared in both `agenc-pool` and `hyperspace` at the same time), so single-session attribution appears to be an unsafe assumption.

Retried after the mission went idle, in case it was a busy-state race; same failure.

## Suggested direction (not a prescription)
Treat an already-absent pane as success rather than an error — the caller's intent is 'this should not be attached', and that state is satisfied. Reconciling AgenC's recorded session against tmux's actual attribution before unlinking, and tolerating windows linked into several sessions, would likely address the class rather than this instance.

## Impact
Attached missions are capped at 6 and a spawn fails outright when the cap is reached, so bookkeeping that over-counts attachments can block mission creation with no obvious cause. Related friction seen the same day: a STOPPED mission with no pane also cannot be detached ('mission has no tmux pane'), so it cannot be cleared from the count either.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `agenc mission detach` succeeds (or reports a clear no-op) when the pane is absent from the recorded session
- Detach works for a mission whose window is linked into a different or additional session than the one recorded
- A mission that cannot hold a pane (e.g. STOPPED) can still be cleared from the attached count

## Provenance
Found in AgenC mission 591187e7-dab6-4b2d-a063-ff12220d4c3a while parking mission dd09fd51-5d07-4125-814c-3c9f24f3f247.

title: Explore driving AgenC interaction through email, backed by missions
description:
Kevin's captured idea (inbox 2026-08-21): what if the primary interface to AgenC work were email rather than the terminal?

The shape he sketched: missions stay the substrate and remain openable when you want to watch what an agent is doing — but when Claude needs to communicate asynchronously, it emails you, and your reply gets threaded back into the session as the next turn. An 'email bridge'.

WHY this matters to him: async, low-attention interaction with running work. Today, staying in the loop on a mission means going to the mission. Email would invert that — work reaches out to Kevin on its own schedule, in a medium he already lives in and that already works on his phone.

Kevin explicitly flagged this as needing a pros/cons pass before any build. Treat the exploration as the deliverable, not an implementation.
acceptance_criteria: A written pros/cons analysis exists that a decision could be made from: what this unlocks, what it costs, what breaks (security of an inbound email channel that drives agent execution, identity/spoofing, latency, threading fidelity, how it interacts with existing notification paths), and a recommendation on whether to build, prototype, or drop. If the recommendation is build or prototype, the smallest viable slice is named.

title: Dead RunHeadless wrapper path + stale arch-doc headless description
description:

title: agenc doctor: warn on leftover claude-modifications overlay in config repo
description: WHY: the claude-modifications overlay was retired in the State-Y flip (#13; agenc-lh8p). Users who upgrade to State Y may still have config/claude-modifications/{CLAUDE.md,settings.json} sitting in their AgenC config repo — now INERT (no code reads it) but confusing clutter, and a place a user might keep editing expecting it to take effect (it won't). A cheap check-loop that surfaces the dead-config leftover for upgraders.

title: Rip out devcontainer-reading infrastructure
description:
Kevin wants the devcontainer-reading infrastructure removed entirely.

WHY: it was never really tested end-to-end, it causes problems, and it is the last thing forcing AgenC to materialize a per-mission config directory and do ~/.claude path rewriting. Once gone, the config model collapses to a pure host-native passthrough (see agenc-tcoh "State Y": unset CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, use the user's real ~/.claude, inject the operational layer via `claude --settings`). Keeping devcontainer support would force us to preserve the materialized-config + path-rewriting machinery solely for a code path Kevin doesn't use.

SCOPE: this is a SEPARATE mission from the shadow removal (agenc-tcoh). The two are independent and can be done in either order, but devcontainer teardown removes the last consumer of the path-rewriting / materialized-config machinery, so doing it clears the way.

CONSTRAINTS: host (non-containerized) missions must be completely unaffected; do not regress normal spawn/attach/reload. This is a deletion, not a rewrite — resist the urge to "improve" adjacent code.

Surfaces to remove (starting map, not prescriptive): internal/devcontainer/ (detection, overlay, project-path encoding), internal/wrapper/devcontainer.go and the container spawn branch, the container hook-entry variants (BuildContainerHookEntries and staticContainerHookEntries in claudeconfig/overrides.go), any `containerized` parameter threading through claudeconfig/wrapper, and the container/devcontainer sections of docs/system-architecture.md.
acceptance_criteria: Devcontainer detection, overlay generation, and container spawn paths removed; no code path reads devcontainer.json; container-specific branches in claudeconfig/wrapper deleted; docs/system-architecture.md drops the containerized-mission sections; make build + make check + make e2e all green; host missions verified unaffected (create/attach/reload).
close_reason: Devcontainer infrastructure fully removed across 4 commits on main (d0de767, f428f89, 3606a12, c03a04d): internal/devcontainer package, wrapper/devcontainer.go, the rebuild command + palette entry, container spawn path, the two container-only socket handlers, and the containerized config param all deleted; host machinery preserved. make check green; make e2e 136/136; opus whole-branch review clean. Kevin confirmed the manual palette check ('looks good'). Design+plan: docs/plans/2026-07-28-devcontainer-removal-{design,plan}.md. Unblocks agenc-vhy8; filed agenc-g9vu for a pre-existing /restart doc bug found during review.

title: agenc server status reports 'not running' while the server is alive
description:
GOAL (why): 'agenc server status' must accurately reflect whether the server is running, so agents and Kevin can trust it as a diagnostic. During mission d46ed46e-4160-4d16-97e6-3918900fe022 (2026-07-07), 'agenc server status' printed 'Server is not running.' while the server was demonstrably alive: pidfile ~/.agenc/server/server.pid held 64388, the unix socket ~/.agenc/server/server.sock existed, and the server was actively writing writeable-copy tick logs to ~/.agenc/server/server.log every few seconds. Relying on the status output would have produced a wrong root-cause ('your server is down') for an unrelated investigation.

HYPOTHESIS (needs confirmation): the status liveness check reads a signal (pidfile staleness, a namespace-hashed identifier, or a probe method) that is out of sync with the actually-running server process. Single unconfirmed observation — not yet reproduced or root-caused.

Provenance: AgenC mission d46ed46e-4160-4d16-97e6-3918900fe022.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 'agenc server status' returns a running/alive result whenever a server process is actually up and serving on ~/.agenc/server/server.sock (verify against pidfile + socket + live log activity). 2) Root cause identified (why the check missed pid 64388) and a regression test added so status can't silently diverge from actual process state again.

title: Writeable-copy auto-sync silently storms against repos with commit hooks
description:
GOAL (why): The writeable-copy sync daemon exists to reliably persist Kevin's working copies to their remotes without his attention. Against a repo with an opinionated git-hook stack it cannot do its job AND fails invisibly.

Observed on the alembiq writeable copy (/Users/odyssey/code/alembiq): the daemon's ordinary 'git commit -m auto-sync:<ts>' is rejected by alembiq's commit-msg hook (commitlint / Conventional Commits) — the 'auto-sync: <timestamp>' message can NEVER pass (type/subject empty). Separately, its pre-commit hook can fail on transient repo state (a missing 'resend' npm dep broke the typecheck gate). When commit fails, runWriteableCopyTick (internal/server/writeable_copies.go:341) treats it as 'transient' and retries forever with NO pause and NO notification — unlike every other failure class (rebase conflict, non-FF, auth, wrong-branch, origin-drift, path-missing, git-corrupt), each of which posts a pause+notification. Worse: the failing pre-commit hook regenerates tracked files (skill manifests), which re-fires the working-tree watcher, producing a tight retry loop.

Evidence: ~/.agenc/server/server.log logged 64,185 failed auto-commits for alembiq over 13 days (2026-06-24 12:17 -> 2026-07-07 14:40), zero notifications, continuously running the alembiq test suite every ~9s. Kevin's only signal was noticing his repo had stopped syncing. This is a 'loud failures, not silent failures' violation and a design mismatch: a persistence daemon should not be gated by (nor trigger the side-effects of — e.g. the pre-push Notion API calls) a repo's interactive commit/push hooks.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Must work uniformly across ALL writeable copies (dotfiles, exobrain, alembiq); do not special-case alembiq.
- Extend the existing pause+notification model as the loud-failure channel for commit/push failures; do not invent a parallel mechanism.
- Do not break the fast-forward pull path (remote->writeable-copy ff works today; it runs no commit hooks).
- Any hook-bypass must be a deliberate, documented decision; the repo's own remote CI stays the real quality gate.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION (Kevin decides, do not choose unilaterally): auto-sync commits/pushes with --no-verify (bypass pre-commit/commit-msg/pre-push entirely, treating sync as pure persistence) VS keep hooks and conform the auto-sync commit message to Conventional Commits + handle gate failures via loud pause. Author recommendation: --no-verify on both commit and push, plus a loud pause after N consecutive failures as defense-in-depth.

Key refs: internal/server/writeable_copies.go:153 (auto-sync msg format), :307 (runWriteableCopyTick), :341 (transient swallow of commit failure). Provenance: AgenC mission d46ed46e-4160-4d16-97e6-3918900fe022.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Daemon persists alembiq working-tree changes to origin/main without manual intervention (make a change in the writeable copy; it lands on origin within a debounce cycle). 2) No infinite retry loop: repeated failure backs off and does not continuously re-trigger via hook side-effects. 3) Sustained commit/push failure produces a pause + notification (loud), like other failure classes — verify by simulating a failing hook. 4) Verified across one hook-heavy repo (alembiq) and one plain repo (dotfiles/exobrain).
notes:
Steps to reproduce: (1) Register a writeable copy of a repo whose git hooks reject the daemon's commit — e.g. a commit-msg commitlint hook enforcing Conventional Commits (the 'auto-sync: <ts>' message fails type-empty/subject-empty), or any failing pre-commit gate. (2) Make a local change so the working tree is dirty. (3) Observe ~/.agenc/server/server.log: 'Writeable-copy auto-commit failed for <repo>' repeating every few seconds indefinitely, with no pause row in writeable_copy_pauses and no notification. Confirm the tree never commits/pushes and (if the failing hook writes tracked files) the loop self-retriggers.
DECISION (2026-07-07, Kevin): Instead of adapting auto-sync to hook-heavy repos, alembiq was REMOVED as a writeable copy ('agenc repo writeable-copy unset mieubrisse/alembiq'). Principle: a real software product with quality-gate hooks (pre-commit/commit-msg/pre-push) should be written via spawned missions that make proper conventional commits, not a continuous persistence daemon. The --no-verify design fork is therefore REJECTED. Bead narrowed + lowered to P3: the remaining general defect is that writeable-copy sync must FAIL LOUDLY (pause+notification) and back off on sustained commit/push failure rather than silently retry-storming — still valid for any future writeable copy whose commit fails transiently. Acute driver resolved (alembiq 13-day backlog committed as 5cf2adb + pushed; storm stopped).
PREVENTIVE ANGLE (same incident, prevention not just detection): beyond failing loudly at runtime, agenc could prevent the mismatch at REGISTRATION time — when 'agenc repo writeable-copy set' targets a repo whose hooks would reject the daemon's auto-sync commits (e.g. a commit-msg/commitlint hook enforcing Conventional Commits, or a heavy pre-commit gate), warn or refuse at set-time instead of silently accepting a writeable copy that can never sync. Encodes Kevin's principle: hook-heavy software products get written via spawned missions, not the persistence daemon. Consider bundling with the loud-failure fix.
