title: Decide fate of devcontainer support after omar's reply on issue #8
description:
## Context

GitHub issue: https://github.com/mieubrisse/agenc/issues/8 (omar-augur, filed 2026-05-28)

A fresh-install user (omar) hit a fatal crash on mission startup when checking out a project that contained a `devcontainer.json` with a JSONC-style comment. Kevin acknowledged on 2026-05-29 and asked omar to post the offending file. As of 2026-06-08 omar has not replied. This bead ices the work pending omar's response.

## Root cause (confirmed)

- `internal/devcontainer/overlay.go:53` parses the repo's `devcontainer.json` with stdlib `json.Unmarshal`, which rejects comments. The devcontainer spec defines that file as JSONC (VS Code parses it that way), so any repo with a comment in it crashes the parse.
- `internal/wrapper/wrapper.go:247` propagates that parse error all the way up and aborts the entire mission at startup. No graceful degradation path.

## The design finding underneath the bug

There is no opt-in for containerization. `detectAndSetupDevcontainer()` (wrapper.go:241) auto-activates the container path purely because the checked-out repo contains a `devcontainer.json`. With no file, missions run Claude directly (`spawnClaudeDirectly`). omar never asked for a container — he checked out a normal project whose repo ships a `devcontainer.json` (extremely common for VS Code repos), and AgenC silently tried to containerize it and died on a comment.

## Footprint of a rip-out

Feature was added in a clean burst of ~5 commits Apr 13–14 (`f383447` → `6486e3f`), so restore-later is genuinely realistic. Surfaces touched:

- `internal/devcontainer/` package: detection.go (28), overlay.go (265), project_path_encoding.go (32) + ~360 LOC of tests
- `internal/wrapper/devcontainer.go` (118)
- wrapper.go integration: setupRun lines 240-260, spawnClaude branching 327-422, handleRebuildCommand 533-574
- `cmd/mission_rebuild.go` (67)
- `rebuildContainer` palette entry in internal/config/agenc_config.go
- server teardown in internal/server/missions.go:720-732
- architecture-doc sections in docs/system-architecture.md

Total ~440 non-test LOC + ~360 test LOC + integration.

## The options on the table

| | Diff size | Unblocks omar? | Keeps feature | Sheds maintenance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A. Rip it out (Kevin's lean) | Large | Yes | No | Yes |
| B. Minimal safety fix — make parse non-fatal (warn, skip overlay, run directly) | ~5 lines | Yes | Yes | No |
| C. B + JSONC parser + opt-in gate | Medium | Yes | Yes (better) | No |

Kevin's lean is A (he doesn't use it, hit issues himself). The picker should wait on omar's reply before committing — his response may shift the crux (e.g. if his case reveals someone IS relying on container isolation, that pushes toward C; if it's just a stray devcontainer.json in a project he didn't intend to containerize, A or B stand).

## omar's side note (separate)

omar flagged that the Claude in his mission couldn't find AgenC's source to self-debug. Not part of this issue but worth a follow-up bead: register agenc in the repo library or otherwise expose its source to missions.

## Provenance

- AgenC mission: 8f58e9e8-3bec-49a9-a395-d0445c7a7137
- AgenC session: 02889eff (run `agenc session print 02889eff --all` for the full investigation transcript)
- GitHub issue: https://github.com/mieubrisse/agenc/issues/8

title: Surface per-mission token-budget observability — where each mission is spending tokens
description:
Today AgenC missions are token-budget black boxes — there's no built-in way to see where a mission's tokens are going (which skills, which subagents, which MCP servers). Cron-fired autonomous missions (arpan-claude-optimization-suggestions, daily-state-summary, hacker-news-daily-pull, exobrain-update, verify-workspace-mcp-denylist) compound this: they run on schedule, their cost-per-run is invisible, and cost regressions ('hacker-news-daily-pull is up 20% week-over-week') only surface when bills arrive.

Claude Code v2.1.149 added a per-category /usage breakdown — skills, subagents, plugins, per-MCP-server cost. That primitive is now available inside every Claude Code session, including every AgenC mission.

Opportunity: AgenC surfaces structured cost data per mission as a first-class concept — captured on session end (or mid-mission via a polling primitive), queryable across missions, with trend analysis. Especially valuable for autonomous cron missions where Kevin can't be watching live.

One concrete starting move: a SessionEnd or PreCompact hook gated on AGENC_MISSION_SOURCE=cron captures the /usage breakdown and writes to a structured location AgenC owns. Over weeks this becomes a queryable cost-trend dataset and could power per-mission cost dashboards in `agenc mission ls` or a dedicated subcommand.

Provenance: AgenC mission ed19373a-ea9a-4ccb-a2ce-fce9bbaf906b — surfaced during claude-code-upgrade-review of v2.1.145→v2.1.153. The /usage primitive is what makes per-mission cost observability cheap to implement now. See https://docs.claude.com/en/release-notes/claude-code

title: Investigate: does Dolt preserve audit history for bead text fields after destructive writes?
description: During a /five-whys on a bd update wipe of agenc-zmhy's notes field (AgenC mission d291a7a0, session 335b6ed8), the recovery succeeded only because the original notes content was still in the agent's tool-result history from an earlier bd show. A fresh-session destructive bead-update with the same bug would have lost the original content from the agent's perspective. Question: does Dolt's row-versioning preserve prior values of text fields (notes/description/design) such that a bd-side recovery primitive could exist (e.g., 'bd undo <id>' or 'bd show <id> --at=<commit>')? If yes, that's a recovery affordance worth surfacing in /beads-system or as a 'bd recover' subcommand. If no, the structural fix from agenc-zmhy/agenc-w039 (hard-gate via skill-invocation tracking) is more urgent. Replay: agenc session print 335b6ed8 --all.

title: writeable-copy reconcile: evaluate vendoring git-auto-sync + git-sync's atomic-symlink-flip pattern
description:
During the 2026-06-08 FD-leak research pass for agenc-ku7h, a divergent web-research sweep surfaced strong evidence that AgenC's writeable-copy reconcile machinery (internal/server/writeable_copies.go) is largely reinventing prior art:

WRITEABLE LEG — GitJournal/git-auto-sync (Apache-2.0, Go)
  https://github.com/GitJournal/git-auto-sync
  Implements ~80%% of AgenC's writeable-leg loop with matching design choices: fsnotify + poll, commit-if-dirty, fetch, rebase-only (no auto-merge), abort-and-notify on conflict. Behavior of pausing-on-conflict matches AgenC's pause states.

  CAVEAT (the reason this bead is exploratory, not directive): the repo has very low star count (~200 stars) and last meaningful commit is ~4 years ago. So before adopting we need ANOTHER expansion-pass of research at pickup time — verify it's still the closest analog, scan for forks/successors, check newer projects in the space that may have superseded it. The current research surfaced it as the closest match in early-2026 but the maintenance signal is weak.

MIRROR LEG — kubernetes/git-sync's atomic-worktree-plus-symlink-flip
  https://github.com/kubernetes/git-sync
  Fetch into a side worktree, atomic symlink flip when ready. Production-proven pattern that ensures mission spawns never see a half-pulled mirror state. Should be adopted into internal/repo/ regardless of the git-auto-sync decision — these are independent leverage points.

THREE-WAY TRIAD specifically
  Nothing models all three legs (writeable + read-only mirror + remote). That's genuinely AgenC-specific. No tool to buy at that layer — but we can compose existing tools for each leg.

WHEN PICKING THIS UP:
1. Re-run the expansion research — git-auto-sync's maintenance signal is the weakest part of this lead. Look for forks, successors, and any new projects that emerged in 2025-2026.
2. Spike git-auto-sync against a test repo with concurrent Claude-agent writes to the same path. The big unknown is whether it assumes exclusive-writer semantics that would conflict with mission writes.
3. Evaluate atomic-symlink-flip for the read-only mirror independently — that one is unambiguously a steal.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: do not conflate this with agenc-ku7h (the FD-leak fix). The watcher refactor on agenc-ku7h uses rjeczalik/notify + go-git's gitignore matcher and is independent of this question.

Related: agenc-ku7h (the FD-leak bug that prompted this research)

Provenance:
- AgenC mission: ab2584f3-1f48-43e8-a61e-e05cfb493707
- Diagnostic session: 0f366f73
- Research subagents that surfaced these leads: a11b36b6a578d90ad, a6d50573fbce481d2

title: writeable-copy: EMFILE-from-git misclassified as 'git_corrupt', triggering false auto-PAUSE
description:
During the 2026-06-07 FD-exhaustion incident (see agenc-ku7h for root cause), two writeable-copies (alembiq, dotfiles) were auto-PAUSEd with reason 'git_corrupt' because their reconcile-tick git subprocess invocations failed.

The actual failure mode in the log was:
  Caused by: git status --porcelain=v1 failed in '/Users/odyssey/code/alembiq':
   --- at /Users/odyssey/app/agenc/internal/server/git_command.go:94 (realGit.runGit) ---
  Caused by: open /dev/null: too many open files

i.e. the git subprocess couldn't even be spawned because the agenc parent process couldn't open /dev/null for stdio redirection. That's a transient resource-exhaustion failure of the host process — not repository corruption.

internal/server/writeable_copies.go runWriteableCopyTick (the resume probe failing here) appears to treat any non-zero git_status exit / spawn failure as 'git_corrupt', without distinguishing:
  - real corruption (objects missing, refs broken)
  - transient host-side failures (EMFILE, ENOMEM, signal interruption)
  - actual git errors that don't imply corruption (lock contention, permission)

Effect: a transient FD-exhaustion event on the parent process permanently degrades writeable-copies to PAUSED state, requiring a server restart to recover. (Both auto-resumed on the 20:11:09 restart, so the user didn't have to act — but only because the writeable-copy state isn't persisted across restarts, or because resume-probe succeeded on the fresh process. Worth verifying which.)

FIX DIRECTION: the pause heuristic should classify by failure shape, not collapse everything to 'git_corrupt'. EMFILE / spawn-time errors should be retried, not PAUSE-ed.

Related: agenc-ku7h (the FD-exhaustion root cause that triggered this misclassification)

Provenance:
- AgenC mission: ab2584f3-1f48-43e8-a61e-e05cfb493707
- Diagnostic session that surfaced this: 0f366f73

title: Set TMPDIR to a per-mission location
description:
**Problem:** Mission-local temporary output (rendered HTML from /html-output, intermediate plans, scratch artifacts) lands in the system tmp dir today, with no link back to which mission produced it. Setting TMPDIR to a per-mission directory would co-locate that output with mission state.

**Why this matters:** Especially relevant for /html-output — currently the rendered HTML lands in the system temp dir and is effectively detached from the mission that generated it. Per-mission TMPDIR makes those artifacts inspectable as part of mission state.

**Open questions for the picker:**
- Cruft accumulation — is per-mission temp a leak risk across many missions?
- Cleanup lifecycle — when does the directory get GC'd?
- Larger frame: would docker-containerized missions make this moot by making everything mission-scoped and disposable? (Bigger change, no answer yet — out of scope for this bead unless the picker concludes otherwise.)

**Provenance:** Inbox capture 2026-06-06. Filed from AgenC mission da02eccd-72ba-414c-ac2f-e8ec0b0c2317.

title: Close sandbox-transitivity gap: make git commit / pre-commit hook work without dangerouslyDisableSandbox dance
description:
Structural fix for the sandbox / pre-commit-hook friction caught in AgenC mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f (Diamond Cascade REFLECT for the repo description feature).

WHY: The project's pre-commit hook runs 'make check', which runs wrapper integration tests that bind unix sockets in temp paths. The default Bash sandbox blocks those binds. The CLAUDE.md tells me to set dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true for direct 'make build'/'make check' invocations, but never names the transitive case where 'git commit' inherits the same requirement via the hook. Five-whys diagnosis: the rule has a documentation gap (category b) — not just my misreading.

TWO FIX CANDIDATES (pick one — they are alternatives, not both):

FIX 2a (priority 1, best — removes the dance entirely):
Update agent/.claude/settings.json to extend the sandbox config so the project's test suite runs sandboxed. Specifically:
- read-allow ~/.cache/go-build (Go build cache)
- write/socket-allow the $TMPDIR-scoped unix sockets the wrapper tests bind to
The /fewer-permission-prompts or /update-config skill can audit recent denials and propose the minimal allowlist. Removes the 'remember to disable sandbox for make-anything' rule entirely, including its transitive applications.

FIX 2b (priority 3, fallback if 2a's allowlist scope is uncomfortable):
Rewrite the agent/CLAUDE.md 'Building and Checking' sandbox paragraph to add: 'git commit triggers the pre-commit hook, which runs make check — git commit therefore inherits the dangerouslyDisableSandbox=true requirement.' Documentation is weaker, but closes the named gap without changing sandbox policy.

CONTEXT TO LINK:
- AgenC mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f for the originating /five-whys analysis
- agent/CLAUDE.md 'Building and Checking' section (the rule being patched or replaced)
- agent/.githooks/pre-commit (the hook that runs make check)
- agent/.claude/settings.json (where the sandbox allowlist lives, for FIX 2a)
acceptance_criteria: Either: (2a) agent/.claude/settings.json sandbox allowlist extended so 'git commit' succeeds without dangerouslyDisableSandbox, verified by a clean commit attempt in default sandbox mode; OR (2b) agent/CLAUDE.md 'Building and Checking' section names the transitive case explicitly.
notes:
Investigation findings from AgenC mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f (the originating session):

1. The actual failing operation, verified from the pre-commit-hook test output, is a unix socket BIND, not a Go cache write:
   'bind unix /tmp/claude-501/wt-883563064/a/m/6e54226c/w.sock: bind: operation not permitted'
   This came from internal/wrapper/wrapper_integration_test.go binding sockets in $TMPDIR.

2. ~/.claude/settings.json (global) sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite is:
     ~/.npm/**, ~/.claude/**, ~/app/dotfiles/**, ~/app/exobrain/**,
     /var/folders/*/*/T/**, /private/var/folders/*/*/T/**
   ~/Library/Caches/go-build is NOT in it. (It IS in permissions.allow as Write()/Edit() — but that is the permission-prompt allowlist, a different mechanism from the Bash sandbox.) So adding go-build to project sandbox would do real work, not be redundant.

3. agent/.claude/settings.json (project) sandbox already has allowUnixSockets including //tmp/claude-*/** which LOOKS like it should match the failing path /tmp/claude-501/wt-.../w.sock — but the bind still fails. Two hypotheses worth checking when this bead is picked up:
   (i) Symlink resolution: macOS /tmp is a symlink to /private/tmp; sandbox may evaluate pre- or post-resolution, and only /private/tmp/claude-*/** is in allowWrite (not /tmp/claude-*/**).
   (ii) BIND requires write permission to create the socket file, which is a separate allowWrite check from the allowUnixSockets list (which may only govern connect()).

4. Scope decomposition the future picker should know about — TWO independent sub-fixes inside this bead, NOT one:
   - SUB-FIX A: add ~/Library/Caches/go-build to project sandbox allowWrite. Independently useful (sandboxed go builds get cache benefits). Does NOT close the git-commit-under-default-sandbox acceptance criterion.
   - SUB-FIX B: add the appropriate write permission for the $TMPDIR socket path (likely /tmp/claude-*/** in allowWrite, or revised pattern that matches symlink resolution). THIS is what actually closes the acceptance criterion.

5. The user (Kevin) reviewed this in mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f and chose to defer both — they are NOT acted on yet. Decision was 'come back later'. When picked up, confirm intent: just SUB-FIX A, just SUB-FIX B, or both?

6. The original bead 2b fallback (CLAUDE.md doc-only patch) is still on the table if neither sandbox edit is appetizing.

title: PreToolUse hook: block wrong-order git chained command (add+pull-rebase without commit between)
description:
Structural fix for the git-command-sequencing failure caught in AgenC mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f (Diamond Cascade REFLECT for the repo description feature).

WHY: The project's CLAUDE.md states the order 'add → commit → pull-rebase → push'. An agent (me) chained 'git add && git pull --rebase && git commit && git push' instead, because (a) the universal git prior 'pull before push' outcompeted the project-specific override stored as prose, (b) end-of-task acceleration treated the four-step list as a recipe to execute rather than a constraint puzzle, (c) the prose's 'A → B → C → D' syntax visually invites && chaining. Prose alone is not sufficient — durable fix needs to be enforcement, not guidance.

PROBLEM TO SOLVE: Detect chained-command shapes where 'git pull --rebase' follows 'git add' via && without an intervening 'git commit', and reject them with a message pointing at the agent CLAUDE.md 'Git Push Workflow' section.

CONTEXT TO LINK:
- AgenC mission cbd867bf-196f-4e1a-9dd5-ef8d354a0f5f for the originating /five-whys analysis (run 'agenc session print --all' on the session for the full tree)
- agent/CLAUDE.md 'Git Push Workflow' section (this is the rule being enforced)
- agent/.claude/hooks/ for existing PreToolUse hook patterns to mirror
- Existing hook examples: the block-direct-beads-writes.sh hook (global) is a reference for matcher-based bash blocking

SCOPE: Project-level hook in the agent repo. Not global — the proactive-pull-rebase rule is project-specific (global CLAUDE.md uses add → commit → push, with pull-rebase only as recovery).

OPTIONAL ADDITIVE: Also rephrase the CLAUDE.md sequence from 'add → commit → pull-rebase → push' to an explicit numbered list with 'do these as separate commands; the index-clean precondition for pull --rebase makes chaining impossible' called out inline. Defense in depth.
acceptance_criteria: A PreToolUse Bash hook in agent/.claude/hooks/ that blocks the failure pattern, with an error message pointing at the agent CLAUDE.md Git Push Workflow section. Verified by attempting the wrong-order chain and observing the block.
close_reason: Re-filing in ~/app/dotfiles/.beads at user request — git-order enforcement is a global-Claude-config concern, not AgenC-specific.

title: In-mission agents don't discover AgenC's secrets-file injection mechanism
description:
An agent running inside an AgenC mission has no in-context way to discover that AgenC resolves 1Password op-prefixed references from the per-repo secrets file at .claude/secrets[dot]env and injects them as environment variables at mission spawn. The feature is documented in README.md and docs/1password.md, but those docs are not surfaced inside a running mission — not in the prime template (cmd/genprime/main.go), not in the Adjutant prompt (internal/claudeconfig/adjutant_claude.md), and not in any skill.

Concrete failure case (mission 50c30209-0fbb-4387-99b3-c5265d5627de, ~2026-06-03 20:28-20:31 UTC): an agent designing a meme-generation skill that needed imgflip credentials reasoned through CLI --help output, searched the agenc directory for secret/env/cred patterns, found only global-credentials-expiry, and concluded that no AgenC secrets mechanism existed. It proposed putting credentials in the shell rc file. The user had to manually correct it (paraphrased: 'agenc injects secrets that are in the per-repo secrets file into the environment of the mission, resolving op-prefixed references') before the agent could continue. The full session is reachable via 'agenc mission print 50c30209-0fbb-4387-99b3-c5265d5627de'.

The underlying problem: any architectural feature whose existence affects agent design decisions — secrets injection is one, but others likely exist (cron scheduling, MCP gateway, trusted MCP servers, etc.) — needs an in-mission discovery path, not just user-facing docs. The right shape of fix is open: a skill that activates on credential / env-var-related reasoning, a routing hint in CLAUDE.md, an entry in the Adjutant prompt, an entry in the prime template, or a different mechanism entirely. Whichever path is picked should generalize — this is unlikely to be the only AgenC feature with the same discoverability gap.

title: Per-mission temp directory so ephemeral artifacts survive with the mission
description:
Missions are ephemeral and their local filesystem is discarded when the mission ends. Agents increasingly produce useful throwaway artifacts during a mission — rendered HTML reports/dashboards, scratch files, intermediate outputs — that currently land in the machine-wide temp dir ($TMPDIR) and are lost over time with no association to the mission that created them.

Proposal: give each mission its own temp directory, owned by and lifecycle-tied to the mission, so these artifacts persist alongside the mission record and can be revisited later (e.g. via mission inspect/print) rather than evaporating into a shared /tmp.

Motivating use case: an HTML-output skill being designed in the dotfiles repo renders ephemeral dashboards/reports to $TMPDIR for the user to open in a browser. The user wants those to eventually live in a per-mission temp dir so they aren't silently lost. For now the skill uses the machine $TMPDIR with a note that per-mission temp dirs are the desired end state — this bead tracks the AgenC-side change.

Open questions for whoever picks this up: where the per-mission temp dir lives, how its lifecycle ties to mission archival, whether it is exposed to the agent via an env var, and retention/cleanup policy.

Provenance: AgenC mission f938a211-e167-4259-be2f-737f1ee03334. Related dotfiles bead for the HTML-output skill: dotfiles-dqx.

title: Separate database.Mission persisted columns from server-computed transient fields
description:
The database.Mission struct (internal/database/missions.go) mixes two distinct concerns: columns that come from the database row, and transient display values computed by the server at request time and explicitly commented 'not stored in the database'. As of this writing those transient fields are ResolvedSessionTitle, IsAdjutant, ClaudeState — and IsAttached is being added as a fourth (the tmux attached-state indicator for the mission attach picker).

The smell: a type named database.Mission, living in the database package, should represent a persisted row. Carrying server-computed view state on it conflates 'what is stored' with 'what was computed for this response'. The reason it grew this way is the client API: client.ListMissions() decodes the wire type MissionResponse and converts it back into *database.Mission via ToMission() before handing it to the CLI, so the CLI's whole rendering layer (buildMissionPickerEntries and friends) operates on database.Mission. Transient fields got bolted onto database.Mission so they'd survive that conversion and reach the renderer.

The fix is to give the CLI rendering layer a proper view/response type to operate on (or have the client return MissionResponse directly), so database.Mission can shrink back to pure persisted columns. This touches every CLI caller that consumes client.ListMissions/GetMission/SearchMissions, so it is its own refactor — deliberately deferred out of the attach-dot feature rather than half-done inline.

Provenance: designed in AgenC mission 7d584435-fb76-437c-93b3-3829a72de40f, session 88c57726. Run 'agenc session print 88c57726 --all' for the full discussion of why the wart was fed rather than fixed for the attach-indicator feature.

description:
[What]: AgenC's default tmux configuration is friction-inducing for users who have never used tmux (which is the entire ICP per strategy/icp.md). This includes: (1) the default tmux/Claude UI text colors being unreadable on dark terminals (Mike Zhao flagged a specific blue element as "really hard to read"); (2) tab-switching not working out of the box (Mike had to ask Claude to add Ctrl-H/Ctrl-L bindings); (3) default hotkeys for common operations not being discoverable. Ship a curated tmux-config-for-non-tmux-users that handles these out of the box. Work is in flight in mission e1a87786-7119-4fc9-9c19-1d28be67f444 — coordinate.
[Why]: tmux is the load-bearing universal friction across every AgenC onboarding (Omar, Pedro, Charles, Yannik, Mike). The ICP explicitly is NOT a tmux user. The bar is not "tmux power-users will love this" — it is "someone who has never typed 'tmux' in their life can attach and switch tabs in 60 seconds."

[Related mission]: e1a87786-7119-4fc9-9c19-1d28be67f444 (in-flight work on tmux defaults)
design:
Design converged in mission e1a87786, session b9274394 (run `agenc session print b9274394 --all` for the full discussion).

## File layout (Approach B)

Two files, distinct ownership models:

- **`~/.tmux.conf`** — owned by the user after creation. AgenC writes it ONCE, only if neither `~/.tmux.conf` nor `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` exists. After that, the only thing AgenC ever touches in this file is the `# >>> AgenC keybindings >>>` sentinel block (existing inject logic).
- **`~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf`** — auto-managed. AgenC overwrites it on every `tmux inject` run (same lifecycle as `tmux-keybindings.conf`), so we can ship improved defaults across releases.

The `source-file ~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf` line lives in `~/.tmux.conf` OUTSIDE the AgenC sentinel block, with a comment telling the user they can remove the line to opt out — and that AgenC will not re-add it. This gives users a one-line opt-out from the defaults while leaving the keybindings sentinel block (which is load-bearing for AgenC operation) auto-managed.

## Generated `~/.tmux.conf` (seed-time only)

```
# Created by AgenC because no tmux config was found when you first attached.
# This file is yours — edit freely.

# AgenC starter defaults for users new to tmux. Remove this line to opt out;
# AgenC will not re-add it. The file it points to may be refreshed by AgenC.
source-file ~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf

# >>> AgenC keybindings >>>
source-file ~/.agenc/tmux-keybindings.conf
# <<< AgenC keybindings <<<
```

## Generated `~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf` (refreshed each run)

```
# AgenC starter defaults — auto-generated, may be refreshed on upgrades.
# To disable, remove the source-file line for this file from ~/.tmux.conf.

set -g extended-keys on

# Window navigation
bind -n C-h previous-window
bind -n C-l next-window
bind -n 'C-;' select-pane -t :.+
bind -n C-S-h swap-window -t -1\; select-window -t -1
bind -n C-S-l swap-window -t +1\; select-window -t +1

# Status line
set -g status-position top
set -g status-interval 1
set -g status-style "bg=colour236,fg=white"
set -g status-left ""
set -g status-right ""
set -g window-status-format " #I:#{=/20/…:window_name} "
set -g window-status-current-format " #I:#{=/20/…:window_name} "
set -g window-status-current-style "bg=colour118,fg=colour236,bold"
set -g window-status-style "bg=default,fg=white"
set -g base-index 1
set -g renumber-windows on

# Bells & passthrough
set -g monitor-bell on
set -g bell-action any
set -g visual-bell off
set -g allow-passthrough on
set -as terminal-features ",xterm-ghostty:hyperlinks"
set -g window-status-bell-style "bg=yellow,fg=black,bold"
```

Audience-scope note: these defaults are tuned for non-tmux users (the ICP per strategy/icp.md). Power-user concerns (e.g. `C-l` shadowing shell clear-screen) are accepted tradeoffs.

## Code surfaces

- New helper in `internal/tmux/` (e.g. `bootstrap.go`): `EnsureTmuxConfigBootstrapped(agencDirpath, homeDir) (created bool, writtenPaths []string, err error)`. Helper takes `homeDir` as a parameter (not via `os.UserHomeDir()` internally) so E2E tests can redirect.
- Always (re)writes `~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf` from a canonical embedded string.
- Seeds `~/.tmux.conf` only when neither `~/.tmux.conf` nor `~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf` exists.
- Promote `findTmuxConfFilepath()` from `cmd/tmux_inject.go:104` into `internal/tmux/` so both code paths share it.
- New path helper `config.GetTmuxDefaultsFilepath(agencDirpath)` next to `GetTmuxKeybindingsFilepath`.
- Call the helper from `cmd/tmux_attach.go` (which `cmd/attach.go` aliases) before the actual tmux attach; also from `cmd/tmux_inject.go` so both keep the two files in sync. The existing sentinel-block injection logic runs on top of the seed and no-ops when the block is already present.

## UX

Silent create + print a summary on first seed only:

```
No tmux config found — created starter files:
  ~/.tmux.conf                  (yours; edit freely)
  ~/.agenc/tmux-defaults.conf   (managed by AgenC; remove the source-file
                                 line in ~/.tmux.conf to opt out)
```

Subsequent runs: silent.

## E2E coverage (scripts/e2e-test.sh)

The helper must accept `homeDir` as a parameter so tests can use a temp dir. Required cases:

- Seed-on-empty: empty fake-$HOME → both files present with expected content.
- Skip-when-`~/.tmux.conf`-exists: pre-create → file untouched; defaults file still (re)written; sentinel block appended by existing inject logic.
- Skip-when-`~/.config/tmux/tmux.conf`-exists: same.
- Defaults-file-refresh: pre-existing stale `tmux-defaults.conf` → overwritten.
- Idempotent re-run: two consecutive attaches → no duplicate source-file lines, no duplicate sentinel blocks.

## Open question (resolve before coding)

Should `agenc mission new` also trigger seeding? It is the other plausible "first interactive tmux moment" for a brand-new user. Default recommendation: yes, for symmetry — but ask Kevin first.

## Pre-coding decision

description:
Feature request: extend 'agenc session print' (or equivalent) with an --until flag that lets a session/mission be sliced at a specific point in time or up to a specific event/marker.

Use case: queue-based work handoff. An agent files a bead for a future agent to pick up. The future agent should be able to read EXACTLY the context the filing agent was working with — not the whole session transcript, but the slice of it leading up to the bead-filing moment. This makes inherited context faithful and bounded.

Today: future agents either get no context (just the bead description) or full transcripts (slow, often-irrelevant). An --until flag is the missing middle.

Sketch: 'agenc session print <session-id> --until <timestamp|marker|event>' returns the transcript up to that point only. Bead descriptions can reference the cutoff explicitly so consumers know what to ask for.

title: Clarify agent_instructions.md vs agenc prime vs adjutant_claude.md roles
description:
Today there are three places that inject context into an agent's Claude:

1. **`internal/claudeconfig/agent_instructions.md`** — baked into every regular mission's CLAUDE.md at config-build time.
2. **`internal/claudeconfig/prime_content.md`** (via `agenc prime`) — auto-generated from the cobra command tree; Adjutant gets it via SessionStart hook, regular missions don't get it baked in.
3. **`internal/claudeconfig/adjutant_claude.md`** — Adjutant-specific prompt with user-facing feature documentation.

The split is currently unprincipled: when adding a new piece of guidance (e.g., the recent `mission reload --async` rule for self-reloading agents), it's not obvious which file owns it. The CLAUDE.md notes some guidance for Adjutant content, but the broader model — what each file is FOR, what their relationships are, whether they should overlap, and whether all missions should see all three — has never been explicitly designed.

Investigate and produce a clear architectural decision:
- What is each file's purpose / audience?
- Should regular missions also receive prime content baked in (already raised in `agenc-oup1`)?
- Should Adjutant also receive agent_instructions, or is its content fully separate?
- When new agent-facing guidance is added, what's the routing rule?
- Are there pieces of agent_instructions that belong in prime, or vice versa?

The existing issue `agenc-oup1` covers a narrow slice (the inject asymmetry between Adjutant and regular missions). This is the broader strategic question.

title: Replace blanket -SA1019 staticcheck exclusion with targeted nolint directives
description: The .golangci.yml staticcheck settings exclude '-SA1019' (deprecated API usage) globally, but there are only 2 instances in the entire codebase: (1) cmd/server_version_check.go:52 — config.GetDaemonPIDFilepath(agencDirpath), deprecated because daemon was replaced by server. (2) cmd/server_version_check.go:67 — config.GetDaemonDirpath(agencDirpath), same reason. Both are in server_version_check.go which INTENTIONALLY uses deprecated daemon functions — its entire purpose is to clean up old daemon artifacts during upgrade. The blanket SA1019 suppression means any new deprecated API usage anywhere in the codebase accumulates silently without warning. Steps: (1) Remove '-SA1019' from the staticcheck checks list in .golangci.yml. (2) Run 'make check' to find flagged instances. (3) At the 2 callsites in server_version_check.go, add targeted '//nolint:staticcheck // intentionally using deprecated daemon paths for migration cleanup' comments. (4) If any other SA1019 violations appear elsewhere, evaluate them: either fix the deprecated usage or add a targeted nolint with explanation. (5) Commit. This project uses github.com/mieubrisse/stacktrace — never use bare 'return err', always wrap with stacktrace.Propagate(err, "meaningful message").

title: Move config get/set/edit to server API endpoints
description: Currently config get/set/edit/unset commands read/write ~/.agenc/config/config.yml directly from the CLI process. This couples the CLI to the filesystem layout and requires the CLI to resolve agencDirpath for file access. These should instead be server API endpoints so the CLI only needs the server socket, consistent with how mission commands work. This would let the server be the single owner of ~/.agenc/ file access.

title: Remove deprecated cron_id and cron_name columns from missions table
description: The crons modernization (2026-03-18-crons-modernization-design.md) replaced the cron-specific cron_id and cron_name columns with generic source, source_id, and source_metadata columns. The old columns were left in place to avoid a disruptive SQLite table rebuild. This bead tracks their eventual removal. Requires a table rebuild migration (CREATE new table, INSERT INTO ... SELECT, DROP old table, ALTER TABLE RENAME).

title: Build auto-refinement loop
description: Build an automatic refinement loop into AgenC that continuously improves the system based on usage patterns and friction points.

title: Add mission provenance fields (spawn_context and spawned_by)
description:
Add two new fields to missions for better provenance tracking:

- spawn_context: UUID of the mission (if any) that the mission creator was looking at when they spawned this mission. This is a weak reference that provides context on what the user was doing before embarking on the new mission.
- spawned_by: UUID of the mission that actually spawned this sub-mission (if any). This is a hard reference, filled in only when a mission programmatically spawns a sub-mission.

The goal is to provide better mission provenance and help users figure out what they were doing before they embarked on their current mission.

title: Attach outcomes to missions
description: Allow attaching explicit outcomes to a mission, so that each mission has a clear record of what it produced. This supports the 'one session = one outcome' model and makes it easier to review what was accomplished.

title: Prompt evaluation test suites
description:
[What]: Build a framework for testing prompts/skills with input/output pairs — verify that refactored prompts still produce correct results before deploying changes.

This is LLMOps-style evaluation applied to skills. He noted "those are also expensive to run too" — so the implementation needs to consider cost (selective test runs, caching, etc.). This would give users confidence to iterate on skills without fear of regression.

title: CASS (Coding Agent Session Search) integration into AgenC
description:
## Summary

Integrate CASS (Coding Agent Session Search) into AgenC to give agents institutional memory — the ability to search past mission conversations, leverage cross-tool knowledge, and accumulate procedural memory over time.

CASS is a Rust tool by Jeffrey Emanuel (github.com/Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search) that indexes conversation history from 15+ AI coding agents into a single searchable knowledge base using Tantivy full-text search with BM25 scoring, edge n-gram tokenization, and optional semantic search via MiniLM.

## Motivation

Today, each AgenC mission starts from scratch — agents have no memory of past missions, no access to solutions discovered by other agents, and no accumulated knowledge base. CASS solves this by indexing all Claude Code session data (and other coding tools) into a searchable corpus that agents can query.

## Design

### Architecture Overview

CASS runs on the **host machine** (not inside ephemeral missions). AgenC agents access it via:

1. **MCP server** — CASS exposes MCP tools that agents can call directly
2. **CLI robot mode** — `cass search <query> --robot --limit N` for structured, token-budget-aware output

### Integration Layers

#### Layer 1: Session Search Across Missions

- Index Claude Code session data from `~/.claude/projects/` so agents can search past mission conversations
- CASS already supports Claude Code as a data source — AgenC needs to ensure the index stays fresh
- Agents query before starting work: "Has any past mission solved a similar problem?"

**Implementation:**
- Add CASS MCP server to the default agent MCP configuration in AgenC
- Create an AgenC skill (e.g., `/cass-search`) that wraps robot mode queries with sensible defaults
- Run `cass index` periodically (cron or on mission start) to keep the index current

#### Layer 2: Robot Mode as Agent Tool

- Agents invoke `cass search <query> --robot --limit N --min-score 0.5` to find relevant prior work
- Robot mode output is designed for agent consumption: structured, token-budget-aware
- Key flags: `--robot`, `--json`, `--limit`, `--min-score`, `--no-history`

**Implementation:**
- Register CASS binary path in AgenC config (`config.yml` key: `cass_binary_path`)
- Add MCP tool definition that wraps CASS CLI invocation
- Include in default agent permissions (sandbox allowlist for CASS binary + index directory)

#### Layer 3: CASS Memory System (Procedural Memory)

- The CASS Memory System (TypeScript/Bun) builds procedural memory on top of search
- Produces a `playbook.yaml` with confidence-tracked rules that mature through stages: hypothesis → emerging → established → core
- Rules represent accumulated knowledge: "When doing X in this codebase, always Y"

**Implementation:**
- Mount `playbook.yaml` as a read-only resource for agents (via CLAUDE.md injection or MCP resource)
- Run memory system extraction periodically to update the playbook
- AgenC config key for playbook path: `cass_playbook_path`
- Consider: should each repo have its own playbook, or one global playbook?

#### Layer 4: Cross-Repo Knowledge Transfer

- CASS indexes across all coding tools (Cursor, Codex, Aider, Gemini, etc.)
- Agents benefit from work done in other tools without any AgenC-specific setup
- This is "free" once CASS is indexing — the search corpus includes all tools

### Key Considerations

- **Dependency management:** CASS and the memory system (Bun) are external dependencies. AgenC should detect their presence and degrade gracefully if absent.
- **Index freshness:** Stale indexes reduce value. Options: index on mission start, periodic cron, or inotify-based incremental indexing.
- **Token budget:** Robot mode flags (`--limit`, `--min-score`) prevent overwhelming agent context windows. Default limits should be conservative.
- **Privacy/security:** CASS indexes raw conversation data. Users should be able to exclude specific directories or repos from indexing.
- **Performance:** Search should complete in <1s to avoid blocking agent startup.

### Phased Rollout

**Phase 1 (MVP):** Add CASS MCP server to default agent config. Agents can search past sessions manually.

**Phase 2:** Create `/cass-search` skill with sensible defaults. Auto-index on mission start if index is stale.

**Phase 3:** Integrate CASS Memory System playbook. Mount as agent knowledge. Periodic extraction.

**Phase 4:** Cross-tool knowledge graph. Relationship mapping between missions, repos, and discoveries.

## Success Criteria

- Agents can search past mission conversations and find relevant prior work
- Search results are token-budget-aware and don't overwhelm context windows
- CASS absence doesn't break AgenC (graceful degradation)
- Index stays reasonably fresh without manual intervention

## References

- CASS repo: github.com/Dicklesworthstone/coding_agent_session_search
- CASS Memory System: TypeScript/Bun layer that builds playbook.yaml
- Claude Code session data: ~/.claude/projects/

title: Allow claude remote-control for AgenC missions
description:
Enable Claude Code's remote-control feature (claude remote-control / /remote-control) so that AgenC mission agents can be monitored and controlled from mobile devices or browsers via claude.ai/code or the Claude mobile app.

Key details about the feature:
- Released in Claude Code v2.1.51 (Feb 24 2026), currently a research preview
- Start with 'claude remote-control' (new session) or '/remote-control' ('/rc') inside existing session
- Flags: --verbose, --sandbox / --no-sandbox
- Outbound HTTPS only (no inbound ports). Session registers with Anthropic API and polls for work. Traffic over TLS with short-lived credentials.
- Requires Max plan (Pro coming soon). API keys not supported. Must be signed in via /login.
- One remote session at a time per instance. Terminal must stay open. ~10 min network timeout.
- Can auto-enable for all sessions via /config -> Enable Remote Control for all sessions
- Many open bugs on GitHub (40+ issues)

What needs to happen for AgenC:
- Determine how to expose the remote-control capability to mission agents (CLI flag, config option, or auto-enable)
- Consider security implications of enabling remote access to agent sessions
- Handle the Max plan requirement gracefully (detect plan, warn if unsupported)
- Decide whether remote-control should be opt-in per mission or a global AgenC config setting
- Test interaction with AgenC tmux-based session management

Docs: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control
CLI ref: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/cli-reference
Assessment: https://simonwillison.net/2026/Feb/25/claude-code-remote-control/

title: Fix non-rune-safe truncation in truncateWindowTitle
description: truncateWindowTitle in internal/wrapper/tmux.go uses collapsed[:maxLen-1] which slices by bytes not rune positions, corrupting multi-byte UTF-8 characters. The ellipsis appended is 3 bytes (U+2026) not 1, so result can exceed maxLen bytes. Fix: convert to []rune before slicing: string([]rune(collapsed)[:maxLen-1]) + '…'
close_reason: Implemented in commit b7770bd

title: Build 'mission manager' interactive TUI subcommand (Charm/Bubbletea)
description:
Add an interactive TUI subcommand (e.g. agenc mission manage or agenc mission tui) that presents a Bubbletea-powered interface for managing missions.

Core functionality:
- List all missions with status indicators (running, stopped, archived)
- Select missions via keyboard navigation
- Stop running missions
- If running from within AGENC_TMUX, also allow resuming missions (attach to tmux session)
- Show mission metadata (name, created date, agent template, etc.)

Technical approach:
- Use Charm Bubbletea (github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea) for the TUI framework
- Use Charm Lipgloss for styling
- Detect AGENC_TMUX environment variable to conditionally enable resume functionality
- Integrate with existing mission DB and tmux session management code

UX considerations:
- Keyboard shortcuts for common actions (s=stop, r=resume, q=quit, enter=details)
- Confirmation prompts for destructive actions (stop)
- Real-time status updates if feasible
- Filter/search capability for users with many missions

When an agent initiates a conversation with another, it gets back the mission UUID which serves as the chat handle for ongoing communication.

title: tmux-resurrect-restored panes are unusable husks, not live missions
description:
After a machine reboot, a user who restores their tmux session with tmux-resurrect gets panes that LOOK like AgenC mission panes but aren't operable — mission-scoped actions (detach, side-shell, send-keys) find no mission for the pane.

WHY this happens (diagnosed): an AgenC mission is a live wrapper process, not restorable terminal state. A reboot kills every wrapper. tmux-resurrect restores the visual panes (with fresh pane IDs) but NOT the wrapper processes. On server startup, pane reconciliation (internal/server/pane_reconcile.go) matches missions to pool panes by LIVE wrapper PID — so it correctly matches zero, leaving each active mission's tmux_pane NULL. The result is 'husk' panes: DB records for missions whose processes are dead, with no live pane binding. resolve-mission returns empty for them, so every mission-scoped keybinding no-ops.

The raw 'returned 1' error this produced was already fixed (commit 8b9b182 makes mission-scoped keybindings show a friendly 'No AgenC mission in this pane' message instead of erroring). This bead is the REMAINING, deeper problem: the husk panes themselves. The interest is a coherent experience for a user who resurrects a session — not a specific mechanism. Deciding the mechanism (detect + rebuild vs. clearly flag vs. document the incompatibility) is part of the work, not prescribed here.

Constraints:
- The pane->mission anchor is the live wrapper PID; it fundamentally cannot survive a reboot, so no solution can 'reconnect' a dead wrapper. 'agenc mission rebuild' already re-creates a pool window + fresh wrapper and is the natural building block for a rebuild path.
- Must not regress the error-surfacing fix (8b9b182) or normal live-pane reconciliation.
- Respect thin-CLI/thick-server: resolution/rebuild logic belongs server-side.

Provenance: originating user report from Steve Wade; diagnosis in AgenC mission 4e7e9c44-ab95-4c8d-b5d2-abd50dee2ee4. Key files: internal/server/pane_reconcile.go (reconcile-by-PID), internal/server/server.go (reconcilePaneIDs on startup), internal/tmux/keybindings.go, internal/database/missions.go (GetMissionByTmuxPane/SetTmuxPane).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Have one or more active AgenC missions running in tmux panes.
2. Reboot the machine (all wrapper processes die; the tmux server exits).
3. Restore the tmux session with tmux-resurrect — panes come back with fresh pane IDs but no AgenC wrapper running in them.
4. On next agenc server startup, observe 'Pane reconciliation: matched 0 missions to pool panes' in server.log.
5. Focus a resurrected pane and invoke a mission-scoped action (detach / side-shell / send-keys): it finds no mission and no-ops with the 'No AgenC mission in this pane' message.
acceptance_criteria: A user whose tmux session was restored by tmux-resurrect after a reboot no longer faces silent husk panes: AgenC either (a) clearly identifies resurrected panes as not-live-missions, (b) offers to rebuild them into real missions via the existing rebuild path, or (c) explicitly documents that tmux-resurrect does not restore missions so the behavior is expected. Whichever is chosen, the husk panes are not silently indistinguishable from live mission panes.

title: AgenC proactive sensitive-info filtering on assistant output via MessageDisplay hook
description:
Today AgenC's secret-protection layer is INPUT-side: hooks like block-env-file-access.sh prevent Claude from reading dotenv files in the first place. Nothing prevents Claude OUTPUTTING secrets it saw before the block was added, or paraphrasing secrets back from another source — tool output echoes from Gmail reads, accidental dumps during config editing, debugging sessions inspecting credential files. Skills like /exobrain-update carry their own in-skill redaction gates, but in-skill checks fail open when the model paraphrases around them.

Claude Code v2.1.152's new MessageDisplay hook event fires on every assistant message regardless of which skill is active. This is the first event surface that can catch leaks on the OUTPUT path.

Opportunity: AgenC ships a centralized redaction hook in its claude-config that scans assistant output for high-confidence credential patterns (Anthropic sk- prefixes, Stripe sk_live, GitHub gh tokens, RSA/SSH headers, AWS access key IDs, dotenv-style KEY=value assignment lines, raw JWTs) and replaces matches with [REDACTED:<type>] inline. Pattern list lives in a sidecar file (analogous to workspace-mcp-action-denylist.txt) for easy extension.

Defense-in-depth: covers leak-in-output paths that input-side blocks can't reach, AND applies to every AgenC mission automatically without per-skill effort.

Provenance: AgenC mission ed19373a-ea9a-4ccb-a2ce-fce9bbaf906b — surfaced during claude-code-upgrade-review of v2.1.145→v2.1.153. See https://docs.claude.com/en/release-notes/claude-code

title: AgenC: easier parent-agent access for cross-repo edits + better parent↔sub-agent briefing handshake
description:
Surfaced during the REFLECT phase of a /diamond-cascade session redesigning /weekly-plan → /build-weekly-plan (AgenC mission 06d4403f-2ada-4289-a321-09f8b2a1c99e, 2026-06-07). /five-whys analysis traced one of the session's load-bearing failures (Failure B — 'side mission deviated from spec') to a pattern: parents spawn side missions for tasks they could have done directly if they had access.

THE PATTERN:

In the originating session, the parent mission spawned a side mission to edit a template file in the checklists-and-templates repo, which the parent had read-only access to via the repo library. The side mission was given a high-level brief and went off-spec (restructured the file against explicit 'DO NOT touch' instruction).

KEVIN'S FRAMING:

The fix is less about training parent agents to write better surgical-edit briefs for sub-agents, and more about giving parent agents EASIER ACCESS to do edits themselves — so spawning a sub-agent is needed less often for small file changes. When sub-agents ARE needed, a possible secondary improvement: have the sub-agent restate its understanding of the work back to the parent before acting (a brief handshake), so spec drift is caught at the briefing stage rather than after the damage is done.

CONCRETE CAPABILITY IDEAS:

1. **Easier parent-agent cross-repo edit access** — some mechanism (additional sandbox path, ephemeral write credentials, a 'surgical-edit broker' subroutine) that lets a parent mission make a small, well-scoped edit to another repo without spawning a full sub-mission. Avoids the spawn overhead AND the brief-quality risk for small changes.
2. **Brief handshake before sub-agent action** — sub-agent reads brief, restates 'here's what I'm about to do', parent confirms, sub-agent acts. Catches spec drift at briefing time rather than after the artifact lands.

Note: this is the lower-priority follow-on to the parent-child relationship work in the P2 bead. The P2 bead covers ownership/verification/wait; this P4 bead covers reducing the NEED for sub-mission spawn in the first place AND tightening the briefing handshake when spawn is unavoidable.

Provenance: derived from /five-whys analysis (Failure B) in the originating session. Full session transcript: agenc mission print 06d4403f-2ada-4289-a321-09f8b2a1c99e.

title: Expose an AgenC endpoint/server for browser HTML to POST data back into the mission
description:
Enable a true interactive feedback loop between browser-rendered HTML artifacts and the mission's Claude — the 'super HTML websites' idea.

Problem: an agent can render an HTML page and the user can open it, but a page opened from the file:// origin cannot silently write to disk (browser security blocks it; the File System Access API requires a secure context — https/localhost — not file://). So today the only no-infra round-trip is a 'copy this prompt' button the user pastes back to Claude. The dream is: the user adjusts controls in the rendered dashboard and those changes flow back to Claude automatically, with no copy-paste.

Possible shape (for whoever picks this up to evaluate, not prescribe): AgenC exposes a local endpoint or small server the rendered HTML can POST to, which writes the payload into the mission's temp directory; Claude then reads it. Could be an HTTP endpoint AgenC manages, or an MCP server, or a static localhost server that unlocks the File System Access API. The win is that any HTML artifact a mission produces becomes a two-way interactive surface rather than a one-way view.

Depends on / relates to: agenc-p0p0 (per-mission temp directory — the natural place for POSTed payloads to land). Motivating consumer: the HTML-output skill being designed in dotfiles (dotfiles-dqx), whose Tier 1 ships with the copy-prompt approximation; this bead is the infra that would unlock the silent Tier 2 loop.

Provenance: AgenC mission f938a211-e167-4259-be2f-737f1ee03334.
notes: Correction: the description's reference to 'dotfiles-dqx' as the HTML-output skill is wrong. dotfiles-dqx tracks a separate question (superpowers vs Double Diamond framework overlap). The motivating HTML-output skill is being authored directly in the dotfiles repo within this same AgenC mission (see provenance UUID), not tracked by dotfiles-dqx.

title: Investigate --bare flag for auto-summarizer to cut latency
description:
The auto-summarizer (`internal/server/session_summarizer.go`) calls `claude --print` to generate session window titles via Haiku. Current invocation takes ~13.7s, dominated by Claude CLI startup overhead (hooks, LSP, plugin sync, auto-memory, keychain reads, CLAUDE.md auto-discovery).

The `--bare` flag (introduced in claude 2.1.x) skips all of that startup overhead and looks like a strong latency win for this use case — a stateless Haiku call that needs none of the interactive context.

**Blocker:** `--bare` deliberately ignores OAuth tokens. Per `claude --help`: 'Anthropic auth is strictly ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or apiKeyHelper via --settings (OAuth and keychain are never read).' The summarizer currently authenticates via `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (session_summarizer.go:77), which `--bare` rejects with 'Not logged in · Please run /login'.

**Measured (mission a92ad7bd... session, 2026-05-28):**
- Current invocation, OAuth token: ✅ 13.7s
- `--bare` + OAuth token: ❌ 0.7s (auth fail)
- `--bare` no auth: ❌ 0.7s (auth fail)

The 0.7s exit on auth failure is the upper bound of what we'd save — i.e., almost the entire current 13.7s is startup overhead `--bare` would eliminate.

**Paths to explore:**
1. `apiKeyHelper` via `--settings` returning the OAuth token — probably won't work (OAuth tokens `sk-ant-oat...` vs API keys `sk-ant-api...` are different credential types), but cheap to test.

title: Check if Claude Code adds a UserInterrupt hook (better state tracking)
description:
Claude Code's `Stop` hook does not fire when the user interrupts a turn (Esc / Ctrl-C). This means AgenC cannot reliably detect when a Claude session was interrupted vs. completed cleanly — relevant for mission state tracking, status dashboards, and any monitoring that depends on knowing whether the last turn ended cleanly.

Tracking issue: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/9516

Current workaround pattern (from issue comments): use a marker file written on UserPromptSubmit and deleted on Stop; if the marker survives to the next UserPromptSubmit, the previous turn was interrupted. Retroactive only — no real-time interrupt detection possible.

Periodically check whether Claude Code has shipped a native UserInterrupt / Stop:interrupted hook. When it does, AgenC's mission state tracking can be improved to distinguish interrupted vs. completed turns natively.

title: Build custom permissions system via PreToolUse hook
description:
Build a PreToolUse hook that reimplements Claude Code's permissioning system, fixing its broken pattern matching. Claude Code's permission pattern matching is broken for multiline commands, heredocs, backticks, env var prefixes, and compound commands (&&, pipes, redirects). The * wildcard only matches within a single line, so patterns like Bash(gh issue create *) never match commands containing heredocs. Clicking 'Always allow' on these commands saves the entire verbatim heredoc into settings.json, corrupting it.

Core bugs (open, no Anthropic response):
- Multiline/heredoc matching: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/11932
- Duplicate with deny-rule bypass: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/25441
- Compound commands/redirects: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/29421
- Env var prefixes break matching: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/8581
- Backticks in slash commands: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/8197

Settings corruption from 'Always allow':
- github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/15742
- github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16462
- github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/25341

Feature requests:
- Parse compound commands: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16561
- Regex/glob support: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/13154
- Reduce heredoc usage: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/11006
- Permission prompt suggests non-matching patterns: github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/29967

Best workaround: PermissionRequest hook that receives full command JSON and implements custom matching. Reference implementations: gist.github.com/silenvx/5334afee5cd77e2dfcc1be4e943ad43b (Python) and blog.korny.info/2025/10/10/better-claude-code-permissions (Rust).
notes:
Idea (2026-06-06): Nono (https://github.com/always-further/nono) as a possible foundation for AgenC's capability/permissions engine. Nono is a sandboxing tool with declarative policies — a candidate building block if AgenC's PreToolUse hook ever evolves toward a real capability model rather than reactive command-pattern matching. Could even be used directly inside AgenC.

Surfaced from HN 'Ask HN: What is your (AI) dev tech stack/workflow?' (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48413629), jpeeler's comment: pairs herde (multi-agent supervision; see agenc-a1di) with Nono for sandboxing as an alternative to microVM isolation. He calls out the tradeoff explicitly — Nono's per-project policy maintenance vs. microVM's stronger boundary at the cost of losing installed tooling. Same tradeoff AgenC will hit when productionizing permissions.

Charles built a web-based prompt management tool with visual diffs, database-backed versioning, and a feedback loop where you describe what you wish had happened differently, see the proposed prompt diff with reasoning, and approve/reject. This is more accessible than CLI-based refinement for GUI-oriented users transitioning from tools like Cursor. His quote: "For all these AI tools, it's very black-boxed. And I want to know, like if I don't like what it outputted, how is it going to fix it? And what's the diff in its logic or instructions that would make it better the next time."
